title: Digital Programme Manager
sectors: Administration, Management, Finance/Accounting, Procurement; Infrastructure, Technology, Engineering, Science
description: Reference: EO245. Contract: Permanent, full time, 35 hours per week. Location: Kings Hill based with hybrid working (minimum 2 days per week in the office). Salary: Up to £67,500 per annum (depending on experience). CAF Bank, part of Charities Aid Foundation (CAF), is looking for an experienced delivery professional to bring structure, pace and clarity to a complex portfolio of digital change within a purpose-led, regulated bank. What you'll do: Own the overall Digital delivery plan, helping progress the highest-value customer, operational and strategic priorities. Coordinate digital change across Online Banking, AI and automation, digital adoption and other priority initiatives, bringing together teams, suppliers and stakeholders so work is well prioritised, realistically planned and delivered with appropriate governance, control and transparency. Specifically: own and maintain a clear, integrated delivery plan across the Digital portfolio; translate strategic priorities and roadmap items into executable delivery plans; maintain visibility of priorities, milestones, dependencies, risks, issues and decisions; establish delivery routines including planning sessions, progress reviews, blocker reviews and retrospectives; coordinate delivery across Digital, Technology, Operations, Risk, Compliance and external suppliers; identify and remove blockers, escalating promptly; own core delivery controls including RAID logs, action logs, milestone trackers, delivery dashboards and dependency tracking; provide clear reporting for governance and senior stakeholders; coordinate supplier plans, estimates and delivery commitments; support release readiness by tracking UAT progress, known issues and operational readiness; improve flow of work from discovery through delivery, testing, release and benefits realisation; and identify opportunities to use AI to increase pace and effectiveness of delivery. Who we are looking for: An experienced digital, technology or change delivery professional comfortable coordinating multiple workstreams and bringing structure to complex or ambiguous environments. Requirements include experience managing delivery plans, milestones, actions, risks and dependencies across multiple workstreams; coordinating digital/technology/change delivery across cross-functional teams; strong delivery planning, prioritisation and workload management; maintaining RAID logs, action logs, milestone trackers and dashboards; identifying blockers, managing dependencies and escalating effectively; working with external suppliers or third-party delivery partners; supporting release readiness, UAT coordination or delivery assurance; understanding of agile, product-led or hybrid delivery environments; strong written and verbal communication; excellent stakeholder management and facilitation skills; ability to work through ambiguity. Experience in banking, financial services or another regulated environment, and in online banking, automation, AI, digital channels or customer journey improvement, is an advantage. Benefits include permanent hybrid working where roles allow, six weeks holiday plus bank holidays, a wide range of development opportunities, a pension scheme with better-than-market employer contribution options and social impact benefit schemes. Closing date: 8 September 2026 HOW TO APPLY: The closing date for applications is Tuesday 8 September 2026. Complete the application form on the vacancy page, attach your CV and cover letter and click 'Submit Application', or send your CV and cover letter to recruitment@cafonline.org quoting reference number EO245. Applicants must be able to provide proof of Right to Work in the UK. As a Disability Confident Employer, CAF guarantees to interview disabled applicants who meet the minimum criteria — indicate this on the application form. For assistance or reasonable adjustments, contact the Recruitment team at recruitment@cafonline.org or 03000 123 566. https://www.cafcareers.co.uk/digital-programme-manager-eo245

title: E-Government Procurement Senior Expert
description: E-Government Procurement (e-GP) Senior Expert The Government of Mozambique, through the Ministry of Finance, is preparing a new governance operation and implementing a Project Preparation Advance (PPA) to strengthen public financial management and public procurement. The Ministry, through the National Directorate of State Assets (DNPE), seeks an individual consultant to serve as e-Government Procurement (e-GP) Senior Expert under a time-based contract for an initial period of two years, renewable subject to need and satisfactory performance. Responsibilities include identifying and managing overall project risks; determining project resource requirements and preparing/managing the corresponding budget and work plan; managing all contracts related to the project and monitoring performance against agreed obligations and service levels; ensuring quality-assurance standards for project management and the e-GP solution; building and disseminating knowledge and capability within the Government of Mozambique to support the effective operation of the e-GP system; and providing advisory support for a smooth transition from implementation to operation, maintenance and long-term sustainability of the e-GP system. Minimum qualifications: a Master's degree in Business Administration, Management, Procurement, IT, Information Systems, Software Engineering or a related discipline; at least ten years of relevant professional experience, including a minimum of five years managing information-systems or ICT projects in a public- or private-sector organization; demonstrated experience managing large, complex projects, preferably including e-procurement, e-government or comparable digital-transformation initiatives; experience in a procurement or procurement-coordination function and knowledge of public procurement, public-sector operations and change management; experience working with projects financed by cooperation partners such as the World Bank, EU, or AfDB; proficiency in Microsoft Office and project-management tools; strong leadership, coordination, stakeholder-management, analytical and communication skills; and proficiency in Portuguese with a working knowledge of English (or vice versa). HOW TO APPLY: Interested individual consultants should submit an Expression of Interest, in the form of a submission letter accompanied by a curriculum vitae demonstrating required qualifications and relevant experience, no later than September 11, 2026, at 3:30 p.m. (local time), delivered in person, by mail, or by email to the address/email below.

title: Program Manager
description: Program Manager, APEC Networks The Asia Pacific Foundation of Canada (APF Canada) is an independent not-for-profit organization focused on Canada's relations with Asia. Its vision is a prosperous, secure Canada shaping its future through high-impact engagement with Asia; its mission is to enable Canadians to understand, connect with, and succeed in Asia. APF Canada strengthens ties between Canada and Asia through research, education and convening activities. APF Canada is seeking a seasoned Permanent Full-Time Program Manager, APEC Networks. The selected candidate will manage relationships with key stakeholders from the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) and Distinguished Fellows networks. Reports to the Vice-President, Research. Major Responsibilities: - Manage APF Canada's support of Canadian members for the APEC Business Advisory Council (ABAC). - Build and foster relationships with government officials, senior executives and staff in global networks. - Supervise the APEC Networks Officer and any relevant contractors. - Liaise with Global Affairs Canada as required. - Lead the work of Canada's APEC Study Centres. - Co-ordinate APF Canada's APEC stakeholder engagement, especially with the private sector. - Monitor current affairs relevant to ABAC, PECC and the Asia Pacific region. - Produce reports, briefings, and policy recommendations for ABAC CEOs and policymakers. - Manage and facilitate international meetings, consultations and events with business leaders and senior officials. - Extensive domestic and international travel throughout the year. Desired Skills and Abilities: - Master's degree or equivalent in economics, public administration, business administration, political science, or international political economy. - At least five years of previous work experience in government, think-tanks, non-profit organizations, or Track 2 organizations. - Previous experience managing stakeholder networks. - Experience working with or in a multilateral organization. - Experience supporting CEOs and senior officials, including briefings. - Strong interpersonal and diplomacy skills. Eligibility: Applicants must be legally entitled to work in Canada. Based in Vancouver, hybrid work arrangement, frequent domestic and international travel required. Compensation: annual base salary range $75,000 to $85,000, plus comprehensive extended health benefits. Apply: https://asiapacific.bamboohr.com/careers/126 deadline is September 24, 2026

title: Co-Head of Investigations
description: Lead bold investigations that expose abuse, shift narratives and drive meaningful change. About the role: As Co-Head of Investigations, you will play a pivotal role in shaping and leading Global Witness's investigations function, ensuring our work is ambitious, impactful and directly connected to our organisational priorities. Working alongside the other Co-Head of Investigations, you will set strategic priorities, oversee a diverse pipeline of investigations and ensure our investigative expertise is deployed where it can have the greatest impact. You will provide strong editorial leadership and judgement, balancing creativity and bold thinking with rigorous standards of accuracy, ethics, legal compliance and risk management. You will work collaboratively across Global Witness, partnering closely with Campaigns, Policy, Strategic Communications, Partnerships, Data Investigations and Fundraising to turn evidence and investigations into meaningful action and change. You will also lead and develop a talented team of investigators, creating a culture that values curiosity, collaboration, creativity and inclusion. As a senior leader and external ambassador for Global Witness, you will help strengthen the profile and influence of our investigations and ensure our work continues to challenge powerful actors and expose the systems driving environmental destruction, inequality and human rights abuses. About you: You are an experienced investigations, journalism or campaign communications leader with a strong track record of delivering high-impact work in complex and fast-moving environments. You bring excellent editorial judgement and the confidence to identify compelling opportunities, ask difficult questions and make decisions about where investigative work can have the greatest strategic impact. You understand how to balance ambitious storytelling with accuracy, ethical standards and robust approaches to legal, security and reputational risk. You are an inspiring and collaborative people leader who knows how to build high-performing teams where people feel supported, respected and empowered to do their best work. Salary: £65,320. Contract type: permanent, full time. Hybrid working, shorter working week (30 hours Monday-Thursday, Friday off, no impact on full-time salary), at least 2 days in office. Offices in London, Washington DC and Brussels. How to apply: Send your CV (max 2 pages) and responses to the shortlisting questions to RecruitmentCampaigns@globalwitness.org by Midnight GMT Sunday 13 September. Use 'Co-Head of Investigations' in the subject line and 'First Name_Last Name_CV' as the CV file name. Preliminary interviews (virtual) week commencing 28 September. Closing date: 13 September 2026

title: Executive Assistant to the CEO
description: The Union for International Cancer Control (UICC) is the largest global membership organisation dedicated to taking action against cancer. Founded in 1933 and based in Geneva, UICC has over 1,100 member organisations in 172 countries and territories. UICC's mission is to both unite and support the cancer community in its efforts to reduce the global cancer burden, promote greater equity and ensure that cancer control remains a priority on the global health and development agenda. UICC has consultative status with ECOSOC and official relations with WHO, IARC, IAEA and UNODC. Job title: Executive Assistant to the CEO Reports to: Deputy CEO, Chief Business Operations Type of contract: Permanent position at 100% Location: Geneva, Switzerland Availability: As soon as possible Summary of the position The Executive Assistant will provide high-level administrative support to the CEO and the leadership team to successfully conduct the day-to-day management and delivery of all activities, and will work with other UICC teams, Board members and external stakeholders to support achievement of organisational objectives. Main responsibilities - Supporting the CEO in the execution of his duties. - Managing the CEO and Deputy CEO's agenda, ensuring meetings are arranged effectively. - Ensuring the CEO has necessary background information for meetings. - Researching topics on behalf of the CEO. - Managing travel logistics for the CEO and Leadership team. - Supporting the Leadership team in planning, coordination and follow-up of joint activities. - Organising follow-up actions from CEO and Board meetings, conference calls and business trips. - Drafting replies to e-mails and other communications on behalf of the CEO. - Taking responsibility for specific projects supporting the CEO and Deputy CEO. Governance - Providing administrative support to UICC's Board of Directors, including logistical organisation of Board meetings virtually and internationally. - Coordinating Board meeting and General Assembly preparations. - Acting as first point of contact for Board/staff communications. - Management of UICC's Board SharePoint platform. Education and experience - Advanced studies and at least two years professional experience, ideally in an international organisation or NGO. - Experience and proficiency in administrative procedures, managing files and records. Competences - Excellent communication skills - interpersonal, written and verbal. - High level of written and spoken English and French; Spanish a plus. - High proficiency in Outlook, Word, PowerPoint and Excel. - Experience with SharePoint site management an asset. - Strong attention to detail, organisational and time management skills. - Able to deliver quality results under time constraints. - Interest and understanding of the non-profit sector. - Candidate should be eligible to work in Switzerland. What we offer - Opportunity to work at the heart of the global cancer control community in Geneva. - Role within a mission-driven, multi-award-winning organisation. - International and diverse team environment close to the United Nations. - International travel to UICC annual events (World Cancer Congress, World Cancer Leaders' Summit). Applications: Send CV and motivation letter to careers@uicc.org. Deadline for external applications: 4 September 2026. Applications evaluated on a rolling basis; only short-listed candidates contacted.

title: Sekretär*in in Teilzeit

description: Sekretär*in (m/W/D) in Teilzeit Das PRIF – Leibniz-Institut für Friedens- und Konfliktforschung analysiert die Ursachen internationaler und innerstaatlicher Konflikte. Als eines der führenden Friedensforschungsinstitute in Europa verbinden wir interdisziplinäre Grundlagenforschung mit dem Transfer von Wissen in Politik, Medien und Gesellschaft. Seit 2009 ist PRIF Mitglied der Leibniz Gemeinschaft. Das PRIF hat seinen Sitz in Frankfurt am Main und unterhält ein Büro in Berlin. Über 100 Mitarbeiter*innen aus Wissenschaft, Verwaltung und Kommunikation tragen zum Erfolg des Instituts bei. Zur Verstärkung unseres Teams im Programmbereich II „Internationale Institutionen“ suchen wir zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt eine*n Sekretär*in (m/w/d) in Teilzeit (80 %), in Entgeltgruppe 8 TV-H, für die Dauer von vorerst 2 Jahren (gem. § 14 Abs. 2 TzBfG), eine Verlängerung ist angestrebt. Zum Aufgabenspektrum zählen: Antragskontrolle, Reisebuchung und Nachbereitung von Dienstreisen; Unterstützung beim Reporting und Pflege des Berichtswesens; administrative Unterstützung der Leitung des Programmbereichs und der Mitarbeitenden; Korrekturlesen und Formatieren von Publikationen des Programmbereichs; Organisation, Vor- und Nachbereitung und Gästebetreuung bei Terminen und Veranstaltungen; Bereitschaft zur Beteiligung an den Gremien der PRIF-Selbstverwaltung (Arbeitssprache in den zentralen Gremien ist Englisch). Ihr Profil: Eine erfolgreich abgeschlossene Ausbildung im kaufmännischen Bereich ist von Vorteil; Erfahrung im Sekretariats- bzw. Assistenzbereich ist von Vorteil; Erfahrung in der Arbeit im forschungsnahen Umfeld (z.B. an Universitäten oder anderen Forschungsinstituten) ist von Vorteil; Interesse an der Friedens- und Konfliktforschung des PRIF; motivierte und effiziente Einarbeitung in neue Themenbereiche; sehr gute Organisationsfähigkeit und Koordination von Meetings und Veranstaltungen; genaue, sorgfältige und gewissenhafte Arbeitsweise; offenes und einfühlsames Auftreten und Freude an der Arbeit mit Menschen in einem internationalen Team; sicherer Umgang mit gängigen Büroprogrammen wie MS365; gute mündliche und schriftliche Kenntnisse der deutschen und englischen Sprache. Es erwarten Sie: familienfreundliche Arbeitszeiten mit der Möglichkeit zum mobilen Arbeiten im Rahmen einer Dienstvereinbarung; Kolleginnen und Kollegen in einem motivierten und international vernetzten Team; die Möglichkeit ein vergünstigtes Deutschlandticket zu bekommen; Vorteile der betrieblichen Altersvorsorge durch die VBL. Schwerbehinderte Bewerber*innen werden bei gleicher Eignung bevorzugt berücksichtigt. Die maximale Größe für Dateianhänge beträgt 10 MB. Bewerbungskosten können leider nicht übernommen werden. https://www.prif.org/en/career/vacancy/sekretaerin-m-w-d-in-teilzeit-80

title: Directeur/Directrice, Bureau De La Gestion Des Ressources Humaines
sectors: Administration, Management, Finance/Accounting, Procurement; Communications, Media, Knowledge Management, Editor; Human Rights, Law, Migration, Conflicts, Justice
description: Numéro de poste : HRM 237. Classe : D-1. Secteur de tutelle : Bureau de la gestion des ressources humaines (HRM). Lieu d'affectation : Paris. Type de contrat : Engagement de durée définie, 2 ans renouvelable. Recrutement ouvert aux candidats internes et externes. CONTEXTE ORGANISATIONNEL : Le Bureau de la gestion des ressources humaines est chargé d'élaborer, de diriger et de coordonner la mise en œuvre de la Stratégie des ressources humaines de l'UNESCO en étroite collaboration avec ses principales parties prenantes (États membres, direction et personnel), afin que l'Organisation dispose d'un personnel diversifié, hautement qualifié et dévoué dans le monde entier. Le Bureau fournit des services d'appui stratégique en matière de ressources humaines et est responsable des activités et services opérationnels statutaires essentiels. FONCTIONS : Sous la supervision directe de la Sous-Directrice générale pour l'administration et le management (ADG/ADM) et sous la supervision générale de la Directrice générale adjointe, le/la Directeur/Directrice du Bureau de la gestion des ressources humaines (DIR/HRM) dirige et coordonne l'exécution des services de gestion des ressources humaines dans l'ensemble de l'Organisation. Le/la titulaire supervise la fourniture de services RH intégrés (planification des effectifs, recrutement, apprentissage et perfectionnement, gestion de la performance, motivation du personnel), dirige une équipe de professionnels des ressources humaines et supervise la mise en œuvre des initiatives de réforme des ressources humaines. RESPONSABILITÉS CLÉS : fournir conseils et soutien à la direction sur toutes les questions RH ; diriger la conception et la communication de la Stratégie RH de l'UNESCO ; mettre en œuvre un cadre intégré de gestion des talents ; diriger une équipe RH et gérer le programme de travail et le budget du Bureau ; entretenir des relations avec les parties prenantes internes et externes ; représenter l'Organisation dans les instances des Nations Unies (CFPI, Réseau des ressources humaines, Comité de haut niveau sur la gestion). QUALIFICATIONS REQUISES : Diplôme universitaire de haut niveau (master ou équivalent) en ressources humaines, administration ou gestion publique ou des entreprises, droit, sciences sociales ou humaines ou domaines connexes. Au moins 15 années d'expérience à des niveaux de responsabilité croissants, à l'échelle nationale ou internationale, dont une grande partie à des postes de direction ; expérience de la direction de projets de réforme et/ou de transformations organisationnelles. Excellente connaissance et capacité de rédaction dans l'une des langues de travail (anglais ou français) et aptitude à travailler dans la seconde. Souhaitable : hautes fonctions au sein du système des Nations Unies, connaissance du régime commun des Nations Unies, connaissance d'autres langues officielles de l'UNESCO. SALAIRE : Le traitement annuel de départ pour ce poste est de l'ordre de 182 355 dollars des États-Unis, plus prestations (30 jours de congé annuel, allocation pour charges de famille, assurance médicale, régime de retraite). Closing date: 25/09/2026 HOW TO APPLY: Tous les candidats doivent remplir une demande en ligne et fournir des informations complètes et exactes. Pour postuler, veuillez visiter le site Web Carrières de l'UNESCO (https://www.unesco.org/fr/careers). Aucune modification ne peut être apportée à la candidature soumise. Le processus peut inclure des entretiens vidéo préenregistrés et/ou des évaluations écrites, des entretiens avec un jury, ainsi que des vérifications de références. Date limite de candidature (minuit, heure de Paris) : 25/09/2026. https://careers.unesco.org/talentcommunity/apply/1370241057/?locale=fr_FR

title: Director, Bureau of Human Resources Management
sectors: Human Rights, Law, Migration, Conflicts, Justice
description: Position Number: HRM 237. Grade: D-1. Parent Sector: Bureau of Human Resources Management (HRM). Duty Station: Paris. Job Family: Administration. Contract Type: Fixed Term, duration 2 years, renewable. Recruitment open to internal and external candidates. ORGANIZATIONAL CONTEXT: The Bureau of Human Resources Management is responsible for developing, leading and coordinating the implementation of UNESCO's Human Resources Strategy in close collaboration with its key stakeholders — Member States, senior management and UNESCO personnel — ensuring that UNESCO has a diverse, high-skilled and committed workforce worldwide that can deliver the Organization's mandate. The Bureau provides strategic HR support services to management and employees by developing, recommending and facilitating the implementation of human resources policies, programmes and initiatives, and is responsible for statutory operational services essential to programme delivery and workforce well-being. FUNCTIONS OF THE POST: Under the direct supervision of the Assistant Director-General of the Sector for Administration and Management (ADG/ADM), and overall supervision of the Deputy Director-General, the Director of the Bureau of Human Resources Management (DIR/HRM) leads and coordinates the delivery of human resources management services across the Organization, providing authoritative advice to senior management on a broad range of HR matters. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: * Provide guidance and support to senior management on all human resources matters and emerging HR issues; promote sound HR practices, a values-based workplace culture, work-life balance and wellbeing, gender equality and diversity. * Lead and coordinate the formulation, development, implementation and communication of UNESCO's Human Resources Strategy, HR policies, programmes and initiatives; support organizational change and HR reform initiatives. * Lead the design and implementation of an integrated talent management framework covering workforce planning, recruitment, learning and development, and performance management; ensure business intelligence on workforce trends for data-driven decision-making. * Lead a team of HR professionals, set objectives, monitor performance and manage the Bureau's approved work programme and budget. * Build and maintain productive relationships with internal and external stakeholders including Permanent Delegations, academic institutes, professional networks and HR service providers. * Represent the Organization in joint staff–management meetings and UN forums including the ICSC, the HR Network and, as appropriate, the HLCM, and in governing body meetings as required. REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS: Advanced university degree (Master's or equivalent) in human resources, public or business administration or management, law, social or human sciences or related fields. A minimum of 15 years of progressively responsible professional experience at national or international level in human resources, public or business administration, or a related field, a significant part at managerial level. Experience leading change-related projects or organizational transformation. Strong managerial and leadership skills, excellent judgment, analytical and negotiation skills, high professional integrity and political sensitivity, and the ability to work in a multicultural environment. Excellent knowledge and drafting skills in one working language (English or French) and ability to work in the second. DESIRABLE: Senior-level assignments at the international level and/or within the UN system; knowledge of the UN Common System and UN HR Rules and Regulations; knowledge of other official UNESCO languages (Arabic, Chinese, Russian or Spanish). BENEFITS: Basic salary plus benefits which may include 30 days annual leave, family allowance, medical insurance and pension plan. The approximate annual starting salary for this post is US$182,355. Geographical mobility is required for staff appointed to UNESCO's international posts. Closing date: 25/09/2026 HOW TO APPLY: All candidates must complete an on-line application and provide complete and accurate information by the application deadline (Midnight Paris Time, 25/09/2026). To apply, please visit the UNESCO Careers website (https://www.unesco.org/en/careers) or use the 'Apply now' link on the vacancy page. No modifications can be made to the application once submitted. The process may include pre-recorded video interviews and/or written assessments, interviews with a Panel, as well as reference checks. UNESCO does not charge a fee at any stage of the recruitment process. https://careers.unesco.org/talentcommunity/apply/1370240957/?locale=en_GB

title: Manager, Maintenance and Auxiliary Services
description: United States International University-Africa is a higher learning institution based in Nairobi, Kenya, and is the most diverse university in East and Central Africa with about 7,000 students from over 60 nations and a global network of more than 25,000 alumni. USIU-Africa is the only university in Sub-Saharan Africa whose degree programs are accredited by both the Kenya Government through the Commission for University Education (CUE) and by the American Government through the WASC Senior Colleges and Universities Commission (WSCUC). Department: Finance & Operations. Job Type: Part-time. Experience level: Experienced. Job Purpose: Reporting to the Deputy Vice Chancellor, Finance & Operations, the Manager, Maintenance and Auxiliary Services is responsible for the efficient management and delivery of maintenance and auxiliary services operations across the University. The role ensures that all facilities, utilities, and support services are well-maintained, safe, functional, and conducive to learning, teaching, research, and residential life. The position oversees maintenance planning, service delivery, vendor management, and compliance with health, safety, and environmental standards while ensuring optimal utilization of resources and high-quality service delivery to the University community. Key Responsibilities: Oversee preventive and corrective maintenance of university buildings, infrastructure, and equipment; ensure timely response to maintenance requests across academic, administrative, and residential facilities; develop and implement maintenance schedules. Manage auxiliary services such as cleaning, waste management, landscaping, transport, and catering support, and monitor outsourced service providers against service level agreements. Oversee efficient operation of utilities including water, electricity and HVAC systems, monitoring usage and implementing cost-control and sustainability initiatives. Ensure compliance with occupational health and safety standards, environmental regulations and university policies; conduct inspections and risk assessments; support emergency preparedness. Coordinate minor construction, refurbishment and renovation projects, liaising with consultants and contractors. Oversee procurement and management of service providers and contracts. Develop and manage budgets, monitor expenditures, and report on financial and operational performance. Maintain an updated asset inventory and lifecycle management plan. Engage academic departments, student services, housing and administration on facility needs. Identify opportunities to improve efficiency and sustainability, promoting green initiatives and smart facility management systems. Qualifications: Master's Degree in Facilities/Real Estate Management, Business Administration or a related field; Bachelor's Degree in Civil Engineering, Construction Management, Quantity Survey or related fields; professional certification in Facilities/Real Estate Management or Project Management desirable; membership in a relevant professional body; proficiency in computer applications and facilities management systems. Experience: Minimum of five (5) years' relevant experience in facilities management, maintenance operations, auxiliary services management and real estate management within a large institution or similar environment; experience managing outsourced services and contractors; demonstrated experience in maintenance planning, budgeting and project coordination. Core Competencies: Strong leadership and supervisory skills; planning and organizational skills; technical knowledge of facilities and maintenance systems; financial and resource management; problem-solving and decision-making; communication and interpersonal skills; attention to detail and quality orientation; risk management and compliance awareness. Closing date: 2026-09-08 HOW TO APPLY: Interested applicants must apply indicating in the subject line of the email: 'Manager, Maintenance and Auxiliary Services'. Provide a cover letter and a current CV, certified copies of educational certificates and transcripts, names and addresses of three referees (two of whom must be your current and previous employer), current salary and benefits, telephone and e-mail contacts by 5:00PM, Tuesday, September 8, 2026 to: Director Human Resource, United States International University – Africa, P. O. Box 14634-00800, Nairobi, Kenya. Email: jobs-finance@usiu.ac.ke. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. USIU-Africa is an Equal Opportunity Employer. https://www.usiu.ac.ke/vacancies/manager-maintenance-and-auxiliary-services-2/

title: Strategy and Policy Officer - Corporate Strategy
sectors: Administration, Management, Finance/Accounting, Procurement; Trade, Finance, Economics, Cooperation, Global
description: Ref. Number: 25263 Position: Strategy and Policy Officer - Corporate Strategy Minimum 5-8 years of relevant professional experience Department/Division: Strategy, Policy and Budget Department (SPB) Job Type **: Global Recruitment Location: Beijing Posting Date: Aug 25, 2026 Closing Date *: Sep 01, 2026 Strategy and Policy Officer - Corporate Strategy The Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) is a multilateral development bank whose mission is financing Infrastructure for Tomorrow in Asia and beyond – infrastructure with sustainability at its core. We began operations in Beijing in 2016 and have since grown to 111 approved members worldwide. We are capitalized at USD100 billion and AAA-rated by the major international credit rating agencies. Collaborating with partners, AIIB meets clients' needs by unlocking new capital and investing in infrastructure that is green, technology-enabled, and promotes regional connectivity. AIIB’s Strategy, Policy and Budget (SPB) Department is responsible for (i) developing and monitoring the implementation of the Bank’s strategic agenda; (ii) developing and overseeing compliance with the Bank’s operational policies and procedures for the Bank’s infrastructure investment operations (non-treasury), including environmental, social, procurement and financial management; and (iii) developing and monitoring the Bank’s annual business plan to implement the Bank’s strategies and manage the Bank’s administrative budget to support the implementation of the annual business plan. The Bank's first Corporate Strategy (CS), approved at the end of 2020, is built on a number of strategic choices, including focus on Asia, building partnerships, mobilizing investments and focusing on the project cycle. The CS is implemented through the annual Business Plan and Budget (BPB), which defines annual operational and institutional focus areas. Prepare relevant documents to facilitate internal and external communications and consultations. Support the development of the annual business plan to ensure the implementation of CS, including developing and overseeing the implementation of the annual business plan and the quarterly business plan updates. Coordinate cross-departmental consultations, and ensure the link between departmental objectives and corporate level priorities, including in how that requires managing institutional change. Perform or coordinate data analytics work to support the implementation of the CS and the BPB. Represent the Bank in external and internal stakeholder engagements to communicate the Bank's strategies. Any other related items as may be needed and identified by the Director General of SPB. Requirements: A minimum of 5-8 years of experience in strategy development and implementation, business planning and institutional change management. A master's degree in public policy, economics, business, finance, or equivalent from a reputable university. Proven experience in developing and implementing corporate/institutional level strategies, including identifying and implementing necessary actions to support changes. Proven experience of working in a regional or multicountry context. Experience in high-level strategic consulting and in an international organization would be valued Proven critical thinking and analytical skills. Solid understanding of economics, with broad knowledge and familiarity with issues in development finance. Knowledge of and experience in the infrastructure sector is an advantage. Strong organizational skills and proven track record of results. Strong written and verbal communications skills in English. AIIB is committed to diversity, transparency, and inclusion. We believe our strength comes from having a team with the right diverse skills, experiences, and abilities selected through a merit-based competitive process. We actively encourage applications from people from both within and outside AIIB members, regardless of nationality, religion, gender, race, disability, or sexual orientation. Join in AIIB's mission to promote sustainable infrastructure investments and to improve social and economic outcomes in Asia and beyond. title: Network Coordinator
description: Network Coordinator Uganda Organization: Mensen met een Missie Closing date: 8 Sep 2026 Mensen met een Missie is an organisation for international cooperation and solidarity. We challenge beliefs and narratives that normalise exclusion, repair relationships between people on opposing sides, and address the patterns and structures that sustain inequality. Together with locally rooted partner organisations across Africa, Asia and Latin America, we work for peace and equality. Through dialogue, reflection and collaboration, we seek to challenge harmful beliefs, reduce mistrust and division, and strengthen relationships across social and religious divides. Our team in The Hague works closely with partners and changemakers to contribute to more peaceful and inclusive societies. Faith in Freedom is a new Mensen met een Missie programme that seeks to strengthen Freedom of Religion and Belief (FoRB) and contribute to more peaceful and inclusive societies. In Sub-Saharan Africa, the programme works in Cameroon, Kenya, Nigeria and Uganda, building on existing relationships and networks of civil society, faith-based and community actors. At the heart of Faith in Freedom is the principle that everyone should be free to hold, practise, change or abstain from a religion or belief without experiencing discrimination or violence. For Mensen met een Missie, FoRB is closely connected to wider questions of dignity, equality, social cohesion and inclusive citizenship. Religion can contribute to exclusion and division, but religious actors and communities can also play an important role in promoting dialogue, solidarity, reconciliation and social change. The programme combines three mutually reinforcing areas of work: strengthening inclusion and constructive change within religious communities, building trust and cooperation across religions and beliefs, and advocating for more inclusive FoRB-related policies and practices. Particular attention is given to the meaningful participation and leadership of women, youth and religious minorities. Faith in Freedom takes an adaptive approach, with a strong focus on conflict sensitivity, learning, local ownership and evidence-based advocacy. For the Faith in Freedom programme in Uganda we are looking for qualified candidates for the position of Network Coordinator Uganda Starting date: October 1, 2026 In Uganda, 4-6 partner organisations will work together as a country network to implement the Faith in Freedom strategy and workplans. The Network Coordinator facilitates this collaboration and helps partners bring together their complementary strengths. The coordinator supports country-level planning, reporting, learning and advocacy processes and helps maintain strong collaboration between partners and relevant external stakeholders. Based in Uganda, the Network Coordinator serves as an important link between the Uganda partner network and the wider Faith in Freedom programme. The coordinator represents Mensen met een Missie at country level while representing the interests of all partners equally and promoting an inclusive, gender- and faith-sensitive way of working. The coordinator will be contracted by Mensen met een Missie. Tasks and Responsibilities • Coordinate and facilitate the Uganda Faith in Freedom partner network and strengthen collaboration, trust and shared ownership among partners. • Support implementation of the Uganda strategy across the intrafaith, interfaith and extrafaith pathways, helping partners contextualise approaches to Uganda’s FoRB context. • Promote the meaningful participation and leadership of women, youth, religious minorities and other marginalised groups. • Promote conflict-sensitive, power-aware and Do No Harm approaches and help partners respond to changing risks and tensions. • When requested, provide strategic advice and accompaniment of the individual partners. • Serve as the bridge between Uganda and the team in The Netherlands: signal relevant changes and opportunities in the context and among partners, communicating back and forth, translating the overall programme framework to local realities and vice versa. • Coordinate the Uganda advocacy agenda and connect partner priorities and community experiences to relevant local and national stakeholders, drawing on technical support from the Mensen met een Missie team where needed. • Maintain strategic relationships with relevant stakeholders, including government institutions, religious bodies, civil society networks and the Embassy of the Kingdom of the Netherlands. Programme coordination, learning and advocacy • Coordinate annual planning, reflection and country reporting processes, bringing together partner inputs in collaboration with the Mensen met een Missie’s programme management and PMEL teams. • Follow up on partner reporting and support consolidation of the country’s overall narrative reports; the coordinator is not expected to write all reporting independently. • Work with the PMEL team to coordinate monitoring, evaluation and learning processes, including baseline, mid-term and endline activities where relevant. • Create opportunities for partners to reflect on progress, context changes, risks and learning, and support follow-up on agreed adaptations. • Organise linking and learning events, peer exchange and cross-country learning opportunities. • Identify capacity-strengthening needs with partners and organise appropriate technical assistance, training, accompaniment or peer learning. • Coordinate logistics for visits and missions, including arranging appointments, travel and accommodation, and coordinating security assessments and other practical arrangements. Safeguarding, inclusion and accountability • Promote gender equality, inclusion, local ownership and mutual accountability throughout the programme. • Ensure partners are familiar with relevant SEAH, safeguarding, integrity and risk-management policies and procedures. • Signal and report suspected misconduct, fraud, safeguarding incidents or other integrity concerns through the appropriate channels. Organisational position The Network Coordinator is a Ugandan citizen, based in Uganda and works closely with the Uganda partner network, the Faith in Freedom Programme Manager and PMEL team, regional and international Lobby & Advocacy (L&A) colleagues, and network coordinators in other FiF countries. Technical expertise in PMEL, advocacy, FoRB and other areas is available from the wider Mensen met een Missie team. Required Technical Skills, Experience & Knowledge • Relevant academic background and professional experience in international development, human rights, peacebuilding, governance or a related field. • Good understanding of FoRB and of Uganda’s religious, social and political context, with willingness to further develop thematic expertise. • Experience working with religious actors, faith-based organisations and/or diverse civil society actors, with sensitivity to religious diversity and inclusion. • Experience coordinating partner networks, multi-stakeholder processes or consortium programmes, with strong facilitation and relationship-building skills. • Experience with programme coordination, planning and reporting, monitoring, evaluation, learning processes and familiarity with advocacy. • Commitment to gender equality, inclusion, conflict sensitivity, Do No Harm and safeguarding. • Strong analytical, organisational and communication skills, with an ability to turn complex issues into practical actions. • Excellent written and verbal English; knowledge of relevant Ugandan language(s) is an asset. • Ugandan citizenship and ability and willingness to travel regularly to programme locations within the country. • Proactive, collaborative and reflective working style, and confidence using Office 365 and online collaboration tools. Our offer • An inspiring and challenging position and assignment within an enthusiastic and motivated partner network. • A competitive country-specific salary. • Opportunities for personal development and training. • Essential supplies (laptop, internet subscription, etc) to set-up your own workplace. How to apply Interested Send your application letter (in English) together with your CV to sollicitatie@mensenmeteenmissie.nl by September 8, 2026. Please clearly mention the job title you are applying for in the subject line of your email. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. For more information about this position, please contact Christina Maasdam via email at christinamaasdam@mensenmeteenmissie.nl. Mensen met een Missie is an organisation where diversity and inclusion are paramount, and everyone feels welcome and valued. We encourage applications from individuals of all backgrounds, regardless of religion, ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation, or age.

description: THE ASEAN SECRETARIAT INVITES ASEAN NATIONALS TO APPLY FOR THE FOLLOWING VACANCY SENIOR OFFICER CULTURE AND INFORMATION DIVISION Background The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) was founded in 1967 with the purpose of promoting regional cooperation in Southeast Asia, in the spirit of equality and partnership and thereby contribute towards peace, progress and prosperity in the region. ASEAN comprises eleven countries in Southeast Asia, with Timor-Leste being admitted as an ASEAN Member State during the 47 th ASEAN Summit on 26 October 2025 in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. It was proclaimed a Community through the “Kuala Lumpur Declaration on ASEAN 2025: Forging Ahead Together”, signed by the ASEAN Leaders during their 27 th Summit 2015. The ASEAN Community Vision 2025 calls for the ASEAN Community in forging ahead together, and to work towards building a community that is politically cohesive, economically integrated and socially responsible. The ASEAN Secretariat was established in 1976 by the Foreign Minister of ASEAN with basic functions of providing greater efficiency in the coordination of ASEAN organs and for more effective implementation of ASEAN projects and activities. It is also envisioned to be the nerve centre of a strong and confident ASEAN Community that is globally respected for acting in full compliance with its Charter and in the best interest of its people. In alignment with the ASEAN Community Vision 2045 and Strategic Plans of the three ASEAN pillars of Political Security Community, Economic Community and Socio-Cultural Community, and ASEAN Connectivity, supported by the Department of Community and Corporate Affairs, the ASEAN Secretariat is inviting qualified ASEAN Nationals to apply for the position of Senior Officer Culture and Information Division. Duties and Responsibilities: Reporting to Assistant Director Culture and Information Division, the Senior Officer shall be responsible to: 1. Provide substantive research and analysis to support policy recommendations, technical advice and initiatives to the respective sectoral bodies’ (namely SOMCA, SOMRI, SOMRI WGs, SCI, SCC, COCI) work plans/programmes Develop research and analysis that can be used to support policy recommendations, technical advice and initiatives including providing input to the drafting of outcome documents, information and position papers, concept notes, briefing notes and talking points, and other knowledge products. Manage and support regional priorities including cross-cutting matters related to the development of the cultural and creative industries to advance the ASEAN Creative Economy, and promote ASEAN awareness and ASEAN Identity, and priorities under the information and media sector (mitigating disinformation, facilitating access to information and fostering information integrity, harnessing artificial intelligence and digital technologies for the media sector), and priorities under the culture and the art sector (promoting and safeguarding cultural heritage, developing the cultural and creative ecosystem, enabling the role of culture to foster tolerance and greater understanding). Coordinate and monitor the reporting input on the status of the above sectoral work plans to the ASCC Analysis and Monitoring Divisions (AMD), and Programme Cooperation & Project Management Division, and other divisions where required. Assist in coordinating with other Divisions including the Community Relations Division to develop effective outreach strategies in promoting ASEAN awareness and branding ASEAN Identity. Liaise with ASCC AMD in the development of the M&E framework and indicators for the two sectors. Monitor relevant policy developments at the regional and international levels. 2. Coordinate and provide technical support on the development, implementation and evaluation programmes and/or projects in support of the ASEAN Socio-Cultural Community (ASCC) and the ASEAN Community Coordinate the development programmes and/or projects, and provide technical support where necessary to drive initiatives in the promotion of ASEAN Identity and awareness. Provide suggestions and ideas for projects and activities that can enhance the ability of the culture and the arts sector, as well as information and media sectors in disseminating information to the public about ASEAN developments, as well as on addressing other strategic issues relating to the sectors. 3. Funding mobilisation and funds management Assist in managing disbursements of the ASEAN Cultural Fund. Coordinate and assist in mobilisation of funds to implement the approved work plans/programmes and projects. 4. Coordinate and provide technical support to promote ASEAN and its contribution in the implementation of global agenda, such as the 2030 UN SDGs Represent the ASEAN Secretariat and serve as a resource person when required. Coordinate and/or manage operational linkages with associated ASEAN bodies, dialogue partners, private sector and other institutions to further strengthen cooperation in culture and arts, information and media, and to promote ASEAN and its contribution in the implementation of global agenda, such as the 2030 UN SDGs. 5. Other duties Coordinate, supervise, and assist in managing tasks and activities of staff, including compilation of technical input and prepare relevant documents including media releases and presentations for the meetings. Coordinate and provide support in meetings, including preparing background papers and drafting meeting reports/summary of discussions, and assisting the hosting institutions on substantial matters. Provide feedback on the performance of technical officer/assistant. Coordinate input to, and assist in managing the budget of the Division And other duties when required. Qualifications and experience: Advanced university degree (Master’s or equivalent degree) in relevant discipline primarily related to the culture and the arts, media and information, or international relations, e.g. Cultural studies and relations, Heritage Management, Art History and Literature, Media and Broadcasting Management, Public Policy, Public Administration, Communications, Journalism, International Relations/Studies, Management or an appropriate related field. At least three (3) years working experience with strong or relevant background in culture and the arts or communication and media and/or international relations in both government sector and/or private sector. Bachelor’s degree with minimum five (5) years’ work experience in lieu of the advanced degree, may also be considered. Extensive experience in message and programme development, with advanced, sound writing skills and a proven track record of managing multiple projects. Strong media and social media acumen to communicate with diverse audiences across multiple channels, including traditional, new media and digital platforms. Keen interest in the arts and culture, information and media sectoral developments. Proven experience in substantive research, project management, public policy development, and in working closely with government officials. Experience in cross-cultural environment and international settings is an advantage. Demonstrated sound political and cultural sensitivity, and ability to maintain a broad and informed understanding of international and regional developments, geopolitical trends, and socio-cultural contexts; and to critically connect developments across countries and sectors in assessing their implications and identifying collaborative opportunities in supporting the development of cross-cutting matters under the two sectors. Demonstrated good interpersonal skills, ability to develop and maintain sound working relationships with public and private sector organisations, stakeholders and partners, and work effectively with people at all levels of the organisations. Competency in digital skills with adequate knowledge of Microsoft Office applications, and in the use of AI tools to optimise workflow. Proven ability for accuracy under pressure and adherence to deadlines. Sound and robust analytical skills, with competency to synthesise, process information and develop them effectively into reports or other knowledge products. An effective, dynamic team player, and able to work independently where required. Excellent command of English, written and spoken. Willing to travel. Remuneration and Benefits: Successful candidate will be offered a basic salary of USD 3,893 and attractive remuneration package including housing, outpatient medical reimbursement, hospitalization & life insurance, children’s education and gratuity. title: Field Coordinator
sectors: Communications, Media, Knowledge Management, Editor; Environment, Climate, Energy, Water, Sanitation
description: Field Coordinator Organization: International Solidarity What are we doing Mission duration: 6 months. Location : Artibonite SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI) is an international humanitarian aid organization that, for over 40 years, has been aiding populations affected by armed conflict and natural disasters by addressing their vital needs: water, food, and shelter. Particularly committed to combating diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death worldwide, SI implements its interventions with expertise in the areas of access to drinking water, sanitation, and hygiene promotion, as well as in the essential areas of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, SI's teams—a total of 3,200 people including expatriates, national staff, headquarters staff, and a few volunteers—operate with professionalism and dedication, respecting local cultures. The mission The Haiti mission currently has a base and coordination office in Port-au-Prince. Projects focus on WASH (Water, Sanitation and Hygiene) and SAME/NUT (Health, Social and Environmental Protection/Non-Food Items) in consortium with national and international partners. It is funded by OCHA, CDCS, SDC, ECHO, UNICEF, and IFSAN, among others. For the past two years, the mission has experienced significant growth in terms of operations and budget, responding to emergencies in the Port-au-Prince metropolitan area while also developing longer-term initiatives. It is within this context that the Haiti mission has decided to open a new base in Artibonite, located in Saint-Marc, to address the WASH needs of the population in this department. The base is currently in its initial stages of opening; the main task of the Territorial Coordination Team will be to formalize and complete the base after its opening. 17 expatriates and 80 national staff are based at the single Port-au-Prince headquarters. An initial setup of 2-3 expatriates and around 20 national staff is planned for the Artibonite base. Job description GENERAL OBJECTIVE The Field Coordinator acts as Country Director (CD) for Solidarités International (SI) in the Artibonite region. Based on the geopolitical and humanitarian context, they propose the strategy for Artibonite and ensure its implementation once approved. They monitor and guarantee that projects are carried out in accordance with the Solidarités International charter and in compliance with internal and contractual procedures. They mobilize the necessary material and financial resources for the successful implementation of programs and oversee their management. They coordinate the teams on the ground and are responsible for their safety in their area of assignment. They are the direct and primary contact for the CD. SPECIFIC ISSUES AND CHALLENGES This position was created following the opening of the Artibonite base. We are looking for a highly experienced Technical Officer (TOO) with expertise in this level of security, as well as extensive experience in structuring a new base after the initial opening phase. The security challenges – level 4 at SI – are numerous, particularly in the context of a new base. PRIORITIES FOR THE FIRST 2-3 MONTHS Project management and implementation Operational management of security in the area and continuity of the access work undertaken Support for the development of new project proposals in the area Working internally on the structuring of the base, finalizing recruitment, finalizing the installation of the living quarters and offices, training on working at SI, setting up procedures. Supporting the strategy on Artibonite and continuing its development To help strengthen ties with our local and international partners and clusters in the area SECURITY CONSTRAINTS Haiti is categorized as Level 4. Security is very volatile/deteriorated in Artibonite due to the presence of armed groups and daily clashes, but this does not prevent activities from taking place. Mission security rules are strict (curfew at sunset). Your profile DEGREE AND EXPERIENCE Diploma: Master's level Experience in the humanitarian sector: 5 years or more Experience in a similar role: 3-4 years SKILLS TECHNICAL SKILLS 1. Ability to monitor and analyze the humanitarian, political, cultural, social, and economic context 2. Skills to ensure the coordination, development, monitoring and evaluation of programs implemented in its area of intervention 3. Propose the human, financial and logistical resources needed for its area of intervention as well as its organization 4. HR management, recruitment, induction, creation of team dynamics, implementation of the remote base - coo relationship for Haiti (the other base is in Port au Prince, directly linked to the coo) 5. To be responsible for the safety of teams and property within their assigned area, as delegated by the DP CROSS-FUNCTIONAL SKILLS 1. Analysis, decision-making and crisis management: ability to assess risks, anticipate, decide and act under pressure. 2. Leadership and communication: guiding, training, raising awareness and conveying clear instructions to teams and partners. 3. Diplomacy and adaptability: negotiating with various actors, maintaining relationships of trust and adjusting to an unstable environment. LANGUAGES 1. French 2. English appreciated SI will offer you the following conditions A salaried position: Depending on experience, starting from EUR 2800 gross per month (2600 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 750. SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's home country and the place of assignment. Breaks: During the mission, a system of alternating work and leave is in place, with 7 working days off every three months (with USD 850 allocated by Solidarités International). In addition to these break periods, one extra day of leave is granted for each month worked. Social and medical coverage: Expatriates benefit from insurance that reimburses all healthcare costs (including medical and surgical fees, dental and ophthalmological care, and repatriation) and a supplementary benefits system that includes war risks. title: Earthquake Response Manager
description: Venezuela Earthquake Response Manager- Readvertised Organization: HelpAge International Closing date: 2 Sep 2026 Location: Venezuela, with flexibility to be based either in-country or in a nearby regional hub. Department: Programme Support Reports to (Line Manager): Head of Programme Support Grade: UK Salary Grade D or its equivalent based on the cost of living in the country of hire Contract Type: 12 months, Fixed term About HelpAge HelpAge International works with a diverse global network of around 200 organisations across 99 countries to promote the rights of older people to lead dignified, healthy and secure lives. Through partnership and collaborations, we work to ensure the inclusion of older people across society and strive to deliver a just and fair world for everyone as they get older. Our work is driven by our desire to achieve real impact for older people, to be inclusive, to work in partnership and to learn from our shared experience. Venezuela Earthquake Crisis On 24 June, two consecutive earthquakes of magnitude 7.2 and 7.5 struck north-central Venezuela at around 18:00 local time, followed by more than 130 aftershocks. The most affected areas are La Guaira, Caracas/Capital District, Miranda, Carabobo, and Yaracuy, with La Guaira reported as the area of most severe humanitarian impact. The earthquake has compounded the chronic deterioration of Venezuela's critical infrastructure, affecting transport networks, electricity, water systems, telecommunications, and public services. Damage to health facilities has further strained an already fragile health system, reducing access to emergency care, disrupting the continuity of treatment for chronic conditions, and limiting the availability of mental health and psychosocial support services at a time of increased demand. We are seeking a passionate, professional and experienced candidate to support our response to the Venezuela earthquake crisis, someone who thrives in collaborating with others (inside HelpAge International and beyond) and who can work in agile ways and across boundaries. About the Job The Venezuela Earthquake Response Manager will be responsible for the overall management of the Humanitarian response programme in Venezuela, which will be implemented by local partners, and will work closely with relevant members of the Programme Support and other Teams engaged with this emergency. There will be a strong focus on promoting the inclusion of older people in the emergency response and engaging in advocacy, as well as supporting roll out of training and guidance to make that happen. We are looking for someone skilled in program design and implementation, proposal preparation (with support from humanitarian staff), partner capacity building and support, quality assurance and monitoring, donor and stakeholder representation. Key areas for impact/influence and responsibilities • Develop overall programmatic response and support 2-5 local implementing partners in programme start-up/scale up in response to the catastrophic earthquake in Venezuela. • Oversee the programme management of humanitarian partner-led response, in line with Humanitarian Inclusion Standards with a focus on older people, in earthquake affected communities • Monitor the quality of the humanitarian response, supporting implementing partners, making recommendations for change where needed to improve the impact on the lives of older people • Work closely with the implementing partner organisations, including building their capacity, to ensure a high quality, age-friendly, inclusive, coordinated response • Identify and develop new funding opportunities and project partnerships to build a humanitarian portfolio of work and increase the impact for older people in the response. • Lead coordination between local implementing partners, HelpAge global teams and supporting members / donors • With support from MEAL colleagues, lead on Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning for the response, tracking progress, sharing and utilizing related information, data, learning and evidence across the organisation and externally • Ensure security of all staff and assets and compliance with external standards and internal requirements • Act as primary representative with host governments, other officials in charge, donors, clusters, UN agencies and other International and national NGOs • With the HelpAge Global Communications Manager be the primary spokesperson for HelpAge International on the ground which may include various media. Skills and experience required You will be someone with: • Extensive experience managing complex multi-sector programs in an acute emergency situation • Experience managing multi-donor funded projects including experience working with key emergency donors such as DEC, ECHO, Appeal funds, Trust and Foundations • Demonstrable experience in leadership and programme management with local partners and geographically dispersed teams and in challenging humanitarian contexts. • Familiarity with the Cluster system and its various areas of focus, with preferable experience in Protection and Inclusion promotion. • Substantial experience in all aspects of Project Cycle Management with particular focus on proposal development, quality assurance, monitoring, • Excellent interpersonal skills and a demonstrated ability to lead effectively in insecure environments • An ability to represent HelpAge with traditional and non-traditional partners, donors and networks. • Extensive knowledge of humanitarian principles, standards and human rights. • Experienced in strengthening and supporting staff and national partner capacity • An ability to travel, occasionally at short notice. • Strong oral and written Spanish and English language communication skills Desirable • Previous work experience in Venezuela or with communities in LAC region • Experience of working with older people and people with disabilities Key Behavioural Competencies Working Collaboratively with Others: Work collaboratively, building mutual trust and respect, withexternal organizations and partners to achieve our strategic aims and objectives; being accountable for the work we do together. Adaptability and Flexibility: Adapt to new directions or opportunities arising within the organisation andin our workarea; being flexible in our role, constantly using the feedback to learn more and evolve further. Supporting and Facilitating Change: Lead behavioural and cultural change through embracing a supportive, collaborative and highly inclusive environment where everybody feels supported, respected and engaged. Extend HelpAge’s Reach and Impact: Extend HelpAge’s reach and impact by creating and identifying new business development opportunities and building relationships with new partners. Diversity and Inclusion: Lead and promote a culture of including the voices of older people across our support, convening and thought leadership roles, in a way that is transformative, empowering and highly inclusive of those marginalised by gender, economic status, disability and other factors of discrimination. Leading Others (for managers): Demonstrate strong leadership to own unit/department and manage people in a well and reputable manner. Create an atmosphere of trust and an enabling environment where staff can contribute their best and develop their potential. Safeguarding HelpAge International is committed to safeguarding the communities with which we work, our partners, staff and any others who we come into contact with. description: Recrutement D'un Consultant Individuel Pour Élaborer Le Manuel De Procédure De Laboratoire National De Contrôle Qualité Des Médicaments (LNCQM) Le Gouvernement de la République du Tchad a reçu un Don de l'Association Internationale de Développement (IDA) N° E2400-TD pour financer le Projet pour l'Autonomisation des Femmes et le Dividende Démographique en Afrique Sub-Saharienne Plus (SWEDD+). Une partie de ce financement sera utilisée pour recruter un consultant individuel chargé d'élaborer le manuel de procédure du Laboratoire National de Contrôle Qualité des Médicaments (LNCQM). Le consultant devra être titulaire d'un diplôme universitaire de niveau Bac+4 minimum en management, administration des entreprises, gestion de projet, droit, finances, ou toute discipline connexe impliquant une formation à la structuration organisationnelle et à la rédaction formelle. Un diplôme dans les domaines de la santé, de la pharmacie ou de la chimie sera considéré comme un atout distinctif. Les critères de sélection sont les références techniques liées à des missions similaires. Les dispositions relatives au conflit d'intérêts du Règlement de Passation des Marchés de la Banque mondiale (édition juillet 2016, révisée novembre 2020) s'appliquent à cette manifestation d'intérêt. Le consultant sera sélectionné selon la méthode de Sélection des Consultants Individuels. L'avis et les termes de référence complets sont disponibles sur le site du projet : www.sweddchad.org. HOW TO APPLY: Les Consultants intéressés doivent transmettre leur CV en langue française, à l'attention du Coordonnateur National du projet SWEDD+, au plus tard le 31 août 2026 à 15h30 (heure locale N'Djaména), en portant clairement la mention de l'avis N°002/MFBEPCI/SE/SG/SWEDD+/PM/2026. Courriel : sweddtchad@gmail.com. Adresse : Unité de Gestion du Projet SWEDD+, BP 2268 N'Djamena, Tchad, Quartier Repos, rue de 30m à côté du Lycée de la Liberté.

title: Procurement Specialist (Individual Consultant)
company: Directorate General of Water Management (DGWM), Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry
description: Procurement Specialist (Individual Consultant) – Türkiye Flood and Drought Management Project The Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry (MoAF) of Türkiye, Directorate General of Water Management (DGWM), has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Türkiye Flood and Drought Management Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. DGWM serves as the co-implementing agency for the Project, whose overall objective is to support climate change projections, determine their impacts on scenario-specific flood and drought disasters, and improve and expand existing early warning systems, while strengthening technical and operational capacities of stakeholders. DGWM has established a Project Implementation Unit (PIU) to manage project activities and intends to engage a Procurement Specialist (individual consultant) to provide technical support to the PIU in managing procurement activities under the Project. The Procurement Specialist will be responsible for planning and providing procurement services, including preparing procurement plans, bidding documents, evaluation reports, training activities, and monitoring contract performance. The consultant will be selected through the Open Competitive Selection of Individual Consultants method in accordance with the World Bank's Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (September 2023). The assignment is expected to commence in September 2026, with a one-year, full-time contract including a two-month probation period, based in Ankara with potential travel to project sites. Detailed Terms of Reference, including qualification requirements and scope of work, are available at the borrower's website. HOW TO APPLY: Interested eligible candidates should submit their CVs in both English and Turkish (in the format specified on the website), clearly indicating the position title and reference number TR-DGWM-564534-CS-INDV in the subject line. Applications must be delivered in PDF format via e-mail no later than September 9, 2026, at 16:00 (local time).

title: IT Support
company: National Directorate of Water Supply and Sanitation (DNAAS), Mozambique
description: IT Support for Dashboard to DNAAS The Government of Mozambique received financing from the World Bank of USD 150 million for the Rural and Small Towns Water Security Project (P173518), aimed at increasing safely managed water and sanitation services in selected small towns and rural areas of Nampula and Zambézia provinces in northern Mozambique. DNAAS invites qualified individual consultants to express interest in providing consulting services to improve the visual resources of the project's dashboard (Kobo, Excel and Power BI). Scope includes: proposing technical adjustments to databases and dashboard tools and defining user responsibilities; implementing validation rules, a data quality view, a data dictionary and transformation map, scheduled updates with error alerts; configuring role-based access for DNAAS/AIAS/provincial/district users with an access matrix; applying a consistent theme aligned with Project/Government/World Bank style, redesigning layouts for clarity, ensuring accessibility and Portuguese/English translation; optimizing queries, DAX and visuals, and documenting performance improvements. Required qualifications: portfolio of prior data visualization work; at least 5 years of experience in data visualization, BI and web design; proven experience with Power BI (data modeling, DAX, access control, performance tuning), certifications an advantage; experience integrating KoboToolbox and Excel into BI workflows; familiarity with M&E in the WASH sector an advantage; knowledge of good digital design practices; and experience with data quality management, stakeholder workshops and training (Portuguese proficiency required). Selection will follow the Individual Consultant Selection method under the World Bank's Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (February 2025). HOW TO APPLY: Interested individual consultants should submit information demonstrating relevant qualifications and experience (CV, description of similar services, experience in similar conditions, availability, etc.) in Portuguese, in physical form to the Ministry of Public Works, Housing and Water Resources, Procurement Department, Av. Karl Marx nº 606, P.O. Box 268, Maputo, and by email to procurementpas@gmail.com, by 15:30 on September 4, 2026.
