description: Procurement and Travel Manager Organization: Pacific Community Closing date: 27 Sep 2026 Description The Pacific Community (SPC) is the principal scientific and technical organisation in the Pacific region, supporting development since 1947. We are an international development organisation owned and governed by our 27 country and territory members. In pursuit of sustainable development to benefit Pacific people, our organisation works across more than 25 sectors. We are known for our knowledge and innovation in such areas as fisheries science, public health, geoscience, and conservation of plant genetic resources for food and agriculture. The Operations and Integration (O&I) collective delivers essential enabling services that support the organisation’s scientific and technical portfolio. Our key functions include corporate services, programme support, partnerships, resource mobilisation, and strategic engagement. These services are coordinated through our regional and satellite offices across the Pacific and Europe. Additionally, the O&I collective leads a dedicated workstream focused on organisational change and transformation to drive continuous improvement and adaptability. The role – Procurement and Travel Manager will lead the Procurement and Travel Team under Implementation Support Services (ISS) in providing high quality advice and service for procurement and travel activities; to provide expert and specialist advice to influence the strategic direction of SPC’s procurement and travel activities; to strengthen internal understanding and capabilities of SPC staff in procurement and travel processes; and to drive procurement and travel improvements as part of the ‘One O&I’ workplan, with a particular focus on improvements in processes, procedures and systems and building excellent relationships internally and externally. The role will also lead the digital transformation of SPC’s procurement function under the ISS transformation programme, including implementation of an eProcurement and the shift to a category-management and business-partnering model. The key responsibilities of the role include: Leadership, Management and Operations: Procurement and Travel Lead SPC’s procurement and travel functions to deliver high quality customer service advice. Provide harmonised and consistent service across SPC to the agreed service standards and in accordance with SPC’s Procurement Policy and Travel Policy. Lead on organisation-wide procurement and travel planning, including strategic planning. Lead on the management of organisation-wide procurement and travel risk management. Lead the shift to a category-management and business-partnering model. Systems and Processes Enhancement In collaboration with Head of ISS and with participation of key stakeholders (e.g. divisions), drive procurement and travel improvements as part of the one O&I business plan, with a particular focus on improvements in processes, procedures and systems. Harmonise processes, systems and procedures across all SPC locations for procurement and travel. Lead the implementation and embedding of the eProcurement (source-to-contract) SaaS platform, including its integration with Business Central (requisition-to-pay). Establish integrated procurement tracking and management information across the source-to-contract lifecycle. Advice Provide advice to influence the strategic direction of SPC’s procurement processes. Provide advice to decision-makers on complex procurement and travel issues (contracts, exceptions, protests, management of COI etc.). Provide recommendations on policy and process updates. Advise on aligning procurement practice with donor and international frameworks. People Management Manage procurement and travel staff and resources. Lead SPC’s training plan for strategic procurement and travel activities. Stakeholder Relationship Management Build robust collaborative relationships with senior staff across O&I and SPC. Ensure excellent communication with key stakeholders and build strong relationships. Provide leadership on internal and external stakeholder relationship management. For a more detailed account of the key responsibilities, please refer to the online job description. Key selection criteria Qualifications Advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in a related field, or equivalent body of knowledge and experience. Technical expertise At least 12 years of experience managing a team, providing advice on procurement matters in a public sector environment. Excellent analytical skills. Language skills Excellent English communication skills (oral and written) with a working knowledge of French being an advantage. Interpersonal skills and cultural awareness Ability to work in a multicultural, inclusive and equitable environment. Salary, terms and conditions Contract Duration – 3 years – subject to renewal depending on funding and performance. Remuneration – The Procurement and Travel Manager is a band 12 position in SPC’s 2026 salary scale, with a starting salary range of 3,743-4,679 SDR (special drawing rights) per month, which currently converts to approximately FJD 11,566–14,458 (USD 5,016–6,270; EUR 4,526–5,658). An offer of appointment for an initial contract will normally be made in the lower half of this range, with due consideration given to experience and qualifications. Progression within the salary scale will be based on annual performance reviews. Remuneration of expatriate SPC staff members is not subject to income tax in Fiji; Fiji nationals employed by SPC in Fiji will be subject to income tax. Benefits for Staff in a position advertised internationally (EPAI) whose duty station is Suva – SPC provides a housing allowance of FJD 1,500–5,200 per month. Establishment and repatriation grant, removal expenses, airfares, home leave travel, health and life and disability insurances and education allowances are available for eligible employees and their eligible dependents. Employees are entitled to 25 working days of annual leave per annum and other types of leave, and access to SPC’s Provident Fund (contributing 8% of salary, to which SPC adds a 10% contribution). Languages – SPC’s working languages are English and French. Recruitment principles – SPC’s recruitment is based on merit and fairness, and candidates are competing in a selection process that is fair, transparent and non-discriminatory. SPC is an equal-opportunity employer, and is committed to cultural and gender diversity, including bilingualism, and will seek to attract and appoint candidates who respect these values. Due attention is given to gender equity and the maintenance of strong representation from Pacific Island professionals. If two interviewed candidates are ranked equal by the selection panel, preference will be given to the Pacific Islander. Applicants will be assured of complete confidentiality in line with SPC’s Privacy Policy. How to apply Application procedure Closing Date: 27 September 2026 at 11:59pm (Fiji time) Job Reference: JM000989 Applicants must apply online at http://careers.spc.int/ Hard copies of applications will not be accepted. For your application to be considered, you must provide us with: an updated resume with contact details for three professional referees a cover letter detailing your skills, experience and interest in this position responses to all screening questions Your application will be considered incomplete and will not be reviewed at shortlisting stage if all the above documents are not provided. Applicants should not attach copies of qualifications or letters of reference. Please ensure your documents are in Microsoft Word or Adobe PDF format. For international staff in Fiji, only one foreign national per family can be employed with an entity operating in Fiji at any one given time. SPC may assist on a case-by-case basis with submissions to Fiji Ministry of Foreign Affairs for their consideration and final approval. SPC cannot and does not make any guarantee whatsoever of approval for such applications to Fiji Ministry of Foreign Affairs and where an application is approved, the spouse or partner will subject to such terms and conditions as may be set from time to time by the Ministry. SPC does not charge a fee to consider your application and will never ask for your banking or financial information during the recruitment process. description: Programme Management - Senior Analyst Organization: UNOPS Closing date: 4 Sep 2026 Job Description Support the delivery of flagship initiatives and strategic partnerships that strengthen the United Nations’ engagement with and for young people globally. UNOPS has signed an agreement with the United Nations to implement the activities for the United Nations Youth Office. The United Nations Youth Office was established to strengthen the UN system’s capacity to engage with and for young people, advance meaningful youth engagement across intergovernmental and policy processes, and support the implementation of global commitments for youth. The Office serves as the system-wide anchor on youth affairs, convening stakeholders across the UN system, governments, civil society, philanthropy, and the private sector to accelerate youth-centered action. Within this context, the Programme Management - Senior Analyst will support the design, coordination, and implementation of strategic initiatives, flagship programmes, and partnerships across the Office’s workstreams. The incumbent will contribute to strengthening ecosystem engagement, operationalizing communities of practice, supporting high-level advocacy and global convenings, and advancing integrated programme delivery across thematic priorities, including youth participation, skills development, mental health and wellbeing, and climate action. The incumbent of this position will be personnel of UNOPS under its full administrative and financial responsibility. The Programme Management - Senior Analyst will provide substantive and operational support for the planning, implementation, and coordination of key initiatives led by the UN Youth Office. This includes supporting flagship events and strategic processes, strengthening stakeholder coordination mechanisms, advancing community-building and partnership ecosystems, and contributing to advocacy and policy priorities. The role requires strong programme management, stakeholder engagement, and coordination skills, as well as the ability to work across teams and with external partners in a dynamic and high-visibility environment. 1. Programme Planning and Delivery • Support the planning, coordination, and implementation of flagship programmes and initiatives led by the UN Youth Office, ensuring timely and high-quality delivery against agreed objectives. • Contribute to the execution of the UN Youth Office annual workplan, including cross-functional coordination across thematic and operational pillars. • Support the delivery of major youth-focused convenings and engagements, including high-level events during the UN General Assembly, ECOSOC Youth Forum, and other strategic global moments. • Contribute to the planning and execution of the annual UN Youth Townhall and related ecosystem engagement mechanisms. • Assist in developing implementation plans, timelines, and operational workflows for strategic initiatives. 2. Stakeholder Coordination and Ecosystem Activation • Support the day-to-day implementation of strategic multi-stakeholder initiatives led by the UN Youth Office, including flagship partnership deliverables focused on youth engagement, skills development, and ecosystem strengthening. • Coordinate stakeholder engagement processes across youth-serving organizations, institutional partners, and aligned networks to support collective action and sustained collaboration. • Contribute to the implementation of the UN Youth Office’s global youth network strategy, including the development of coordination structures, engagement pathways, and collaboration mechanisms under key partner-supported initiatives. • Support the operational delivery of the Misk Foundation partnership workplan, including coordination of activities related to the establishment and growth of a global youth network and associated communities of practice. • Maintain and strengthen stakeholder management systems, including partner mapping, engagement tracking, and follow-up processes to support effective collaboration and accountability. • Facilitate regular coordination with youth constituencies, implementing partners, and ecosystem actors to ensure alignment, visibility of opportunities, and continuity across initiatives. • Support the preparation of stakeholder briefings, convening materials, and engagement summaries to inform decision-making and strategic planning. 3. UN Youth Compass Coordination and Community Building • Support implementation of the UN Youth Compass as a flagship system-wide initiative, ensuring effective coordination across internal teams and external stakeholders. • Contribute to the operationalization and expansion of the UN Youth Compass Community as a global community of practice and “network of networks” for youth-serving stakeholders. • Conduct stakeholder mapping and ecosystem analysis to identify opportunities for strategic engagement, alignment, and partnership-building. • Support development of value propositions, engagement frameworks, and coordination models for communities of practice and partner networks. • Facilitate coordination with aligned initiatives across the UN system and external ecosystem actors. 4. Advocacy, Communications and Influencer Engagement • Support the development and implementation of advocacy initiatives to advance key UN Youth Office priorities, including youth mental health and wellbeing, youth skills, and civic participation. • Facilitate the day-to-day engagements of the Young Leaders for the SDGs, as the UN Youth Office’s flagship recognition scheme for young people around the world. • Contribute to the design and execution of influencer engagement strategies and external-facing campaigns. • Coordinate outreach and engagement with digital creators, youth advocates, and public-facing partners to amplify youth priorities. • Draft briefing notes, speaking points, key messages, and background materials for senior leadership engagements. 5. Youth Climate Engagement and Strategic Coordination Support coordination and engagement with UN system climate partners and youth constituencies under relevant youth climate coordination mechanisms, including engagement with EOSG, UNFCCC, YOUNGO, and COP-related youth actors. Coordinate regular meetings, consultations, and follow-up processes related to youth and climate action. Support the Assistant Secretary-General for Youth Affairs on climate-related engagements through drafting, logistical support, and stakeholder coordination. Contribute to policy and advocacy inputs connecting youth priorities to climate and sustainability agendas. 6. Monitoring, Knowledge Management and Reporting • Support tracking of programme implementation, milestones, and deliverables across assigned workstreams. • Maintain internal coordination tools, stakeholder databases, and reporting frameworks. • Contribute to drafting donor updates, internal reports, meeting summaries, and strategic briefs. • Capture lessons learned and support knowledge-sharing across initiatives and partnerships. • Support data collection and analysis to strengthen evidence-based programme planning and partner engagement. description: Project Director Organization: International Rescue Committee Closing date: 24 Sep 2026 BACKGROUND The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGOs), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities, helping people survive, reclaim control of their futures, and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, join us in positively impacting the lives of millions worldwide toward a better future. The IRC was present in Sudan from 1981 to 2009. In November 2019, the IRC re-registered in Sudan and opened a main office in Khartoum, with programming beginning in 2020. The IRC expanded into non-SAF-controlled regions of Darfur and South Kordofan in 2024. It is currently operational in Al Jazeera, White Nile, Gedaref, River Nile, Blue Nile, South Kordofan, West Darfur, Central Darfur, and North Darfur states, including a satellite office in Tunaydbah (Gedaref). The IRC's impact groups are vulnerable individuals impacted by conflict and crisis, including women, children, the elderly, persons with disabilities, refugees, mixed populations, and host communities. Since the outbreak of war in April 2023 between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), the country has spiraled into relentless violence, institutional collapse, and mass displacement. Despite multiple ceasefire announcements, violence has continued for nearly two and a half years, displacing over 12 million people across all 18 states. Sudan is facing one of the most complex and devastating humanitarian crises in the world today. More than 30 million people now require humanitarian assistance, and around 25 million people face acute food insecurity, including 770,000 children suffering from severe acute malnutrition. Damage to infrastructure, supply shortages, and restricted humanitarian access continue to severely hinder the humanitarian response. In response to increasing needs, the IRC has scaled up its humanitarian efforts despite immense challenges. The IRC supports Sudanese communities, within the country and across national borders. The project is expected to run for the duration of the World Bank-financed award (exact start date and duration to be confirmed on award). Project Director Scope of Work The IRC is seeking a Project Director for an upcoming World Bank-funded health project in Sudan. The project is intended to restore access to a basic package of health and nutrition services and preserve the main elements of essential public health functions in Sudan. The project is expected to run from February 2027 for 3 years. This position is open to expatriates. The Project Director provides overall strategic, technical, managerial, and fiduciary leadership for the IRC's implementation of the project and is the primary accountability holder for delivery against the project's development objective, results framework, and all World Bank fiduciary and environmental/social safeguard requirements. The Project Director serves as the IRC's principal representative to the Ministry of Health PMU and the World Bank task team, reporting to the IRC Sudan Country Director. The postholder provides overall leadership, management, and coordination across all project components, ensuring alignment with the annual workplan and budget agreed with the World Bank. title: Senior Global Digital Campaigner
description: Senior Global Digital Campaigner Engagement - United Kingdom (Remote) 350 is looking for a highly skilled digital campaigns expert who will work on global campaigns in addition to national and regional digital engagement for 350 supporters in the UK and Europe. This is a full-time role, which can be done remotely from anywhere in Europe, with a preference for being based in the UK. About 350 350’s mission is to keep carbon in our atmosphere to a safe level, below 350 parts per million. We do this by mobilizing ordinary people to campaign for universal access to clean energy and an end to fossil fuels. Our campaigns are rooted in local organising, so that while achieving measurable reductions in fossil fuel emissions, we also build the power and potential of the climate movement for yet more impact to come. The values that guide and drive our work are listed here. 350 is an equal opportunity employer. 350 strives to be an inclusive and collaborative group of people who bring a variety of approaches to our work. We’re committed to the principles of justice, and we try to build a safe workplace where everyone is treated fairly and enjoys working together. We value new perspectives, ideas of all sorts, and different ways of working. Diverse perspectives and experiences improve how 350 carries out our work – including what we decide to work on and how creatively/effectively we do it. We do our best to make staff positions accessible to all potential team members, regardless of race, national origin, ethnicity, age, disability, assigned gender, gender expression or identity, sexual orientation or identity, religion or creed, veteran status, marital or parental status, and genetic information. We also strive to include team members in communities most impacted by climate change or impacted by other kinds of environmental, social, and economic injustice. About the Senior Global Digital Campaigner: The Senior Global Digital Campaigner will work closely with global and national teams to drive bold, effective multi-platform international digital campaigns, including Europe / UK, to grow, engage and inspire our network of followers and supporters. They will use digital tools and platforms, community engagement tactics, and data to create online supporter journeys and content to help recruit and inspire people to take action for the climate. They will lead the development and rollout of online campaigns and longer-term projects to phase out fossil fuels and scale up the transition to 100% renewable energy that is affordable for everyone. The role-holder should be someone who has a deep commitment to furthering intersectional climate justice and the aims of 350.org, is comfortable making decisions based on data, has an affinity for online tools and technology, and can write creative content that inspires people to take action. This is a highly collaborative role, with often-changing priorities and requiring both flexibility and good time and workload management. Key Result Areas: Digital Campaigns: Lead the development and rollout of online campaigns and longer-term digital engagement projects for global audiences, including UK and European English speakers. Supporter and Income Growth: Reverse supporter decline and increase supporter engagement through data-led engagement pathways with a focus on our UK and Europe supporter lists while also supporting national teams in the same time zone; Brand Visibility & Narrative: In collaboration with the global communications team, contribute to the development of disruptive communications strategies to regain cut-through in a fast-changing information environment. Technology & Data: Support the Digital Engagement and Technology Director in ensuring the adoption of innovative tools and methods that grow, activate, and absorb more supporters. Culture & Values: Support an inclusive, agile, collaborative and results-driven culture in the global engagement team. Duties and Responsibilities: Develop and implement inspiring and integrated global digital campaigns and supporter engagement strategies in support of our global strategy, including the UK and the rest of Europe. Lead on long-term projects and campaigns to ensure supporter engagement and impact. Coordinate the creation and dissemination of digital campaigning and engagement content (websites, email, online actions, videos, social and multimedia content) for assigned projects and mobilisations. Identify opportunities and lead planning and implementation of global rapid-response online campaigns around a variety of targets that meet our goals of growing and empowering the global climate movement, including supporting bottom-up, user-generated campaigns. Provide guidance for and mentoring digital engagement specialists on country teams (in the same time zone region). Contribute to driving a data-informed approach that incorporates testing, analysis and reflection to drive towards a steady increase in online reach, traffic and new audiences; Contribute to the training and digital empowerment of 350’s staff in digital campaigning and organising skills and tools. Engage in initiatives that foster team collaboration, including meetings, trainings and special projects. Other duties as assigned Required qualifications: A minimum of 5 years running multi-country integrated digital campaigns and organising strategy in a global context with a proven track record of successful digital engagement strategies and campaigns. A track record of digital supporter engagement in the UK or experience working on UK campaigns relating to climate and energy issues. Experience developing supporter engagement strategies and journeys, or experience in digital organising and mobilisations. Knowledge of and ease in using digital campaigning or organising software, such as mass mailers, CRMs, databases, and campaigning tools. Ability to explain complex ideas in a simple and easy-to-understand way, and outstanding content writing skills. Flexibility, ability to work independently, and good collaboration with others in a distributed, multicultural team, where work happens online and across different time zones. Self-awareness and commitment to anti-oppression and the principles of justice, equity, diversity and inclusion. At least a basic knowledge of climate change issues and a dedication to support and strengthen the climate movement in Europe. Interest and experience with data, analytics, AB testing and optimisation. Experience in online ads and marketing. Fluency in English; fluency in other European languages a plus Desired but not required skills and experiences: A track record of supporter engagement in an international setting or with other European countries in addition to the UK. Familiarity with the digital tools used by 350.org (ActionKit, NewMode, ControlShiftLabs, Wagtail, Slack, Instagram, Canva, Trello). Technical knowledge of HTML, CSS, WordPress and SQL, or demonstrated ability to pick up similar skills quickly. Experience at the intersection of online and offline organising, mobilisations, and direct action. Experience in social media engagement strategies and managing social media channels. Experience working in a multilingual context, especially with managing a multilingual digital presence. Work Environment: This role is home-based, although the role-holder is expected to participate in external meetings, events and campaign activities. Ability to maintain a healthy work/life balance in fast-paced, high-pressure working environments. We are looking for someone comfortable working both independently and in teams, highly responsive, and able to lead initiatives as well as take direction from others. We value team members who: Take initiative and are accountable for their work. Communicate effectively and respectfully. Collaborate well with others and contribute to a positive team environment. Adapt quickly to change and are eager to learn. Uphold professionalism, integrity, and ethical standards. Travel: May occasionally travel from time to time (domestic and international) Position Type: Full Time (36hrs per week). Application Deadline: Although we hope to begin interviews during the first week of September, this job is open until filled, or the hiring manager determines that they can no longer accept applications. Start Date: October 1st, 2026 (flexible) Compensation: Salary tier 2.3 - GBP 60,000 annually (UK) Benefits: In addition to a fully remote, 36-hour work week and two all-staff breaks per year, we offer a suite of comprehensive benefits - details depend on the location of the role, but we generally aim for employees to receive high-quality health insurance and retirement planning benefits in their respective location. Location: Remote within Europe (UK preferred). Current countries in Europe where 350 employs staff: France, Germany, Italy, Netherlands, and the UK. Applicants must have the legal authorization to work for any employer in their country of residence. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa at this time. If you have suggestions for us on how to do this better, we really value your input and strongly encourage you to write to us at jobs@350.org with the subject line ‘Hiring Feedback’. Job Specific Context Launched in 2020, the Global Fund for Coral Reefs (GFCR) was established as a coalition to mobilize new sources of public and private finance to safeguard the world’s most climate-resilient coral reefs—coral refugia—and prevent their collapse. The GFCR mission is to enhance the resilience of coral reef ecosystems, communities and economies by unlocking new public and private resources that accelerate sustainable businesses and finance solutions (reef-positive solutions). GFCR applies a blended finance approach that sequences different forms of capital to support coral reef conservation, economic, and community resilience outcomes. The approach combines grant funding, technical assistance, concessional finance, risk-sharing structures, and private investment to address constraints from early pipeline development through scale. At later stages, commercial and near-commercial capital can support expansion of proven reef-positive enterprises and larger-scale investment opportunities. The GFCR supports reef-positive businesses and financial solutions across four core investment pathways: Sustainable Ocean Production; Sustainable Coastal Development; Circular Economy and Pollution Management; and Financial Mechanisms. description: Regional Environmental and Social Safeguard Coordinator Organization: Wildlife Conservation Society Closing date: 14 Sep 2026 Position: Regional Environmental and Social Safeguards Coordinator Location: Kigali, Rwanda with travel around the region Reports To: Technical Director of Rights and Communities Collaborators: Regional Community Conservation Coordinator, other regional technical and program teams Start date: Immediate Duration: Full-time Background The Wildlife Conservation Society is an international NGO headquartered at Bronx Zoo in New York City, USA, working to save wildlife and wildlands and to meet global challenges in over 60 countries in Africa, Asia, the Americas and the world’s oceans. WCS believes that conservation of nature and natural resources is essential to life on earth, the future of humanity, and the wellbeing and cultural identities of Indigenous Peoples and traditional and local communities. Program Overview The Central Africa and Gulf of Guinea program is one of the largest of WCS’s 13 Global Regional Programs, spanning Democratic Republic of Congo, Republic of Congo, and Gabon. This is a rapidly growing program with a diverse and expanding portfolio of donors, partners, and projects. The region presents a set of complex conservation challenges to biodiversity and their habitats and WCS country programs are addressing these through a number of initiatives including protected area management, community engagement, sustainable livelihoods, policy reform and sustainable financing. WCS recently formally established its regional hub in Kigali, Rwanda which hosts a growing team of technical specialists and regional management to support our country programs and field offices. Purpose The purpose of the Regional Environmental & Social Safeguards Coordinator is to support WCS Central Africa and Gulf of Guinea regional, country, and site teams in the practical application of WCS’s Environmental and Social Safeguarding Framework and related policies. The coordinator will help teams identify, assess, and address environmental and social risks in ways that are technically sound, responsive to field realities, and consistent with WCS and donor standards. This is a hands-on advisory and problem-solving role, not solely a compliance function. The coordinator will be expected to engage directly with country and site teams, critically assess how safeguards are functioning in practice, identify emerging risks or implementation weaknesses, and proactively develop practical solutions. Attention will be given to human rights, the rights of Indigenous Peoples and local communities, land and natural resource use, law enforcement, stakeholder engagement, grievance mechanisms, and Free, Prior and Informed Consent (FPIC). The position will also take a proactive lead in reviewing donor requirements and developing appropriate safeguard instruments and materials. The coordinator will report to the Technical Director of Rights & Communities for Central Africa and work closely with the Regional Community Conservation Coordinator, country and site teams, program development staff, the Africa Protected Areas Management Unit (APAMU) and the WCS Global Rights + Communities team. Key Responsibilities Regional Safeguards Support • Provide support and guidance on the implementation of environmental and social safeguards procedures and initiatives at the country program and site levels throughout the region which align with WCS global and international standards • Review, outline and monitor various donor requirements (e.g. EU, KfW, GCF, GEF, etc.) and lead or support development of materials, risk assessments, etc. in response to donor requirements including those implemented with government, civil society, and UN agencies. • Provide direct support to country directors, site directors, and program managers in maintaining current environmental and safeguards protocols and rolling out the implementation of new protocols, procedures, and mechanisms as necessary • Promote and support the adherence and implementation of WCS’s global environmental and social safeguards policies at the national and site level, with a strong emphasis on a rights-based approach and gender equality and social inclusion (GESI) • Work directly with country and site teams to understand operational realities and translate safeguard policies and donor requirements into practical, context-appropriate measures that can be implemented and monitored at the site level. • In coordination with R+C regional staff, proactively identify emerging environmental and social risks, implementation weaknesses, or unintended consequences of conservation activities and work with relevant teams to develop feasible and timely solutions. • In coordination with R+C regional staff, apply critical judgment when reviewing safeguard instruments and project implementation, going beyond procedural compliance to assess whether proposed measures are appropriate, effective, and responsive to the rights and concerns of affected people. • In coordination with R+C regional staff, provide practical advice on complex issues at the intersection of conservation, human rights, community rights, natural resource use, security, and law enforcement. Safeguards Implementation • Conduct or support environmental and social risk and impact assessments, working closely with project teams and affected rights-holders to understand the local context, identify both direct and indirect risks, and develop practical mitigation and monitoring measures (in coordination with ongoing monitoring efforts). • In coordination with R+C regional staff, provide technical guidance on the rights of Indigenous Peoples and other potentially marginalized groups, including culturally appropriate engagement, FPIC, land and natural resource rights, participation in decision-making, and measures to prevent exclusion or adverse impacts. • Support teams to identify and address human rights risks associated with conservation activities, including protected-area management, access and use restrictions, law enforcement, community engagement, livelihood activities, and benefit-sharing in coordination with the R+C regional team. • Support the design, implementation, and continuous improvement of accessible and trusted grievance redress mechanisms, including analysis of grievance data to identify recurring or systemic problems and recommend corrective action. • Provide guidance to field teams on FPIC and other participatory decision-making processes, helping teams determine when FPIC is required and supporting processes that are meaningful, culturally appropriate, properly documented, and reflected in project decisions in coordination with the R+C regional team. • Support timely and appropriate responses to safeguard incidents and allegations, including initial risk analysis, documentation, coordination with relevant teams, corrective action planning, and follow-up. Safeguards Reporting and Compliance • Support the country program and site teams to ensure all projects and programs align with WCS and donor environmental and social safeguards standards • Oversee the completion and monitoring of environmental and social safeguards frameworks (e.g. ESSF/ESIA/EMMP) across all sites; • Develop and maintain a regional database that tracks all impact assessments, E&S risk and mitigation plans, reports, and reviews; • Monitor not only the completion of safeguard instruments and mitigation measures, but also whether they are being implemented effectively and are producing the intended results for affected people; • Critically review project proposals, risk assessments, management plans, and donor deliverables to identify gaps, inconsistencies, unrealistic assumptions, and potential unintended impacts, and recommend practical improvements; • Analyze safeguard, grievance, and incident data to identify trends and systemic issues requiring management attention or changes in program implementation. Capacity building • Lead on capacity building for staff and partners to build knowledge and skills on environmental and social safeguards • Disseminate lessons learned and best practices from the safeguard’s implementation throughout the region and other regions or departments (e.g. APAMU), as relevant • Design training modules and train field teams based upon a gap analysis of existing tools and capacity gaps, including addressing donor specific requirements. • Track and document E&S training for country programs and sites to ensure staff have up-to-date safeguards training. description: Budget and Reporting Coordinator Organization: International Rescue Committee Closing date: September 24, 2026 CONTEXT The International Rescue Committee (IRC) is a non-partisan, non-profit, and non-religious humanitarian organization that assists refugees worldwide. The IRC implements programs aimed at promoting sustainable solutions for displaced persons, refugees, and host communities through public health, sanitation, shelter, rehabilitation, and education projects. The IRC has been working with refugees since 1933 and operates in 40 countries across Europe, Africa, Asia, and the United States, where it provides resettlement assistance. The IRC is committed to freedom, human dignity, and self-reliance. This commitment is reflected in its high-quality resettlement assistance, comprehensive emergency relief, rehabilitation, and advocacy for refugees. The IRC began operations in Chad in 2004 to respond to the humanitarian crisis caused by the influx of refugees from Darfur into eastern Chad, with an intervention in the Oure Cassoni refugee camp. Assistance to Sudanese refugees has now expanded to include the management of ten camps in the east and one in the west, providing support to refugees and local communities in the areas of health, nutrition, and water, hygiene, and sanitation. In 2012, to address drought and food insecurity, the IRC expanded its geographic coverage in the Guéra region. The IRC currently works in three health districts—Mongo, Mangalmé, and Melfi—and provides malnutrition prevention and treatment services to the local population. In May 2016, the IRC opened an office in the Lake region to respond to the Boko Haram crisis. The IRC implements assistance projects in the areas of health, nutrition, protection, and response to gender-based violence. IRC Chad, in its 2025-2030 strategic action plan, is committed to continuing to provide essential humanitarian services in health, nutrition, and protection/GBV, while improving the economic well-being and strengthening the resilience of beneficiaries, particularly women and girls. IRC Chad will continue to work closely with and support government actors and relevant ministries in key areas to ensure that IRC activities are integrated into national policies, thereby fostering greater ownership of the actions undertaken. description: Type of contract: Consultant Contract. Level 2 - Middle. Hiring Unit: Education Sector (ED). Duty Station: Maldives. Work location: Remote. Duration of contract: 6 months. OVERVIEW: CSESI was launched in early 2023 by the Global Partnership for Education (GPE) in partnership with Save the Children, UNESCO's Education for Sustainable Development (ESD) Section and UNESCO-IIEP. The initiative is implemented in 35 countries and seeks to mainstream climate change adaptation and environmental sustainability into education sector plans, policies and budgets, and to enhance education ministry capacity for cross-sectoral coordination on climate- and environment-related policy and programming. OBJECTIVE: The main objective of this consultancy is to support the integration of climate change, environmental sustainability and DRR into teacher training programmes in the Maldives by: reviewing existing pre-service and in-service teacher training resources; identifying priority climate and environmental topics and learning outcomes aligned with national frameworks and UNESCO guidance; assessing teachers' and school leaders' readiness to teach climate/environment/DRR; and updating teacher training materials and developing supplementary teaching aids that promote learner-centred, inclusive and action-oriented pedagogies. The consultant will work closely with the Ministry of Education (MoE), the National Institute of Education (NIE), teacher training institutions and TRCs, supported by UNESCO and CSESI partners. SCOPE OF WORK: Step 1 - Assessment and mapping of existing pre-service and in-service teacher training curricula, modules and materials (primary to secondary levels) to identify gaps, opportunities and priority topics drawn from the Greening Curriculum Guidance and aligned with the National Curriculum Framework. Step 2 - Teacher readiness assessment via an online survey measuring knowledge (climate science and pedagogy, with emphasis on local issues such as sea-level rise, coastal erosion and extreme weather), attitudes and confidence, and practice. Step 3 - Development and updating of teacher training materials and supplementary teaching aids (lesson exemplars, facilitation notes, formative assessment tools), prioritising transformative, action-oriented, place-based, inclusive and gender-responsive pedagogies. Step 4 - Consultation, validation and finalization, supporting UNESCO, MoE and NIE in organizing validation workshops and incorporating feedback, including recommendations for institutionalization through NIE and national teacher education systems. DELIVERABLES: Assessment and Mapping Report on Teacher Training Resources; Teacher Readiness Assessment Report; Updated Teacher Training Materials and Supplementary Teaching Aids; Consultation and Validation Workshop Report. REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS: An advanced university degree (Master's or equivalent) in education, curriculum development, teacher education, pedagogy, Education for Sustainable Development (ESD), environmental education, or a related field; alternatively a Bachelor's degree with three years of relevant experience. A minimum of seven (7) years of progressive professional experience in the education sector, with demonstrated expertise in curriculum development, teacher training, teaching and learning materials (TLMs), pedagogy, and institutional capacity development. Strong knowledge of global standards and best practices in curriculum design, teacher education and TLM development, including integration of climate change, environmental sustainability and/or Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR). Proven experience designing, reviewing and revising curricula and teacher training resources, ideally in Small Island Developing States (SIDS) or similar contexts. Demonstrated experience in climate change education, ESD and/or DRR integration in education systems. Demonstrated experience working in the Maldives, including familiarity with the MoE, NIE and teacher training systems. Experience conducting capacity assessments, including survey design, data collection and analysis. Experience facilitating stakeholder consultations with government counterparts, teacher training institutions and development partners. Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English, with proficiency in Dhivehi required. The consultant is responsible for arranging their own logistics (office space, administrative support, telecommunications, travel, printing), the costs of which must be included in the lump sum proposal. Technical assets produced will be the property of UNESCO. In line with UNESCO's gender mainstreaming strategy, the contractor is expected to integrate a gender perspective in all activities. title: Director, Safeguarding and Child Protection
sectors: Social, Education, Gender, Youth, Child
description: Job description Role at a glance • Job title: Director, Safeguarding and Child Protection • Reports to: Global Director, Member Support (a member of the Senior Management Team) • Team: Double reporting line to five safeguarding staff based in our five regional offices and work supported by a volunteer team of more than 50 WOSM Consultants worldwide • Location: Kuala Lumpur Support Centre, Malaysia • Contract: Full-time role, with a three-year renewable contract • Travel: A minimum of 4 travels per year should be expected • Languages: English essential. French, Spanish or Arabic an advantage. About World Scouting: In this role you will join World Scouting, one of the world's largest and most influential youth education movements. With a presence in communities across the globe, Scouting empowers young people to develop the skills, values, and confidence they need to create positive change in their lives and the world around them. At the heart of Scouting is a powerful mission to contribute to the education of young people through a values-based approach grounded in the Scout Promise and Law, helping to build a better world where young people and volunteers can thrive and make meaningful contributions to society. Today, World Scouting is a global membership network of 176 National Scout Organizations, representing more than 60 million Scouts worldwide. Supported by over 5 million dedicated adult volunteers, our movement reaches young people in more than 1 million local Scout groups across diverse cultures and communities. What makes Scouting unique is our grassroots, youth-led approach. Through peer-to-peer learning and leadership, supported by committed adult volunteers, young people are encouraged to explore, grow, and lead. While every local Scout group adapts its activities to meet the needs of its community, all are united by a shared set of values and a common educational method that inspires personal development, active citizenship, and service to others. As an independent, global, non-profit and non-partisan organisation, World Scouting supports and strengthens the Scout Movement around the world. By fostering collaboration among National Scout Organizations, promoting shared values, and advancing the growth and development of Scouting, we enable millions of young people become leaders and changemakers in their communities and beyond. The World Scout Bureau (WSB) serves as the secretariat of World Scouting. Together with approximately 140 staff members from more than 40 countries, you will work as one global team, committed to supporting our worldwide membership from seven locations worldwide: • Belgium, Brussels (Europe Support Centre) • Egypt, Cairo (Arab Support Centre) • Kenya, Nairobi (Africa Support Centre) • Malaysia, Kuala Lumpur (Global Support Centre) • Panama, Panama City (Interamerica Support Centre) • Philippines, Makati City (Asia-Pacific Support Centre) • Switzerland, Geneva (Europe and Global Support Centre) Why this role exists now Safeguarding at World Scouting has changed shape over the past decade. What began as one strand of our work on volunteering is now a function in its own right, with its own staff, volunteers, standards, training and support. Meeting minimum safeguarding standards is today a constitutional membership requirement of World Scouting, not an aspiration. The foundations are in place, but we need to focus on what comes next. • Close gaps in compliance across the membership, ensuring that safeguarding requirements are understood, applied, and monitored more consistently. This is one of the clearest measures of success for this area of work. • Embedding Safeguarding at every level of Scouting rather than being seen as a separate exercise or additional requirement, it must be integrated into decision-making, events, education, member support, volunteer engagement, and organisational practice. • We are in an evolving landscape with new and emerging risks, particularly in online and digital spaces, requiring stronger anticipation, guidance, and organisational readiness. • We have more to learn from outside Scouting. World Scouting also has an opportunity to learn from expertise beyond the Movement, including statutory agencies, sport, other youth movements, research, and organisations with relevant safeguarding practice. This role exists to connect these priorities and lead the next phase of safeguarding development, ensuring that safeguarding is not seen as an obstacle to Scouting, but as the foundation that makes safe, positive, and high-quality Scouting possible. What you will do: 1.Set the strategy • Lead World Scouting’s safeguarding strategy: Lead the ongoing development and prioritisation of this important area and make the case for it to senior leadership and to our governing bodies. • Turn our long-term ambition, that every young person and adult in Scouting has a safe experience, into a plan with stated outcomes, timescales and measures. • Help define where the safeguarding portfolio should evolve, stop or refocus 2. Own the standards and drive compliance • Own the safeguarding standards member organisations are assessed against, and the assessment process itself. Keep both current and proportionate. • Drive measurable improvement in the number of members who meet the standards. Set the targets, and hold the organisation accountable to them. • Make sure assessments are applied consistently across all five regions and that decisions can withstand external scrutiny. • Guide and provide leadership to the volunteer panels in each region that review members’ assessments, so their judgements are consistent, evidenced and well-founded. 3. Oversee cases and event safety • Own the system by which safeguarding concerns reach World Scouting and are addressed. • Make sure cases escalated to World Scouting are handled promptly and professionally, and in a way that puts the safety and wellbeing of the person harmed first. • Oversee safeguarding procedures at our largest international events: the risk assessment, the on-site arrangements, the reporting routes available to participants, and the rules about which cases we hold centrally and which return to the national organisation. • Make sure what we learn from cases changes what we do, so that case data shapes our strategy, standards and training where appropriate. 4. Lead the team and the volunteer network • Lead the five safeguarding staff based in our regional support centres. They take professional and technical direction from you, whilst their day-to-day line manager is based in the Region. • Set objectives, standards of practice and development plans for the team, and hold a consistent bar across the team. • Lead the recruitment, induction and development of the volunteers who deliver safeguarding work, the regional panel members, and the volunteer consultants who run tailored support and deliver capacity building with member organisations. • Own the safeguarding budget, and influence member organisations to resource safeguarding properly in their own structures. 5. Build capability across the membership • Decide, in coordination with the regional support centres, what support member organisations need, based on evidence, and design the support offer accordingly. • Own the quality of our safeguarding guidance, training and resources: ensuring it is current, usable in several languages, and workable in very different legal and cultural settings. • Make sure expertise is available where it is needed. 6. Stay ahead of emerging risk • Lead our thinking on risks that are changing quickly: online grooming and abuse, image-based abuse and AI-generated material, harmful sexual behaviour between young people, and harm that happens outside the home; at camps, in scout groups, and online. • Bring in evidence and practice from outside Scouting, and translate it into something our members can act on. 7. Advise governance and represent World Scouting • Serve as subject matter expert to our Senior Management Team, to the World Scout Committee (our elected governing body) and to its subcommittees. • Report to governance bodies, partners and donors, ensuring that our governance bodies know where standards are being met, where they are not, what the trends are, and what is being done about it. • Represent World Scouting with funders, safeguarding bodies and peer organisations on the topic of safeguarding. Job requirements What we are looking for We are interested in what you have built and led, regardless of how many years it took you or which degree you hold. Our recruitment approach is competency-based, which means we look for evidence of how you apply your skills, knowledge, and experience to real challenges, as well as your openness to learning and continuous development. Safeguarding and child protection expertise. Assessed at application and interview • Strong knowledge and expertise in safeguarding and child protection, gained in practical experience in areas such as social work, education, statutory services, regulation, sport, or an international organisation. • Experience developing, strengthening, or implementing safeguarding systems, standards or policy at an organisational level. • Strong experience overseeing the handling of serious or sensitive safeguarding cases, using sound judgement to assess risks, interpret standards, advise on difficult situations, and recommend proportionate action. Working in a global matrix structure and across cultures Assessed at application and interview • Ability to work in complex organisations where decisions depend on coordination, influence, and alignment across different teams, levels, or stakeholders. • Experience leading professionals you do not directly line manage and who are based in different geographic locations. • Experience contributing to work that requires both strategic thinking and practical implementation. • Demonstrated ability to translate safeguarding standards, evidence and technical guidance into practical tools, support and implementation approaches across very different legal systems, cultures and levels of resource, and to adapt a global standard to local reality without lowering it. Leadership and Influence Assessed at application and interview • Experience providing expert technical guidance and professional direction to colleagues, volunteers, consultants, specialists, or partners who may not be directly line managed by you. • Ability to influence, guide, and support others to apply standards and improve practice, even where direct authority is limited. • Experience working collaboratively with senior stakeholders, technical experts, volunteers, or governance structures. • Ability to strengthen the connections between standards, assessment, compliance, reporting, learning, training, events and member support to improve consistency and accountability, Communication and judgement Assessed at application and interview • Fluent to written and spoken English. Working knowledge of French, Spanish or Arabic is an advantage. • Sound judgement when dealing with sensitive, complex, or ambiguous situations. • Ability to prepare clear guidance, advice, reports, or recommendations that support decision-making and action. • Ability to explain complex and sensitive issues clearly to non-specialist audiences. Useful, but not essential • Experience in a membership-based, federated or volunteer-led organisation. • Experience supporting safeguarding at large-scale events. • A relevant qualification in safeguarding, child protection, social work, law, psychology, education or a related field; or a recognised professional safeguarding certification. How we work At the World Scout Bureau, we work with a core competency framework aligned with our values. These competencies will be assessed during the recruitment process, together with the technical competencies and requirements outlined above. • Members Support. You keep building your own knowledge and skills so that the support we give members and stakeholders keeps getting better. • Focus on results. You take personal responsibility for delivering your responsibilities on time and to a high quality standard. • Flexibility and persistence. You adjust as conditions change, and you keep going when things get difficult. • Leadership and decision-making. You think clearly and creatively, and you support others motivate and commit to achieve organisational goals. • Interpersonal relations. You listen intently and handle difficult conversations diplomatically. You build strong relationships with staff, volunteers and stakeholders outside the organisation, across cultures and countries. • Collaboration work. You involve others building trust, sharing information, listening to different perspectives, and contributing actively to shared goals. • Organisational Integrity. You understand the objectives and values of the organisation, and you take responsibility for your own conduct. What expect and how to apply This is a full-time, three-year contract based at the Kuala Lumpur Support Centre in Malaysia. The role requires regular in-person engagement with teams, partners, and stakeholders, and remote employment will not be considered for this position. The remuneration package will be aligned with the seniority of the role and applicable Malaysian regulations. Full details of the salary and benefits package will be discussed during the final stages of the selection process. Relocation package is available. The standard working week is 40 hours, Monday to Friday. Given the global nature of World Scouting and the responsibilities of this role, some evening and weekend work will be required as well as frequent travels. Annual leave and public holiday entitlements will be provided in line with Malaysian law and the WSB Leave Policy. Relocation support will also be available for the successful candidate, where applicable. We know that moving into a role like this is an important decision. Throughout the process, we will aim to give you the information you need to understand the role, the working arrangements, and the package before any final decision is made. Applications must be submitted by 23:59 Kuala Lumpur time zone (GMT+8) on 30th August. Your application should include a curriculum vitae and career history, as well as contact information for up to three people who can provide references. We encourage you to use the application questions to tell us not only what you have done, but what you have built, strengthened, influenced, or helped change in practice.* *We recognise that AI tools may support your application, whether for brainstorming or structuring your thoughts, and we welcome that. However, job opportunities at the World Scout Bureau are content-driven leadership roles where original thinking and collaborative ideas are central to success. This will serve you best during both the application and interview stages. We encourage you to ensure your responses genuinely reflect your own perspectives and experiences, so we can better understand your unique voice, ideas, and approaches. The World Scout Bureau is an equal opportunity employer and strongly believes in and practices diversity, equity, and inclusion. We are committed to creating an inclusive and diverse work environment where all qualified candidates receive equal consideration in applying for job opportunities and subsequent career advancement. Our employment practices are open to everyone regardless of race, gender, disability, sexual orientation, or other protected characteristics. We believe that fostering an inclusive culture and embracing diverse perspectives strengthens innovation and growth within the World Scout Bureau. We encourage people of all backgrounds, including those from underrepresented communities, to apply for the job opportunities created and announced by the World Scout Bureau. description: Individual Consultant - Campus Africa Programme Implementation Support UNESCO's Regional Office for Eastern Africa (ROEA), based in Nairobi, implements the Campus Africa Programme, a continental initiative aimed at transforming higher education across Africa to drive inclusive development, innovation, and regional integration. In Eastern Africa, the Programme focuses on four interconnected pillars: enhancing research capacity through networking and partnerships; improving relevance through links to employers and skills development; building robust quality assurance systems and fair recognition of qualifications; and strengthening institutional governance and leadership. Over the 2026-2027 biennium, UNESCO ROEA has prioritised activities spanning gender-responsive research in applied STEM, AI integration in higher education (including support to the East African Alliance for Digital Skills and AI Research and Innovation, AI for EAC), social entrepreneurship for student innovators, and recognition of qualifications under the Addis Ababa Convention. description: The European Stability Mechanism (ESM) is looking for candidates pursuing, or recently graduated from, a master's or PhD programme to assist the Financial Sector and Market Analysis division within the Chief Economist's department. The Financial Sector and Market Analysis division plays a key role in the design and implementation of analytical tools that support the ESM's mandate. The team provides financial stability risk analysis at both euro area and country level, as well as technical advice on regulatory and policy matters related to the euro area financial sector and its member states. It monitors financial sector developments and market activity of both bank and non-bank financial institutions, along with related indicators. It also supports country monitoring with financial sector analysis and assists other divisions in responding to financial assistance requests by assessing potential financing needs and sectoral weaknesses relevant to conditionality setting. Purpose of the traineeship: This role provides the opportunity to acquire practical experience and knowledge of the day-to-day work of the different business areas within a multilingual and multicultural environment. Working closely with experienced professionals, you will gain hands-on experience and develop skills in applied economic analysis, data analysis, and modelling. You will be assigned to ongoing analytical projects, including a novel workstream to deepen the analysis of macro-financial linkages, and will support the team in collecting, cleaning, and analysing data. Key accountabilities: - Assist in compiling, managing, and analysing large macro- and microeconomic datasets. - Code to extract, transform, and load data from various data sources. - Support in conducting econometric analysis. - Assist in presenting findings in internal notes, presentations, or seminars. Education and experience: Candidate for or recent graduate (under one year since graduation) holding a master's degree in data science, statistics, finance, economics, or a related field. PhD students must be within a year or two of completing a PhD and hold active student status in those fields. Fluency in English, both oral and written, is required. Applicants should demonstrate good understanding and ability to apply: panel data econometrics; Python for data acquisition, transformation, and analysis, including accessing data from external databases and APIs; statistical/econometric modelling packages such as Python, R, Stata, for model estimation, hypothesis testing, and visualisation; Power BI and dashboard design principles. Key competencies: strong analytical and technical skills; excellent written and verbal communication; flexibility and results-orientated approach; intellectual curiosity and eagerness to learn; problem-solving skills and creativity; positive team spirit and adaptability; proactive attitude and self-organisation. Practical information: Expected start date as soon as possible; expected duration at least six months, renewable once for up to another six months; competitive allowance granted; place of the traineeship is Luxembourg, with the possibility to work remotely usually up to two days a week from Luxembourg and the border region (or from further away under certain conditions). Job identification: 370. Posting date: 27 July 2026.

title: Research Assistant
description: Research Assistant - Market Shaping Accelerator The Center for Global Development (CGD) is an independent, non-partisan, non-profit policy research organization in Washington, DC, and London, UK that focuses on the issues and institutions critical to inclusive development. Through rigorous empirical research and active engagement with the global policy community, CGD focuses on the intersections between the policy and financial priorities of low- and middle-income countries and the governments, institutions, and corporations that can be partners in delivering greater progress. Founded by Rachel Glennerster, Michael Kremer and Christopher Snyder, the Market Shaping Accelerator (MSA), housed at CGD, aims to catalyze the development of advance market commitments and other market shaping mechanisms to incentivize innovations addressing pressing global challenges including global health, pandemic preparedness, climate, AI safety, and drug repurposing. MSA is hiring a Research Assistant based in Washington D.C. The Research Assistant will work with Professor Christopher Snyder of Dartmouth, Professor Rachel Glennerster of the University of Chicago and CGD, and other MSA colleagues to support the development and adoption of high-impact market-shaping proposals designed to incentivize innovations addressing climate change, pandemic threats, global health challenges, and other pressing global problems. The position offers excellent preparation for graduate study or a future policy career. Responsibilities: Economic appraisal and quantitative modeling of market-shaping proposals (40%), including benefit-cost and cost-effectiveness analysis, estimating potential benefits of innovation, market size and cost of market shaping incentives, microeconomic modeling, and data analysis in Stata, R, Python and/or MATLAB; policy and sector analysis related to climate change, global health and pandemic preparedness (25%), including writing and revising drafts for policymakers and economists and analysis of market dynamics, structure, regulatory environment and implementation challenges; desk research to identify promising candidate problems for market-shaping interventions (25%); communication and coordination with stakeholders (10%). Required qualifications: Bachelor's degree in economics or a related field including coursework in intermediate microeconomics and multivariable calculus or equivalent; strong quantitative skills and experience with empirical research methods and/or microeconomic modeling; programming experience in at least one relevant language such as Stata, R, Python or MATLAB; excellent analytical and critical-thinking skills; strong written and oral communication skills; ability to manage multiple projects in a fast-moving research environment. Preferred: advanced quantitative preparation (linear algebra, probability, statistics and econometrics, real analysis, ordinary differential equations, advanced microeconomics); demonstrated interest in climate change, pandemic preparedness, global health or related policy areas. Some domestic and possibly international travel may be required. Salary range: $54,500 - $60,000. Hybrid environment with staff required to be in the office at least three days per week; CGD is registered to employ staff living in DC, Maryland and Virginia and is unable to sponsor work authorization for this position. Closing date: 2026-11-19 HOW TO APPLY: Apply online via the CGD application portal. Application documents required: Resume/CV, Cover Letter, Writing Sample (ideally an independently written quantitative paper), Unofficial Transcripts, and contact information for 3 professional references. Closing date: October 15 at 11:59 pm ET. There may be an additional hiring round in early 2027. https://centerforglobaldevelopment.applytojob.com/apply/gS6SSb6wjR/Research-Assistant-Market-Shaping-Accelerator

GFI Asia Pacific (GFI APAC) collaborates with scientists, corporates, and policymakers to make plant-based, fermentation-enabled, and cultivated meat delicious, affordable, and accessible. GFI is currently establishing GFI Korea as a focus country office; until it is formalized, initiatives may run under the GFI APAC brand, and this role is one of the first hires building the team on the ground. The Corporate Engagement Lead will drive growth in Korea's biomanufacturing and alternative protein ecosystem, partnering with conglomerates, VCs, and startups to build a sustainable food system. You will lead GFI's private-sector strategy in Korea, working with business leaders and investors to overcome market barriers, implement impactful initiatives, and exchange best practices globally, including securing public funding for commercial scale-up infrastructure. As a senior leader in an entrepreneurial nonprofit you will set the strategic direction of the industry workstream in Korea with significant autonomy. Key responsibilities: identify systemic alternative protein scale-up barriers across ingredients, manufacturing, infrastructure, supply chains, investment, commercialization, and consumer access; determine priority interventions for the Korean ecosystem using market insights, industry data, and stakeholder input; develop initiatives and mobilize resources and partnerships to improve the taste, price, and accessibility of alternative proteins; work with the Policy Specialist to turn industry needs into policy recommendations and a multi-year strategy to unlock government funding; establish GFI Korea as a credible, evidence-based partner and build relationships across food-tech, biotech, and AP value chains with conglomerates, suppliers, CDMOs, investors, accelerators, and startups; represent GFI Korea at industry events, forums, and in the media; track industry and investment landscape developments and report into GFI platforms; collaborate with GFI APAC's Head of Corporate Engagement and global teams; and support programmatic budgeting and corporate engagement spending with the Operations Manager. title: Willow Tit Research Officer
description: Durham Wildlife Trust | Rainton Meadows, Houghton-le-Spring | £30,633.00 per annum pro rata | Full time, fixed term 3 months (extension possible) Join the national fight to save one of Britain's fastest-declining birds. Durham Wildlife Trust is seeking a Willow Tit Research Officer to lead the North East's contribution to a major new Natural England and RSPB-led species recovery programme, spanning Cheshire, Lancashire, the West Midlands, Derbyshire, Cornwall and County Durham. The Willow Tit has declined by 96% since 1975. The Willow Tit Research Officer will set up and deliver autumn population monitoring across sites in Tyne & Wear and County Durham, using mist netting and colour-ringing to gather standardised data on survival, breeding productivity and juvenile numbers — evidence that will shape a national recovery plan. You'll need a BTO ringing licence at C level or above (with passerine mist net endorsement), strong record-keeping skills, and the flexibility for some early morning, evening and weekend work. Experience with Willow Tit or similar woodland/scrub species, volunteer supervision and GIS tools would all be an advantage. This is a rare opportunity to play a hands-on role in a genuinely national, landscape-scale conservation effort, working closely with Durham Wildlife Trust's Ecology Manager, Community Ecologist and volunteers. Location: Rainton Meadows Nature Reserve, Houghton-le-Spring, DH4 6PU. Closing date: Friday 28 August 2026 HOW TO APPLY: To apply, complete the application form (available on the job page) and submit it with a personal statement (max 2 sides of A4) to jobs@durhamwt.co.uk, subject line "Willow Tit Research Officer". CVs and covering letters will not be accepted. Closing date: 5pm, 28 August 2026. Interviews: Friday 4 September 2026, at Rainton Meadows Nature Reserve. For an informal discussion, contact Mark Dinning, Ecology Manager: mdinning@durhamwt.co.uk / 0191 584 3112. https://www.durhamwt.com/jobs/willow-tit-research-officer

title: Faculty Position in Mathematics of Learning
description: The School of Basic Sciences at EPFL invites applications for a faculty position in Mathematics of Learning. The appointment will be at the Tenure Track level, with an expected start date in fall 2027. We seek outstanding candidates with a research agenda focused on the mathematical foundations of learning and artificial intelligence. Indicative areas include, but are not limited to, theoretical performance guarantees, learning dynamics and generative modelling, sampling and transport methods, statistical foundations, and uncertainty quantification. The candidate should demonstrate the potential to become a leading researcher in their field and is expected to establish an independent, internationally competitive research program. The successful candidate will supervise PhD students, engage with researchers in related fields across the EPFL campus, and show a strong commitment to excellence in undergraduate and graduate teaching. EPFL, with its main campus located in Lausanne, Switzerland, on the shores of Lake Geneva, is an international, dynamically growing and well-funded institution fostering excellence and diversity. The EPFL environment is multi-lingual and multi-cultural. As a technical university spanning a broad range of disciplines in engineering and science, EPFL offers an attractive environment for multidisciplinary research collaboration. The mathematical environment at EPFL is strengthened by the Bernoulli Centre for Fundamental Studies, its world-class faculty, and outstanding facilities. EPFL is an equal opportunity employer and family-friendly university. It is committed to increasing the diversity of its faculty. It strongly encourages women to apply. Application deadline: 1 November, 2026 HOW TO APPLY: Applications should include a cover letter, a CV with a list of publications, a concise statement of research (maximum three pages), a statement of teaching interests (one page), and the names and contact of three to five references who are ready to supply a letter upon request. Applications should be uploaded to the EPFL recruitment page: https://facultyrecruiting.epfl.ch/position/65044491. Application deadline: 1 November, 2026. Inquiries can be addressed to Prof. Maryna Viazovska, Director of the Institute of Mathematics, Chair of the Search Committee, e-mail: math2026@epfl.ch

INSO fournit aux ONG enregistrées une gamme de services gratuits, notamment le suivi des incidents en temps réel, des analyses contextuelles, des données et cartographies liées à la sécurité, un appui à la gestion de crise, ainsi que des sessions d'orientation et de formation pour le personnel. Ouvert à la demande des ONG, le programme d'INSO en Haïti a vocation à répondre aux contraintes d'accès résultant des cycles récurrents de catastrophes naturelles, d'instabilité politique et de criminalité violente rencontrées par les ONG humanitaires et de développement. Objectif général du rôle : le (la) titulaire est chargé(e) de fournir un appui administratif efficace et efficient en matière de ressources humaines aux opérations du Bureau de pays de l'INSO, sous la supervision du Country Administration Manager (CAM). Le poste fait partie de l'équipe des Opérations. Principales tâches et responsabilités — Conformité : s'assurer que les politiques et procédures RH d'INSO sont conformes aux lois et réglementations locales du travail ; suivre les périodes d'essai et dates d'expiration des contrats ; maintenir la communication avec les autorités locales (bureau des impôts, ministère du Travail) ; veiller à ce que le personnel entrant/sortant dispose des documents appropriés (visa, carte INSO, permis de travail, enregistrement des expatriés). title: International Consultant - Conservation and Management Manual for Cambodian Memorial Sites

description: Type of contract: Consultant Contract. Level 3 – Senior. Hiring Unit: Culture Sector (CLT). Duty Station: Phnom Penh (work location: remote).
