OVERVIEW: The UNESCO Office in Phnom Penh is implementing the "Peace Education, Archives Preservation and Digitalization, and Site Conservation for Youth Empowerment (PEACE)" Project in Cambodia with support from KOICA for 2024–2028. The project supports preservation of archives and sites linked to the memory of the Khmer Rouge regime (1975–1979). In 2025 the World Heritage Committee inscribed "Cambodian Memorial Sites: From centres of repression to places of peace and reflection" — comprising the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum, the Choeung Ek Genocidal Centre and the former M-13 prison site — on the World Heritage List, recommending improved standards of material conservation and storage of artefacts, documents and objects, including human remains. OBJECTIVE: Develop a practical Conservation and Management Manual giving theoretical and operational guidance for the handling, documentation, conservation and storage of human remains and other artefacts held or to be discovered at the Cambodian Memorial Sites, and strengthen institutional capacity through training workshops. ASSIGNMENTS: Under the overall authority of the UNESCO Representative to Cambodia and direct supervision of the Culture Programme Specialist, and with the support of a national consultant, the international expert will: (A) develop the manual, covering international best practices and legal/institutional frameworks, ethical principles for treatment of human remains and artefacts, documentation and recording procedures, field recovery and first aid for newly exposed remains and artefacts, environmental management and preventive conservation, storage requirements and facility management (textiles, clothing, metals), risk management and monitoring, templates and forms, and long-term conservation planning; (B) undertake two field missions to Cambodia (fact-finding/consultation, 10–15 days; training delivery and manual presentation, 6 days); (C) design and deliver two capacity-building workshops of 20–30 participants each, plus reusable training materials. DELIVERABLES: draft outline (Month 2), draft manual of 50–60 pages (Month 4), final manual in English after peer review by a Cambodian expert (Month 6), two workshops and final activity report (Month 8). The Senior Accountant will have particular responsibility for multi-entity consolidation, intercompany accounting, foreign currency considerations, nonprofit accounting, and general ledger management. The role will establish consistent accounting treatment across Global Citizen entities while ensuring compliance with U.S. GAAP and applicable nonprofit accounting standards. While Accounts Payable and Payroll are executed by designated staff, the Senior Accountant maintains accounting oversight of these processes and ensures their accurate integration into the general ledger and financial reporting. Key Responsibilities Global Consolidation & Financial Reporting — 35% • Own the monthly, quarterly, and annual consolidation of Global Citizen’s domestic and international entities. • Prepare consolidated financial statements and supporting schedules, ensuring completeness, accuracy, and consistency across entities. • Own intercompany accounting, including reconciliation of intercompany balances and transactions and preparation of consolidation and elimination entries. • Manage multi-currency accounting and foreign currency translation considerations across international entities. • Review entity-level financial information and identify and resolve inconsistencies before consolidation. • Establish and maintain standardized accounting treatments, reporting packages, chart-of-account conventions, and close procedures across entities. • Partner directly with international finance and accounting contacts to resolve accounting issues and ensure timely and accurate submissions. • Analyze consolidated results and provide clear explanations of material balances, movements, and accounting matters to Finance leadership. General Ledger, Nonprofit Accounting & Close — 35% • Own the general ledger and personally drive the month-end and year-end close process from transaction-level accounting through final financial statements. • Prepare and review journal entries, account reconciliations, accruals, prepaid expenses, fixed assets, cash activity, allocations, and other close-related accounting. • Maintain the accuracy and integrity of the chart of accounts and ensure transactions are appropriately classified across entities, departments, programs, and funding sources. • Apply U.S. GAAP and nonprofit accounting standards to day-to-day and complex accounting matters. • Ensure appropriate accounting for net assets with and without donor restrictions, contributions, grants, functional expenses, and other nonprofit-specific transactions. • Review balance sheet accounts and supporting schedules, investigate discrepancies, and ensure reconciling items are resolved promptly. • Develop and document accounting positions for complex or non-routine transactions. • Maintain disciplined close schedules, account ownership, supporting documentation, and reconciliation standards. • Continuously improve accounting processes, policies, procedures, and internal controls with an emphasis on accuracy, scalability, and efficient execution. • Maintain strong data integrity within Sage Intacct and related financial systems. AP, Payroll & Financial Controls — 10% • Maintain accounting oversight of Accounts Payable and Payroll activities performed by designated staff. • Review payroll and AP activity as necessary to ensure complete and accurate recording in the general ledger. • Ensure appropriate reconciliations and controls exist over cash disbursements, payroll, vendor activity, and other financial transactions. • Identify control gaps and implement practical improvements while maintaining efficient operating processes. • Ensure AP and Payroll close activities are completed in accordance with reporting deadlines. Fundamental Requirements Education & Experience • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field; CPA preferred. • 7+ years of progressive accounting experience, with significant hands-on responsibility for general ledger accounting, financial close, and financial statement preparation. • Strong nonprofit accounting experience and demonstrated knowledge of U.S. GAAP and nonprofit accounting standards. • Demonstrated experience owning accounting for a multi-entity organization, including preparation of consolidated financial statements. • Significant hands-on experience with intercompany accounting, consolidation entries, eliminations, and entity-level reconciliations. • Experience working with international entities and foreign currency accounting and translation. • Demonstrated experience leading month-end and year-end close processes and working directly in the general ledger. • Experience leading external financial statement audits and supporting IRS Form 990 preparation. • Advanced Excel skills, including the ability to work efficiently with large and complex financial datasets. • Strong proficiency with accounting and ERP systems; Sage Intacct experience strongly preferred. Attributes • A hands-on accountant who is equally comfortable analyzing consolidated financial statements and investigating the underlying journal entry or reconciliation. • Deep attention to detail and a strong sense of ownership over the accuracy and completeness of financial information. • Strong technical accounting judgment and the ability to independently research and resolve accounting issues. • Highly organized, with the ability to manage a complex close calendar across multiple entities and jurisdictions. • Able to identify inconsistencies across entity-level books and work collaboratively with international colleagues to resolve them. • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with an instinct for understanding why balances changed rather than simply reporting that they changed. • Able to translate complex accounting matters into clear, concise information for Finance leadership and non-accounting stakeholders. • Comfortable operating independently in a senior individual-contributor capacity while collaborating closely across Finance and the broader organization. • Committed to building disciplined, well-documented, and scalable accounting processes. • Using AI tools to work smarter and drive impact is an essential part of every role at Global Citizen. All staff must integrate AI into their daily work, whether improving workflows, analyzing information, or enhancing communication in service of our mission. Global Citizen is a fast-moving, mission-driven organization where bold ideas, smart risks, and decisive action are part of how we create impact. We are looking for people who are energized by ambitious goals, comfortable navigating change, and ready to work collaboratively across teams, time zones, and sectors. The pace is high and the work is meaningful, making this a strong fit for people who bring initiative, adaptability, courage, and a deep commitment to driving real-world change. Benefits Why Global Citizen? In this coming decade of action and accountability, Global Citizen will be the leading international voice, educator, and influencer that rallies humanity to take full responsibility and accountability for eradicating extreme poverty. You have a chance to contribute and make this world a better place for all. description: Poste de chercheur postdoctoral (CDD 12 mois) au laboratoire ILANCE (CNRS-IN2P3 / The University of Tokyo), rattaché au Laboratoire Leprince-Ringuet (UMR 7638), basé à Tokyo (campus de Kashiwa), avec prise de fonction le 02/11/2026. Les missions : le candidat retenu sera responsable de l'application de notre algorithme de reconstruction basé sur l'apprentissage profond (CAVERNS-WatChMaL) aux données atmosphériques de Super-Kamiokande et T2K. Il réalisera la première analyse d'oscillation de Super-Kamiokande basée sur un algorithme d'apprentissage profond, avec l'objectif de surpasser les résultats obtenus avec les algorithmes traditionnels basés sur la vraisemblance. Le chercheur devra d'abord développer la robustesse de l'algorithme de reconstruction aux différences entre les données simulées d'entraînement et les données de Super-Kamiokande, puis développer la pipeline afin de tester l'algorithme sur les données atmosphériques, évaluer les incertitudes systématiques et réaliser les analyses de sensibilité et d'oscillation de neutrinos. Activités : finalisation de la chaîne complète de reconstruction d'événements et d'estimation des erreurs systématiques de Super-Kamiokande ; réduction des incertitudes systématiques via l'apprentissage automatique et les échantillons de contrôle ; test des algorithmes sur les données de calibration, d'accélérateur (T2K) et atmosphériques (SK) ; participation à l'analyse d'oscillation de Super-Kamiokande et à la construction d'Hyper-Kamiokande (site de Kamioka) ; présentation des résultats en réunions de collaboration et conférences ; publication dans des revues à comité de lecture. Le candidat aura l'opportunité de superviser plusieurs étudiants et pourra passer jusqu'à six mois par an en France au Laboratoire Leprince-Ringuet. Solides compétences en physique des neutrinos et en reconstruction d'événements exigées ; expérience significative en apprentissage automatique appréciée ; grande autonomie scientifique et goût pour l'encadrement d'étudiants. description: Endline Evaluation for I-JET in ASEAN Program Consultancy to Conduct Endline Evaluation for I-JET in ASEAN Program Location: Phnom Penh, Cambodia Oxfam in Cambodia seeks to engage an independent consultant or consulting team to undertake the Endline Evaluation of the Influencing Just Energy Transition (I-JET) Project. The assignment runs from October 2026 to March 2027, covering a total of 30 working days, and the assignment location is remote. The I-JET Project is a regional initiative funded by the Australian Government through the Australian NGO Cooperation Program (ANCP) from 1 July 2022 to 30 June 2027. It is jointly implemented by Oxfam International-Asia with the Climate Action Network Southeast Asia (CANSEA), the ASEAN Centre for Energy (ACE), Oxfam in Cambodia, Oxfam Pilipinas, Oxfam in Laos and Oxfam in Vietnam, in collaboration with civil society organisations and strategic partners. The project strengthens the capacity and leadership of CSOs, women leaders, people with disabilities and other marginalised groups to influence energy policies and promote sustainable community-owned renewable energy solutions (SCORE), working through ASEAN energy governance processes including the ASEAN Plan of Action for Energy Cooperation 2026-2030. The evaluation will determine the extent to which the project has achieved its intended outcomes against its Theory of Change in advancing a gender-responsive and socially inclusive just energy transition across ASEAN, while identifying lessons learned, good practices and evidence-based recommendations to strengthen accountability and organisational learning. Specific objectives include assessing performance against OECD-DAC criteria; determining outcome achievement in narrative change, policy influence and financing for SCORE solutions; assessing implementation strategies, partnerships, stakeholder engagement and capacity strengthening; identifying achievements, challenges and unintended outcomes; and providing recommendations to enhance sustainability. Scope covers the implementation period (1 July 2022 - 30 June 2027), regional-level interventions in ASEAN and national-level interventions in Cambodia and the Philippines (including Lao PDR and Vietnam). Key deliverables are an inception report and presentation (October 2026), data collection through KIIs, FGDs and a field visit in the Philippines (November 2026 - January 2027), a draft evaluation report and presentation (February 2027), and a final endline evaluation report (March 2027), with payments of 40%/40%/20% against approved deliverables. Requirements: the Team Lead must have a minimum of 7-10 years of experience in evaluating complex influencing and advocacy programmes, expertise in OECD-DAC criteria, mixed methods, contribution analysis, outcome harvesting and report writing, with proficiency in English. All deliverables must be produced independently and not generated by artificial intelligence systems beyond limited spell-check, grammar and transcription uses. description: The Geneva Graduate Institute, founded in 1927, is a world-renowned centre of excellence for the study of international relations and development. Located in Geneva, Switzerland, it offers a stimulating, multicultural and interdisciplinary academic environment, with masters and doctoral programmes and cutting-edge research on major global challenges. The SNSF-funded research project "Narrative Belonging: Memory Politics and NATO Enlargement in Europe", hosted by the Department of International History and Politics and the Centre on Conflict, Development and Peacebuilding (CCDP), examines how memories of the past have shaped NATO enlargement and Europe's evolving security order since the end of the Cold War. Moving beyond conventional military and strategic explanations, the project places historical experiences, collective memory, and narratives of belonging at the centre of the analysis, investigating how national memories interacted with NATO's own institutional narratives, symbolic practices, and representations of its history and identity. It focuses on successive phases of enlargement - the 1999 accession of the Visegrad countries, the 2004 enlargement involving the Vilnius Group, and the recent accessions of Finland and Sweden - combining archival research, media analysis, and oral history. Key responsibilities: lead the project's research on NATO as an institution, examining how the Alliance has articulated, represented, and commemorated its evolving identity; examine NATO's institutional narratives and symbolic practices, including commemorations, anniversaries, strategic narratives and public diplomacy; investigate how NATO's representation of its own history interacted with the memory politics of new and aspiring member states; conduct archival research, including in NATO archives in Brussels and relevant national archives; contribute to the comparative and conceptual development of the project's broader research agenda; develop high-quality single- and co-authored publications; present findings at international conferences and workshops; contribute to organising project workshops and dissemination activities; and work closely with the project's doctoral researchers, including on the project's open digital archive. Requirements: PhD in international history or a related discipline, completed by the starting date; demonstrated research expertise in areas such as NATO and transatlantic relations, Cold War or post-Cold War Europe, memory studies, international history, or European security; proven capacity to conduct research of the highest academic standards; strong archival research skills (oral history experience an asset); excellent academic writing and publication skills; ability to develop an independent research agenda while working in a collaborative international team; excellent command of spoken and written English, with additional European languages an asset. The role offers close collaboration with the Principal Investigator and doctoral researchers, and an international research environment spanning the Geneva Graduate Institute and the University of Oxford. The Institute is an equal opportunity employer committed to a safe and inclusive working environment. Contrato de consultoría por 4 meses y 6 días, con sede en Lima/Perú, modalidad remota. Objetivo general: Identificar oportunidades de mejora en los procesos de formulación y ejecución presupuestal y de abastecimiento de las intervenciones para prevenir y reducir la anemia infantil en tres Gobiernos Regionales con alta prevalencia de este problema de salud pública, y proponer recomendaciones para fortalecer estos procesos, contribuyendo al logro de resultados en la lucha contra la anemia infantil. Objetivos específicos: (1) Examinar la calidad de los procesos de formulación y ejecución presupuestal de las intervenciones del PPoR DIT a cargo de las Unidades Ejecutoras de Salud de los tres Gobiernos Regionales (Redes de Salud, Dirección Regional de Salud y Gerencia Regional de Salud), analizando la priorización del financiamiento de insumos estratégicos, la oportunidad y calidad del gasto, los niveles de ejecución y la identificación de potenciales brechas de cobertura y financiamiento. Contexto: la anemia infantil es un problema de salud pública latente en el Perú. title: Baseline Survey Consultant
description: Baseline Survey Consultant 1.Background Information: Vétérinaires Sans Frontières Germany (VSF Germany) is an International Non-Governmental Organization (INGO), providing humanitarian aid and development assistance to pastoralists and vulnerable communities in areas where livestock is of importance. VSFG supports animal health, livestock related agriculture, marketing, food safety, drought responses and mitigation, capacity development of communities and governmental institutions, peace and conflict resolution with the ultimate aim of improving food security and strengthening livelihoods and resilience of pastoralist communities. VSFG currently implements activities in Ethiopia, Kenya, Uganda, Somalia, Sudan and South Sudan with country programs coordinated from the Regional Office Nairobi. VSF-Germany has been in South Sudan since 1998 covering the States of Upper Nile, Jonglei, Warrap, Eastern Equatoria, Western Bar el Ghazal and Lakes State, supporting emergency and recovery programmes alongside communities in the said States. VSF-Germany has received grant from EU in South Sudan under EU Alliance in support of the Horn of Africa Initiative. The proposed is Kapoeta East Pastoralists' Livelihoods, Empowerment, Adaptation and Peace (LEAP) Project planned to be implemented in Kapoeta County of Eastern Equatoria State of South Sudan with the overall objective of contributing to strengthening resilience of agropastoral communities to recurring climate shocks and livelihood-induced conflicts in Kapoeta East. The proposed project has total budget of Euro 3,157,895.52 and will be implemented in two (2) Payams of Kapoeta East together with its partner, Enjojo Foundation, for the period of 30 months (June 01, 2026 – January 31, 2029). In addition, the action targets Natinga Payam which is strategically located in the cross-border area of Kapoeta East and other counties in the Eastern Equatoria state for the peace component intervention. As part of the project implementation process, VSF-Germany and its partner (Enjojo Foundation) planned to undertake project baseline survey through external consultant to collect qualitative and quantitative baseline data for each of the project indicators (see attached log-frame as annex) that will be used to monitor and evaluate the progress of the project, update the project’s monitoring and evaluation (M&E) system, and revise the project documents. Details of the baseline survey assignment is indicated below for the better understanding of the assignment. 2. Description of the Project: 2.1: Relevance and context analysis: South Sudan faces a complex and protracted humanitarian crisis rooted in historical marginalization, chronic poverty, and underdevelopment, compounded by recent shocks including climate change, conflict, and economic instability. It ranks among the top five global hunger hotspots and is one of the most climate-vulnerable countries. As of early 2026, South Sudan is experiencing extreme food insecurity, driven by ongoing conflict, widespread displacement, flooding, and economic instability. During the lean season (April to July 2026), approximately 7.55 million people (53% of the population) are projected to face Crisis or worse conditions (IPC Phase 3 or above), with around 1.3 million in Emergency (Phase 4) and tens of thousands at risk of Catastrophe (Phase 5). Climate change has intensified both droughts and floods, disrupting agriculture and pastoralism - key livelihood sectors. Vulnerable groups such as women, children, the elderly, and the disabled are disproportionately affected. Resource scarcity, especially water and pasture, fuels localized conflicts, worsened by weak governance and limited institutional capacity. Kapoeta East County, located in Eastern Equatoria State along the South Sudan - Kenya border, epitomizes the challenges of pastoralist borderlands: recurrent droughts, fragile livelihoods, and protracted insecurity. The semi-arid environment is marked by highly variable rainfall, frequent drought cycles, and progressive land degradation, which have drastically reduced pasture and water availability. Livestock - particularly cattle, goats, and sheep - form the backbone of household economies, social status, and cultural identity. However, these assets are increasingly undermined by climate shocks, disease outbreaks, and cross-border cattle raiding. The county’s estimated population of 120,000 -180,000 is predominantly pastoralist (Toposa ethnic group), with over 60% under the age of 25. Youth face limited livelihood opportunities, often resorting to cattle raiding or armed group participation. Women and vulnerable groups bear disproportionate burdens, with restricted access to resources, services, and decision-making. Weak state presence, poor infrastructure, and reliance on customary governance further exacerbate vulnerability. Cross-border insecurity with Turkana (Kenya) and Nyangatom (Ethiopia) communities perpetuates cycles of violence, while porous borders facilitate illicit arms flows and livestock theft. Despite these challenges, Kapoeta East holds significant potential for resilience-building. Livestock production, informal cross-border trade, and traditional peace institutions provide entry points for integrated interventions. To ensure effective coordination, maximize resource efficiency, and avoid the duplication of interventions across Kapoeta East, a comprehensive partner mapping highlights the strategic positioning of key stakeholders, their operational footprints, and implementation methodologies. Dan Church Aid (DCA), through the SPREAD Project, operates across the Narus, Katikor, and Lotimor Payams, utilizing an integrated peacebuilding and resilience approach that mobilizes community action groups, facilitates cross-border dialogues, and strengthens local economies through Village Savings and Loan Associations (VSLAs), livelihood support, small-scale irrigation schemes, and market linkages. Complementing these efforts, the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) deploys two distinct initiatives: the PLACE Project, active in Narus, Kauto, and Lotimor payams, which focuses heavily on environmental and livestock stewardship through rangeland restoration, livestock systems strengthening, water and natural resource governance, transhumance route mapping, value chain development, and structured cross-border coordination; and the BREFONS Project, which commands a wider footprint across the Narus, Kauto, Katodori, Jie, Mogos, and Lotimor Payams to deliver critical infrastructure and climate resilience support, including the construction of water facilities such as hafirs and boreholes, veterinary services, mass livestock vaccination campaigns, and the development of slaughterhouses and rehabilitated rangelands. Finally, the World Food Programme (WFP), working through its cooperating partner, the Organization for Peace, Relief and Development (OPRD), provides broad safety-net and agricultural coverage across the entirety of Kapoeta East, deploying an emergency lean-season response via direct cash transfers, sustaining an essential school feeding program across 26 localized institutions, and anchoring long-term resilience through the distribution of agricultural inputs, the establishment of farmer field schools, and integrated peacebuilding activities. However, coverage remains uneven, with underserved Payams such as Mogos, Jie, Katodori and Natinga/Natina facing acute gaps. The LEAP project will complement these efforts by targeting resilience, livelihood diversification, and conflict-sensitive programming in priority Payams. 2.2: Overall objective and expected outcomes of the actions: Overall Objective: To contribute to strengthening resilience of agropastoral communities to recurring climate shocks and livelihood-induced conflicts in Kapoeta. This will be achieved through enhanced production and productivity of agropastoral households; increased opportunities for diversified livelihoods, income generation, and job creation amongst agro-pastoral households, particularly for women and youth; and strengthened community-driven conflict prevention, resolutions, and disaster risks management mechanisms and services in Kapoeta East County in Eastern Equatoria State by 2029. The Action has proposed to achieve three expected outcomes: Outcome 1: Enhanced Production and Productivity of Agropastoral Households This outcome will be achieved through targeted interventions including technical training for CAHWs and establishment of a sustainable veterinary drug supply system. Awareness campaigns will promote climate-smart husbandry and One Health approaches across livestock value chains. Infrastructure for animal health services will be developed, and marketing capacity of off-takers will be enhanced. Livestock keepers will be trained in basic husbandry and fodder production, with hay and silage making promoted at household and village levels. Feedlot practices will be introduced to support small ruminant fattening, adding value and increasing income. Vulnerable households will receive small ruminants and poultry through a pass-on mechanism. Livestock marketing infrastructure, market access, and information systems will be strengthened. Advocacy and policy engagement will promote pro-pastoral development and cross-border trade. Outcome 2: Increased Opportunities for Diversified Livelihoods, Income Generation, and Job Creation Amongst Agro-pastoral Households, Particularly for Women and Youth This outcome focuses on empowering women and youth through technical and financial capacity building. Support will be provided to establish small-scale enterprises in livestock and agricultural value chains. The Action will strengthen the survival base of conflict- and disaster-affected populations by enhancing income and investment opportunities. Marketing of animals and their products will be improved through value addition, business management training, and establishment of microfinance systems. Key activities include forming VSLA groups, providing technical training via local institutions or Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) and supporting mentorship, apprenticeship, start-up capital, and market linkages. Outcome 3: Strengthened Community-driven Conflict Prevention, Resolutions, and Disaster Risks Management Mechanisms and Services This outcome will be realized through a structurally integrated, co-located geographical framework designed in partnership with the World Food Programme (WFP) to maximize operational complementarity and ensure clear institutional division of tasks. While both organizations operate within the same target territories to offer comprehensive shocks-and-stressors mitigation, WFP takes the organizational lead on Addressing Climatic Shocks and Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) interventions. Specifically, WFP drives the establishment and strengthening of community-based DRR committees, handles the formulation of institutional disaster preparedness plans, and manages the dissemination and livelihood-utilization of climate early warning systems. The action has also proposed to achieve the following outputs contributing to the achieve the above results and consultant also expected establish baseline result for the below outputs Output 1.1: Climate-smart agricultural inputs, technologies and practices provided to producer groups. This output is not part of the assignment and brought here to demonstrate the distinct logical flow of the two independent interventions under a shared EU Alliance for the Horn of Africa Initiative logical framework, Output 1.1 will be executed exclusively by the World Food Programme (WFP), in complementarity with the VSF Germany's pastoralist-focused activities. Output 1.2: Improved access to livestock health care management and extension services and water Output 1.3: Improved livestock husbandry practices adopted by agro-pastoral producers Output 2.1: Access by agro-pastoral women and youth to finance and business opportunities strengthened. Output 2.2: Women and youths’ vocational/life skills development strengthened. Output 3.1: Community-based structures for disaster management equipped with knowledge and skills. Similar to output 1.1 that this output also brought here to show synergistic Alignment and Complementarity with WFP’s Disaster Risk Reduction Framework under Outcome 3. 2.3: Implementation Approaches: The Project will be implemented for 30 months’ period employing the following methodologies • Inception Phase: The Action will use the first three months as mandatory preparatory phase for planning. • Sustainable Livestock Health Services inclusive of One Health Approach**:** Communities targeted by the project are increasingly vulnerable to the impacts of climatic variability leading recurring flood, livestock diseases build ups, and conflict adversely affecting traditional coping mechanisms; thus, pose challenges to existing pastoral and agro-pastoral livelihood strategies. To reduce these adverse effects, the communities’ local capacities on livestock health management and their traditional institutions that ultimately enable self-anticipation, preparation and early action will be built. Attention will also be directed to one health initiative ensuring a cross collaboration between the animal and human health care providers with the environment care lens. • Market System Approach: The Action aims at stimulating existing and new livelihood opportunities with the aim of income generation, job creation and livelihoods diversification to boost market-oriented production. The Action will adopt the Market Systems Development (MSD) Approach; a system that enhances and stimulate market access and shall be strengthened further by formation of a Multi-Stakeholder Platforms (MSPs) that will bring together livestock input suppliers, livestock extension service providers, business development service providers (BDS) and buyers of livestock and policy makers. The project will facilitate linkages between value chain target groups and established commodity off takers in counties, states and at national level through Public Private Partnerships to promote reliable and steady access to markets. • Credit Service Access Stimulation Initiatives**:** Facilitation of access to financial services for resource-poor pastoralists is an essential means of enabling sustainable small farm business development. Therefore, the project will establish partnership with micro-finance institution (MFI) and cooperatives and enhance the potentials of self-saving groups through VSLAs to deliver for investment and working capital purposes. • Community Driven Development (CDD): The involvement of target communities and local government partners in all the stages of project cycle management is considered important in order that the stated specific objective and expected results of this project be m b will focus on the inclusion of women and the youth in key opportunity areas which is key to ensuring equitable participation and allocation of resources to all persons in the community. • Nutrition sensitive programming: As a mainstreaming strategy, the action will integrate nutrition objectives into the pastoralist’s livelihood interventions to address the root causes of malnutrition. This approach ensures that improved food production and nutrition awareness directly and indirectly lead to better dietary diversity and health outcomes for vulnerable households. 3. Purpose of the Baseline Survey: The overall purpose of the baseline survey is to provide information on all indicators, which will be used to monitor and assess the project activities’ progress and effectiveness during implementation and after the activities are completed. The survey will enable project indicators at output and goal/outcome level to be measured and tracked. The baseline information gathered is expected to be informed by both quantitative and qualitative data at household, Key informants and community levels which ultimately will be used to determine the extent of Kapoeta-LEAP project contribution to strengthening resilience of agropastoral communities to recurring climate shocks and livelihood-induced conflicts in Kapoeta East County. Specifically, the objectives of the baseline survey are: • To assess the project’s theory of change (TOC), identify, & clarify the priority needs of the communities within the context of the project location. • To develop baseline indicators for the entire indicator in the project Result Frame (RF) at impact, Outcome and Output level. The baseline Results for all the indicators in the Result Frame will be used as a benchmark in the monitoring and evaluation of the project performance • To collect and analyze the relevant information of existing situation of project’s targeted beneficiaries (including disadvantaged households and impact of inter communal conflict to target beneficiaries and project implementation), service providers, and/or related stakeholders. • To generate a high-quality baseline survey report that will provide an accurate reference framework for both mid-term and end-term evaluation. • Identify conflict hotspots in Kapoeta East areas and document the main drivers of communal conflicts, their pattern, seasonality and typology. • To inform development of the project monitoring and evaluation plan • Identify other peacebuilding initiatives, if any, and main challenges faced. 4. Scope of the work: The consultant is expected to undertake the following tasks: • Submit a proposal on how to conduct the baseline survey; • Carry out a desk-review of relevant project documents including, the project monitoring, evaluation and learning (MEL) framework, budget and other relevant documents prior to the implementation of the study; • Provide an inception report detailing the proof of concept; • Develop the baseline survey tools (questionnaires, interview checklists, guidelines for enumerators, etc.) in consultation with project staff; • Train research assistants/enumerators on data collection tools and undertake a pre-test of the questionnaire • Conduct the baseline survey: perform Household interviews, focus group discussions and/or key informant interviews, etc. • Analyze and quality check the data, including through review meeting(s) with trained enumerators to get more in-depth understanding of the data collected. • Prepare and discuss with the Consortium members a draft report with sufficient detail to specify findings within each specific outcome, robustness of the indicators and/or their revisions and provide key recommendations for implementation • Undertake a validation of baseline survey findings with the Consortium members • Incorporate the comments from Consortium members into the final report • Prepare and submit a final report. 5. Approach and Methodology: 5.1: Approach The consultant will be required to develop clear methodology and procedure to carry out the task. The Consultant (s)/firm is expected to employ both qualitative and quantitative methods to ensure inclusion of all the project actors/stakeholders in the baseline survey process. The final decision on what type of methodology and selection of persons/groups interviewed or consulted will be the responsibility of the Survey Consultant /firm and expected to fully justify the choice of the methods in the final report and explain any limitations. The consultant will incorporate relevant elements of the Methodological notes as developed jointly by the Donor and Grantees. The design and implementation of the baseline must also ensure that principles of gender equality, inclusion and non-discrimination are considered and acted upon throughout, and that the meaningful participation of the most vulnerable groups and other key stakeholders is promoted in the design and implementation of the baseline. The baseline methodology designed should be replicable

description: Program Manager - Nigeria INTERSOS is an independent humanitarian organization that assists the victims of natural disasters, armed conflicts and exclusion. Gender-based violence (GBV) has been a significant protection concern faced by IDP women and girls in the area. Number: 25288 Position: Digital Program Specialist (Digital Strategy and Governance) Minimum 8 years of relevant professional experience Department/Divisionl: Information Technology Department (ITD) Job Type **: Global Recruitment Location: Beijing Posting Date: Aug 20, 2026 Closing Date *: Sep 10, 2026 Digital Program Specialist (Digital Strategy and Governance) The Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) is a multilateral development bank whose mission is financing Infrastructure for Tomorrow – infrastructure with sustainability at its core. We began operations in Beijing in January 2016 and have since grown to 103 approved members worldwide. We are capitalized up to USD100 billion and Triple-A-rated by the major international credit rating agencies. Working with partners, AIIB meets clients’ needs by unlocking new capital and investing in infrastructure that is green, technology-enabled, and promotes regional connectivity. The Information Technology Department (ITD) serves as AIIB's enterprise authority and service provider for digital technology. It develops and implements the Bank's digital strategy; delivers and operates digital solutions, AI capabilities, enterprise platforms, infrastructure, and workplace services; safeguards digital assets through cybersecurity, technology risk management, and resilience; and partners with business units to enable institutional priorities through secure, innovative, and client-centric digital capabilities. The Digital Program Specialist will support the leadership team in strengthening ITD's strategic planning, governance, business engagement, and organizational effectiveness. The role combines strategic analysis, program management, governance coordination, and organizational improvement responsibilities to support the planning, execution, and continuous enhancement of the Bank's digital capabilities. Working across ITD, business units, and external partners, the incumbent will conduct strategic analysis, support departmental planning, facilitate cross-functional initiatives, coordinate capability improvement programs, and promote the adoption of practices that strengthen ITD's ability to deliver business value. The incumbent will primarily be a strategic program manager and facilitator, working across ITD and business units to coordinate initiatives, enable organizational improvements, promote collaboration, and drive continuous enhancement of ITD's capabilities and ways of working. Responsibilities: Represent ITD in Bank-wide initiatives, cross-functional working groups, and institutional programs as delegated. Coordinate ITD's participation in Bank-wide initiatives, ensuring alignment across IT teams and facilitating implementation of agreed actions and outcomes. Participate in and, where appropriate, lead ITD's engagement with multilateral development banks (MDBs), international financial institutions (IFIs), industry forums, and professional communities to promote knowledge exchange, benchmarking, and collaboration. Lead or support strategic initiatives assigned by the IT leadership team. Coordinate cross-functional activities across ITD to facilitate successful implementation of strategic priorities. Coordinate with IT teams to assess, adapt, and promote relevant leading practices, methodologies, and innovations that strengthen ITD's capabilities and support the Bank's priorities. Prepare briefing materials, benchmarking reports, and recommendations summarizing key observations, lessons learned, and opportunities arising from external engagements and institutional initiatives. Monitor the implementation of agreed actions, identify issues requiring management attention, and recommend practical solutions. Support continuous improvement by identifying lessons learned, good practices, and opportunities to strengthen ITD's organizational effectiveness. Support engagements with business departments to understand their priorities, operating models, and strategic directions. Develop sufficient understanding of business domains to support executive discussions, strategic papers, benchmarking activities, and cross-functional initiatives. Gather business feedback on delivered digital capabilities, and identify common themes, opportunities, and improvement areas. Work closely with IT delivery teams to promote alignment between business priorities and digital capabilities. Develop and maintain executive dashboards that provide strategic visibility of the Bank's IT portfolio. Analyze portfolio performance, business outcomes, delivery trends, and organizational impact to support executive decision-making. Collect and consolidate feedback from business stakeholders regarding the effectiveness, adoption, and business value of digital solutions. Complement project delivery reporting with business-focused insights and recommendations to improve value realization across the portfolio. Support continuous improvement of portfolio reporting, performance indicators, and business value measurement. Support the development and continuous improvement of IT governance practices, planning processes, methodologies, and departmental standards. Maintain and coordinate subject matter experts to create and update templates, playbooks, guidance materials, and governance artifacts that promote consistency across ITD. Coordinate the implementation of departmental improvement initiatives, and monitor progress against agreed objectives. Prepare governance papers, executive presentations, and management reports for leadership meetings and governance forums. Coordinate department-wide initiatives that strengthen ITD's knowledge management practices, working closely with solution owners, business analysts, and other subject matter experts. Facilitate the development, maintenance, and adoption of reusable knowledge assets, templates, playbooks, and guidance materials while ensuring that ownership remains with the appropriate business and technical teams. Promote knowledge sharing and reuse across ITD to improve consistency, organizational learning, and delivery effectiveness. Monitor progress of knowledge and capability development initiatives, and recommend opportunities for continuous improvement. Coordinate department-wide initiatives that improve ITD's productivity, collaboration, and operational effectiveness through the adoption of digital technologies, AI capabilities, and automation. Work with IT teams to identify, prioritize, and implement opportunities that simplify internal processes, improve collaboration, and reduce manual effort. Develop implementation plans, monitor progress, and facilitate adoption of internal digital productivity initiatives across ITD. Promote sharing of successful practices, and encourage broader adoption of AI-enabled ways of working within ITD. Evaluate emerging technologies, and recommend initiatives that enhance ITD's effectiveness and employee experience. Conduct research on emerging technologies, AI trends, digital practices, and peer MDBs and IFIs to support IT strategic planning. Analyze business strategies, departmental priorities, and technology trends to identify opportunities that inform ITD's strategic planning and organizational priorities. Support the development and periodic refinement of the Bank's digital strategy, AI strategy, and ITD strategic plans. Prepare strategic analyses, benchmarking studies, executive briefings, and recommendations to support management decision-making. Requirements: Minimum 8 years of relevant professional experience in digital strategy, IT governance, enterprise project management office (PMO) functions, business analysis, management consulting, organizational improvement, or related disciplines. Bachelor's degree in information systems, business administration, computer science, organizational development, or a related discipline. Master's degree preferred. Experience working in consulting firms, international organizations, or financial institutions is an advantage. Experience supporting strategic planning, governance, portfolio management, or cross-functional organizational initiatives. Experience preparing executive reports, strategic analyses, business cases, and management presentations. Demonstrated ability to conduct research, benchmarking, and comparative analysis and translate findings into practical recommendations. Experience participating in cross-functional initiatives, international working groups, industry forums, or collaborative programs involving multiple organizations is desirable. Experience applying AI tools, digital workplace technologies, or workflow improvements to enhance organizational effectiveness is desirable. Good understanding of enterprise IT, AI, business process management, portfolio management, and modern software delivery practices. Knowledge of Agile, product management, business analysis, business process management, or software development life cycle (SDLC) methodologies is desirable. Strategic thinking and analytical problem-solving abilities. Experience in research, benchmarking, and insight generation; IT governance and portfolio management; program management and organizational coordination; and business engagement and stakeholder relationship management. Ability to influence and coordinate across multidisciplinary teams. Strong organizational and planning skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities. Curiosity and continuous learning, with an interest in emerging technologies, AI and leading industry practices. Good executive communication and presentation skills. Excellent command of written and spoken English. AIIB is committed to diversity, transparency, and inclusion. We believe our strength comes from having a team with the right diverse skills, experiences, and abilities selected through a merit-based competitive process. Number: 25286 Position: Senior Evaluation Specialist At least 10 years of progressively responsible experience Department/Division: Complaints-resolution, Evaluation and Integrity Unit Job Type **: Global Recruitment Location: Beijing Posting Date: Aug 18, 2026 Closing Date *: Sep 08, 2026 Senior Evaluation Specialist The Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) is a multilateral development bank whose mission is financing Infrastructure for Tomorrow in Asia and beyond – infrastructure with sustainability at its core. We began operations in Beijing in 2016 and have since grown to 111 approved members worldwide. We are capitalized at USD100 billion and AAA-rated by the major international credit rating agencies. Collaborating with partners, AIIB meets clients’ needs by unlocking new capital and investing in infrastructure that is green, technology-enabled, and promotes regional connectivity. The Complaints-resolution, Evaluation and Integrity Unit (CEIU) was established in 2016 as an independent unit within AIIB and is part of AIIB’s Oversight Mechanism created by its Board of Directors under Article 26(iv) of the AIIB Articles of Agreement. The 2019 Decision on the Oversight Mechanism by the Board of Directors formally established AIIB’s Independent Evaluation Function (IEF) under the responsibility of CEIU. AIIB’s first Learning and Evaluation Policy was approved by the Board of Directors in May 2021. The policy covers the purpose of learning and evaluation in the Bank and outlines the principles and internationally accepted criteria that underpin its learning and evaluation activities. Reporting to the Head of IEF, the Senior Evaluation Specialist will lead and contribute to project-level early learning assessments (ELAs) and project learning reviews (PLRs) across the full range of AIIB operations, covering both sovereign-backed financings (SBF) and nonsovereign-backed financings (NSBF) in equal measure. NSBF coverage includes financial intermediation, funds, bonds, guarantees, equity, and other forms of private sector investment. SBF coverage spans AIIB’s infrastructure sectors, themes, strategies, and institutional processes, in line with CEIU’s work program and evaluation protocols. The incumbent will also lead and conduct thematic evaluations at the sector, strategy, instrument, and corporate levels, synthesizing evidence across both financing modalities. Responsibilities: Develop and update guidance to facilitate the implementation of AIIB’s Learning and Evaluation Policy, with attention to both nonsovereign and sovereign operations. Undertake ELAs of ongoing operations and PLRs of completed AIIB financings, covering SBF and NSBF in balanced measure and across all financing modalities, in accordance with CEIU protocols. Lead and conduct thematic evaluations – spanning sectors, strategies, financing instruments, institutional processes, and cross-cutting themes across both the SBF and NSBF portfolios – from approach paper and methodology design through evidence gathering, report preparation, and presentation of findings to management and the Board, as assigned by the Head of the IEF and in line with the CEIU work program approved by the Managing Director, CEIU (MD-CEIU). Prepare and deliver training sessions, awareness-raising activities, and explanatory materials to facilitate organizational learning from evaluation findings. Provide independent inputs to inform the development and review of operational policies, instruments, and strategies, covering both SBF and NSBF, as appropriate. Participate in joint evaluation activities with development partners and cofinanciers on projects of shared interest. Lead or contribute to the preparation of thematic evaluation reports, synthesis papers, working papers, and knowledge products relevant to both SBF and NSBF. Contribute to the CEIU Annual Activity Review, ensuring comprehensive and balanced coverage of SBF, NSBF, and thematic evaluation activities. Provide technical comments on draft evaluation reports and on AIIB operational documents, drawing on subject matter expertise. Support the dissemination of evaluation findings, and promote institutional learning across AIIB, its development partners, and members. Support other activities within CEIU, as needed, and undertake additional tasks assigned by the Head of the IEF, including tasks requested by MD-CEIU through the Head of the IEF. Requirements: At least 10 years of progressively responsible experience in multilateral development banks (MDBs), international financial institutions, or comparable development organizations, with balanced exposure to both SBF and NSBF operations. Prior experience in another MDB, particularly within an independent evaluation function or office, is highly desirable. Minimum five years’ relevant experience in project design, implementation, supervision, and/or evaluation across sectors (e.g., energy, transport, urban, water, climate finance, and finance), with demonstrated exposure to both SBF and NSBF operations. Master’s degree or equivalent in economics, finance, law, public policy, or related disciplines from a recognized institution. Familiarity with MDB operational policies, financing instruments, and results measurement frameworks for both sovereign operations and private-sector engagements (e.g., financial intermediaries, funds, public-private partnerships, equity, guarantees). Proven expertise in development evaluation, applied research, and analytical work across the project, sector, thematic, and country levels, with the ability to assess institutional, technical, economic, and policy aspects. Demonstrated experience in designing and leading thematic, sector, strategy, or corporate-level evaluations, including the formulation of evaluation questions and methodology, synthesis of evidence across multiple projects and countries, and presentation of findings and recommendations to Senior Management and Board. Strong experience in providing independent evaluation inputs to operational strategy reviews, policy dialogues, and programming discussions within an MDB context. Proficiency in leveraging technology and innovation in evaluation practice, including the use of artificial intelligence tools, data visualization and synthesis tools, and geospatial platforms, for enhanced evidence generation and validation. Experience working across multiple countries in Asia would be preferred. Demonstrated ability to navigate complex stakeholder environments and cultural contexts. Strong ability to synthesize evaluation findings into actionable recommendations and effectively communicate lessons learned to both operational and strategic audiences. Able to manage competing priorities. High levels of personal integrity, professionalism, and diplomatic acumen, with a commitment to collaboration and knowledge sharing. Outstanding written and oral communication skills in English. Knowledge of another AIIB member language would be an asset. AIIB is committed to diversity, transparency, and inclusion. We believe our strength comes from having a team with the right diverse skills, experiences, and abilities selected through a merit-based competitive process. We actively encourage applications from people from both within and outside AIIB members, regardless of nationality, religion, gender, race, disability, or sexual orientation. Join in AIIB’s mission to promote sustainable infrastructure investments and to improve social and economic outcomes in Asia and beyond. Previous experience and qualifications will determine the grade and job title at which successful applicants will enter AIIB. Apply Here

title: Caseworker
sectors: Administration, Management, Finance/Accounting, Procurement; Social, Education, Gender, Youth, Child
description: Caseworker The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future. Job Overview: The Caseworker provides trauma-informed services to refugees and other ORR-eligible immigrants to support a positive integration experience and the achievement of client self-sufficiency. This position delivers individualized case management services, develops self-sufficiency plans in partnership with clients, and connects households to essential resources in the community. The Caseworker works closely with clients, colleagues, and external service providers to ensure timely access to benefits, housing, healthcare, employment, and other supports necessary for successful resettlement. Major Responsibilities: Responsibilities include, but are not limited to: • Conduct intakes and needs assessments to identify strengths, barriers, and goals for enrolled clients. • Develop Family Self-Sufficiency Plans (FSSPs) and Individual Employability Plans (IEPs) with clients, ensuring alignment with program and donor requirements. • Provide trauma-informed case management services, including direct support, referrals, and advocacy with service providers. • Coordinate access to housing, benefits, healthcare, education, and employment services. • Monitor client progress toward goals, adjusting plans as needed, and ensure documentation is timely and accurate in case files and data systems. • Maintain strong relationships with community partners and service providers to expand available resources for clients. • Participate in case conferences, team meetings, and trainings to promote quality service delivery and professional development. • Follow all IRC policies and procedures, including safeguarding, data protection, and confidentiality protocols. Job Requirements: Education: • Bachelor’s degree in Social Work or related field strongly preferred; comparable work experience may be substituted. Work Experience: • Minimum 2 years of case management experience in a social services environment. • Experience working with vulnerable or underserved populations preferred. Demonstrated Skills and Competencies: • Strong organizational and time-management skills; detail-oriented. • Ability to work effectively as part of a cross-cultural, multi-disciplinary team. • Problem-solver with ability to work independently and manage competing priorities. • Proficient in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook, Teams). • Excellent verbal and written communication skills; public speaking experience preferred. Language Skills: • Proficiency in English required; bilingual ability in Spanish, Dari, Swahili, Kinyarwanda, Arabic, French, or other refugee/immigrant language preferred. Certificates or Licenses: • Valid driver’s license, active insurance policy, and access to reliable transportation. • Must possess or be eligible for a fingerprint clearance card per Arizona state law. Working Environment; • A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities. • Occasional evening or weekend work may be required. • Must be able to lift 35–50 pounds (furniture, household supplies, food boxes). Compensation: ($20.97/hr). Compensation is based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements How to apply: Visit IRC Careers: https://theirc.wd1.myworkdayjobs.com/External_Careers/job/Phoenix-AZ-USA/Caseworker_JR00004628-1

title: Water Resources Partnership Manager
description: Catchment partnerships hold a wealth of local knowledge about their rivers and catchments, yet this is not always reflected in the regional decisions that shape investment in water resources. Two new roles are being created to change this, working across the South East and Thames River Basin Districts; this role is hosted by South East Rivers Trust (SERT). The roles are fixed term for two years, funded by Water Resources South East (WRSE) and supported by the WRSE team and their technical consultants, their Environmental Stakeholder Advisory Board and members of Catchment Based Approach Working Groups. In this role you will be the primary point of contact between WRSE and catchment hosts, helping Catchment Based Approach (CaBA) partnerships engage with regional planning. This includes supporting the creation of regional plans covering Environmental Destination scenarios, the Regional Water Industry National Environment Programme (WINEP) and the wider WRSE Regional Plan, and supporting catchment hosts in understanding water resources data and modelled outputs so local knowledge informs regional planning. What you'll be doing: - Act as the main liaison between WRSE and catchment hosts, working mainly through hosts to reach CaBA partnerships. - Support partnerships to engage with Environmental Destination, Regional WINEP, catchment solutions and wider regional water resources planning. - Coordinate and make sense of existing catchment evidence to support identification of catchment options, including nature-based solutions. - Join up this work with Drainage and Wastewater Management Plans, River Basin Management Plans and Local Nature Recovery Strategies. - Translate technical water resources and modelling outputs into clear, accessible briefings and materials. - Identify and help resolve barriers to progressing catchment options. About you: a natural communicator able to convey complex concepts clearly, with a good understanding of catchment-based approaches and water resource issues; experience facilitating engagement with multi-partner programmes and environmental stakeholders; ability to interpret technical information and translate it for different audiences; strong analytical, problem-solving and organisational skills; and the ability to work independently across multiple workstreams. Hybrid working with attendance at the Leatherhead office up to four times a month, and extensive travel across the SERT region (Hampshire to Kent, south of the Thames). A driving licence is required. Salary £40,810 - £45,611 per year, full-time, two-year fixed term contract. Closing date: 13 September 2026 HOW TO APPLY: Apply online via the South East Rivers Trust careers site for this 2-year fixed term contract; see the full job description at https://www.southeastriverstrust.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/JD-Water-Resources-Partnership-Manager-SERT.pdf. Closing date for applications: Sunday 13th September, 11.59pm. Interviews in-person in central London on Wednesday 23rd September. The Trust reserves the right to close this job advert early. https://careers.southeastriverstrust.org/jobs/8184284-water-resources-partnership-manager-south-east-rivers-trust

title: Consultant
company: Ministry of Finance, Sierra Leone (Sierra Leone Digital Transformation Project)
description: Recruitment of an Individual Consultant for the Review for the Cybersecurity and Crime Act 2021 and Development of Governance and Regulatory Framework The Government of Sierra Leone, through the Sierra Leone Digital Transformation Project (SLDTP), invites eligible Individual Consultants to express interest in reviewing the Cybersecurity and Cybercrime Act, 2021 and developing a future-ready governance, legal, and regulatory framework for the country's cyberspace. The assignment requires the consultant to conduct a legal, regulatory, and institutional assessment of the Act's adequacy and enforceability; evaluate coherence among existing cybersecurity, data protection, and digital governance policies; benchmark against international instruments such as the Malabo Convention, Budapest Convention, ITU Global Cybersecurity Index, NIST framework, and ISO/IEC standards; identify legal, institutional, and capacity gaps; rationalise institutional roles across MDAs, law enforcement, regulators, and other stakeholders; design a fit-for-purpose regulatory framework with subsidiary legislation and enforcement protocols; develop a national cyber governance and coordination framework including incident response and information-sharing mechanisms; and formulate a costed implementation roadmap. Selection will follow the World Bank's Individual Consultant Selection method under its Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, with attention to conflict-of-interest provisions in Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17. Detailed Terms of Reference are available via the SLDTP and MoCTI project websites. HOW TO APPLY: Interested Individual Consultants should submit Expressions of Interest by e-mail to the Project Coordination Unit, Sierra Leone Digital Transformation Project, Attn: The Project Coordinator, 5th Floor, NaTCA Building, Southridge, IMATT, Freetown, Email: coordinator@sldtp.mocti.gov.sl, CC: procurement@sldtp.moic.gov.sl, on or before 28 August 2026, 12:00 GMT. title: M&E Consultant of PMT
company: Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development (MARD), Albania
description: The World Bank is assisting the Government of Albania with financing the Climate Resilience and Agriculture Development Project (CRAD, P178715), which aims to increase competitiveness and climate resilience of priority agri-food value chains. The Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development (MARD) invites individual consultants to express interest in the position of M&E Consultant of the Project Management Team (PMT). The M&E Specialist will establish and operationalize robust monitoring and evaluation systems for the project, ensuring activities across all components are tracked, analyzed, and reported in line with the project's development objectives. Key responsibilities include developing an M&E framework with indicators, data collection methodologies, and reporting protocols; coordinating collection and analysis of data on productivity, irrigation/drainage upgrades, food safety compliance, and institutional strengthening; building MARD and municipal capacity for data management, including gender-disaggregated indicators; facilitating participatory monitoring with local stakeholder groups; preparing progress reports and evaluations for government and World Bank counterparts; supporting safeguards compliance monitoring including grievance redress; and providing technical support for digital tools such as the Irrigation and Drainage Management Information System (IDMIS) and GIS mapping. Required qualifications: a university degree (preferably Master's) in Economics, Business Administration, Statistics, Public Administration, Agricultural/Rural Development, Social Sciences, or a related field; at least 15 years of overall professional experience; at least 7 years in design, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of development projects in agriculture, food safety, or irrigation; at least 10 years working on projects financed by international development organizations, preferably in agriculture/rural development; World Bank-financed project experience is an advantage; strong knowledge of results-based M&E methodologies; excellent analytical, report-writing, and presentation skills; excellent Albanian and English; strong interpersonal and teamwork skills. The assignment is a full-time, Time Based Contract for an initial 12 months (3-month probation), renewable up to 38 months based on satisfactory performance. Selection follows the World Bank's Selection of Individual Consultant procedures. HOW TO APPLY: Interested individual consultants should submit: (i) a motivation letter underlining their advantages for this position, (ii) Curriculum Vitae, and (iii) information/references demonstrating the required qualifications. "Dëshmorët e Kombit", Nr. 2, 1001, Tirana, Albania, Attn: Mr. Arben Molla, Project Manager of PMT, or electronically to arben.molla@bujqesia.gov.al.

description: Consultant: Technical Advisory Services Proposal ASSIGNMENT DESCRIPTION A key priority for CVF-V20 is to bolster the global financial safety net and cushion the yawning financial protection gap. Parametric insurance has become a leading instrument to assist in this endeavor. However, limited market sizes in Low-Income Developing Countries (LDCs) and Small Island Developing States (SIDS) pose a structural impediment to achieving scale; this often takes time and requires considerable investment and resources. Given the underdeveloped microinsurance market and growing climatic risk, increasing reinsurance pricing is a key hurdle hindering the scaling of microinsurance coverage. This contributes to three key challenges: (1) high reinsurance premium costs that could make products unviable; (2) the withdrawal of reinsurance or a significant increase in pricing due to extreme events; and (3) a lack of interest from reinsurers due to the small size of these markets. Regional Risk Pools (RRPs) can play an instrumental role by providing anchor reinsurance for insurance providers, specifically for the inclusive insurance segment of the market. Preliminary discussions have been held with the Caribbean-domiciled RRP, CCRIF SPC (formerly the Caribbean Catastrophe Risk Insurance Facility), as they have a keen interest in embedding a reinsurance window for inclusive insurance coverage. The V20 Secretariat will support this initiative. To advance this important work, the V20 Secretariat has secured funding from the Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) of Germany and seeks the services of a competent firm or individual to provide technical advisory. The successful candidate will be required to provide technical advisory support including, but not limited to, the following: 1. Feasibility and Technical Advisory Report An in-depth feasibility study and detailed advisory report on CCRIF venturing into the reinsurance segment to safeguard the exposures of inclusive insurance. The report should cover, inter alia: * Technical and financial feasibility of establishing and operating the reinsurance window. * Risk modeling, capital and financial requirements, and risk management considerations. * Regulatory considerations and requirements. * Review of the governance and institutional framework and recommendation of a suitable set-up. The assessment should consider whether the current set-up is sufficient to meet the needs of the private insurance market. * Review of the proposed cell structure and its potential to maximize risk diversification within the proposed reinsurance window. * Assessment of the additional technical and operational capacity that CCRIF would require to establish and operate the reinsurance window effectively. * Advisory recommendations to the CCRIF Board and Management on the pros and cons of establishing the reinsurance window as a business unit. 2. Stakeholder Workshop Coordinate with CCRIF to jointly organize, with the CVF-V20 Secretariat and the World Bank Group (WBG), a stakeholder workshop to socialize the proposed reinsurance initiative. The workshop should engage key stakeholders, including Ministries of Finance, insurance regulators and other relevant regulatory authorities, development partners, and private sector insurance and reinsurance stakeholders. The consultant will support the preparation of workshop materials, presentation of the feasibility findings and recommendations, facilitation of stakeholder discussions, and documentation of feedback and agreed next steps. Eligible applicants should not have been cited for suspension or been banned for corrupt or fraudulent procurement or business practices by recognized international organizations such as the United Nations, the World Bank, or any recognized public body locally or internationally. description: Chapter Authors for the Fifth African Transformation Report (ATR5) Location: Accra, Ghana The African Center for Economic Transformation (ACET), founded in 2008, is an economic policy institute providing research, policy advice and institutional strengthening for African countries to develop their economies, reduce poverty and improve livelihoods. ACET invites expressions of interest from qualified individual consultants and researchers to serve as chapter authors for the Fifth African Transformation Report (ATR5), its flagship publication, which examines Africa's prospects for productive transformation, resilience and strategic agency in a fragmented and uncertain global environment. The report applies and extends ACET's Growth with DEPTH framework, measuring transformation through diversification, export competitiveness, productivity, technology upgrading and human wellbeing, and analyses five simultaneous shifts: geopolitical fragmentation and contested power; the reconfiguration of development cooperation and finance; green industrialization, energy transition and critical minerals; technological acceleration and AI; and the youth quake and shifting demographic window. Eight of the report's ten chapters are open for expression of interest (Chapters 2-9); consultants may apply for more than one chapter, indicating order of preference. Shortlisting criteria: at least a master's degree in economics, development economics, public policy or a related field (PhD/MPhil an advantage); a minimum of ten (10) years of relevant professional experience; a strong record of high-quality, policy-relevant research and writing on African or comparable developing economies; strong empirical and analytical skills including work with quantitative data and the ATI; expert knowledge of the economic transformation landscape in one or more African countries; experience producing and reviewing research papers, journal articles, book chapters, policy reports and books; demonstrated ability to work to deadlines and contribute within a multi-author, peer-reviewed process; familiarity with ACET's Growth with DEPTH framework an added advantage.
