About EJF: The Environmental Justice Foundation (EJF) is a global non-profit organisation working to protect the natural world and our fundamental human right to a secure environment. Through field investigations, rigorous research, and strategic international advocacy, EJF exposes environmental crime, challenges impunity, and catalyses systemic reform. Campaigns span four interconnected areas: oceans, climate, forests and wetlands, and the training, protection, and empowerment of environmental defenders and investigative journalists. About the role: EJF's Ocean team investigates and documents illegal, unreported and unregulated (IUU) fishing and the human rights abuses that so often accompany it - forced labour and trafficking, physical violence, and deaths at sea. As Senior Oceans Campaigner you will deliver the advocacy and campaign strategy for the Ocean programme: identifying the changes sought, the decision-makers who can deliver them, and designing the sequence of pressure, persuasion and partnership that moves them. You will work across governments in market, coastal and flag states, parliamentarians and regulators, international fora, and the seafood industry. Current priorities include full transparency in the global fishing industry through the Global Charter for Fisheries Transparency; robust import controls and carding regimes in major seafood markets; ratification and enforcement of key labour rights conventions; ending abusive trans-shipment at sea; beneficial ownership disclosure; and accountability for distant-water fleets. Key responsibilities: Develop and deliver advocacy and campaign plans with clear objectives, targets, tactics and timelines; work with investigations, policy, film and communications colleagues to translate evidence into campaign propositions; map decision-makers, influencers and opposition; identify and act on political openings such as legislative reviews and treaty negotiations; prepare briefings, position papers and policy asks and lead meetings with senior decision-makers; press retailers, importers, processors and certification bodies to act; support the launch of films, reports and investigations for maximum political impact; act as a spokesperson with media and at public events; contribute campaign content including briefings, op-eds, digital actions and petitions; monitor, evaluate and report on campaign progress. Essential skills and experience: Demonstrable experience designing and delivering advocacy or campaign strategies that secured concrete changes in policy, law, regulation or corporate practice; superb written and verbal communication skills with the ability to produce high-calibre, precise copy quickly; experience working on ocean policy, fisheries, environmental governance, human rights or a related discipline; extensive experience presenting to diverse audiences; ability to build effective strategies for delivering core messages and creative problem-solving; strong political judgement; rigorous attention to detail and commitment to factual accuracy; ability to manage several campaigns and deadlines at once; a clear commitment to EJF's vision, mission and values; ability to work independently and collegiately within a team. Desirable: familiarity with trends in global fisheries governance; experience of corporate engagement, supply chain accountability or certification schemes; working knowledge of a second language relevant to EJF's programme countries. What we offer: 22 days' annual leave (exclusive of bank holidays), increasing with service, plus discretionary additional paid leave between Christmas and New Year; private healthcare package; generous pension scheme with employer contributions increasing over time; flexible working hours and hybrid working (3 days office / 2 home); cycle-to-work scheme; a dynamic, supportive and inclusive working environment with opportunities for professional development. title: ESO Fellowship Programme Chile 2026/2027
sectors: Infrastructure, Technology, Engineering, Science; Monitoring, Evaluation, Policy, Research, Analysis
description: The European Southern Observatory (ESO) invites applications for the ESO Fellowship Programme 2026/2027. The Programme is designed to help early career scientists develop their independent research programmes and reach the next step of their scientific careers by: developing their scientific profiles in a rich and structured scientific environment alongside more senior scientists; becoming mature and independent researchers who develop their own research projects and contribute to collaborative scientific endeavours; preparing to take on higher scientific, technical or supervisory/managerial responsibilities; and developing their understanding of instrumental and observational techniques through supporting observatory operations. ESO Fellows are expected to actively participate in ESO's scientific life by proposing and contributing to the organisation of scientific workshops, co-supervising PhD students, coordinating thematic research groups, joining scientific committees, and organising seminars. The ESO Vitacura Office in Santiago is where ESO Fellows interact with Instrument and System Scientists and Science Operations Managers from Paranal, ALMA and La Silla, with a continuous flow of visiting astronomers. ESO Chile is an excellent place to build collaborations with the Chilean astronomical community and with other international observatories in the country. Fellowships in Chile are granted for four years. During the first three years, Fellows are assigned duties within one of the Science Operation groups of Paranal or ALMA, contributing to observatory operations at a level of 80 nights per year (50% of working time). ALMA duties may include observing at the telescope, data processing and analysis, software testing, serving as technical experts in the ALMA proposal review process, and developing new array capabilities. At Paranal, Fellows act as support astronomers executing service-mode observations or assisting visiting astronomers, and join an Instrument Operations Team. Fellows may spend the fourth year at any astronomy/astrophysics institute in an ESO member state, in Australia, at a Chilean institution, or at ESO; there are no functional duties in the fourth year. Qualifications: open to applicants who will have obtained their PhD in astronomy, physics or a related discipline before 1 November 2027. Early-career scientists from all astrophysical fields — observational, theoretical and computational — are welcome. The ideal candidate should demonstrate comprehension of general science cases outside their own field of research, have good communication and time management skills, work independently, and take personal responsibility for their work. Remuneration: an attractive package including a competitive salary and allowances, comprehensive social benefits, and financial support for relocating families. The Office for Science provides funding for attending international conferences and workshops and for science visits to other institutes during the fellowship. Closing date: 15/10/2026 HOW TO APPLY: Apply online by completing the web application form available at https://recruitment.eso.org. The application consists of three documents: the Motivation letter form, the Research plan form, and the Academic and Research track record form, all uploaded in PDF format to the related vacancy at the ESO recruitment portal. Templates (Word, LibreOffice, Latex) are available at https://www.eso.org/sci/activities/fellowships-and-studentships/FeSt-overview/fellowship_programme/application_guidelines.html. Applicants must also provide names and contact details of three people familiar with their scientific work and willing to provide a recommendation letter; for the Chile Fellowship Programme referees are automatically invited to submit letters by the application deadline of 15 October 2026 (midnight Chilean time). Incomplete or late applications will not be considered. https://recruitment.eso.org/jobs/2026_0052

title: Audiovisual Media Internship
sectors: Communications, Media, Knowledge Management, Editor; Infrastructure, Technology, Engineering, Science
description: The European Organisation for Astronomical Research in the Southern Hemisphere (ESO) is the foremost intergovernmental astronomy organisation in Europe and the world's most productive ground-based astronomical observatory, operating three observing sites in the Chilean Atacama Desert. ESO is building the Extremely Large Telescope (ELT), the largest optical and near-infrared telescope on Earth, with partners across Europe and in Chile. ESO's Headquarters are in Garching near Munich, Germany. ESO's Department of Communication (ESO COMM) is responsible for all aspects of internal and external communication for the Organisation, including audiovisual productions that excite the public about science, astronomy and engineering. As Audiovisual Media Intern you will support ESO's Creative Team, part of ESO COMM, in numerous video productions - such as the hosted show Chasing Starlight with Suzanna Randall, a documentary on the construction of the ELT, and explainers about scientific discoveries. You will work alongside seasoned professionals in film, animation and graphic design, participating in all stages of the production workflow from pre-production to release, with a focus on video editing. You will also help structure footage, prepare interviews and maintain archives, and will learn how a large international scientific organisation works, how to edit videos for science communication across formats and audiences, and how to collaborate within a diverse multinational team. Main duties: video editing for various lengths, formats and audiences; structuring interviews, preparing footage and creating compilations; assisting with video recordings on location and in the studio; organising archival footage; additional audiovisual tasks as required. Requirements: highly motivated and proactive students or graduates of Audiovisual Media or a comparable degree programme; experience in video editing, audio processing and working with camera and lights (a demo reel or video portfolio is requested); experience with the Adobe Creative Suite, particularly Adobe Premiere; experience in post-production or motion graphics is a strong plus; ability to work under pressure to agreed deadlines and standards; ability to work on own initiative and as part of a team; ability to collaborate across cultures and disciplines. A good command of English is essential as it is the working language; Spanish or German is a plus. Internship details: internships take place in Garching, Germany (remote or hybrid is not possible) and last 6 months. Accommodation is provided along with a monthly allowance to cover living expenses, plus the cost of a return trip from/to the home station. ESO does not sponsor visas for this internship; applicants are responsible for securing their own right to enter, live and work in Germany. Recruitment preference is given to nationals of ESO Member States, host states and strategic partners. Closing date: 31/12/2026 HOW TO APPLY: Apply online at http://jobs.eso.org/. Applications must be completed in English and should include a motivation letter (1 page) and a CV (1-2 pages). Applicants must also provide links to past work samples, a demo reel or portfolio; for collaborative projects, indicate which parts of the production you were specifically responsible for. Only complete applications with all required materials in English will be accepted. Internships start every March and September; as this is a rolling position there is no fixed application deadline, and applications received less than 3 months prior to the starting date will be considered for the next open slot. Questions: vacancy@eso.org https://recruitment.eso.org/jobs/2025_0081

description: Position Title : External Evaluator Consultant Duty Station : IOM Philippines Country Office (Cotabato City) Classification: Consultant Type of Appointment: Consultancy Estimated Start Date: ASAP Closing Date : 28 August 2026 In 2019, over half of the employed persons in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM), 57.8 per cent, were working in the agricultural sector[1]. Despite having the fastest growth among the 16 regions in the value of production in agriculture and fisheries at 7.2 per cent in 2021, communities in BARMM remain one of the poorest, registering the lowest average annual family income of Php 184,000[2]. With support from the European Union, IOM as leading agency, together with FAO and ITC, implemented the Farmers-Fisherfolks’ Advancement and Integration to Resilient Value Chains in BARMM (FAIR-VALUE) project from 12 September 2023 to 11 September 2026 to improve the local agricultural/sea-aqua product production in quality, diversity, consolidation and its response to the needs of the market, with a primary focus on agri-fishery communities and smallholders in conflict-affected or conflict-prone areas in the island provinces of Basilan, Sulu, and Tawi-Tawi (BaSulTa). FAIR VALUE delivered a series of interventions directly supporting more than 500 farmers across the BaSulTa through the 12 production clusters of coffee (4 clusters), rubber (6 clusters) and seaweeds (2 clusters) established through the project, and capacitated around 50 government stakeholders on quality production and food safety. Key outputs of the project include: 1) the mapping and analysis of local value chain to inform the decision-making of agri-fishery communities and government stakeholders; 2) capacity-building of farmers for quality, diversified, and market-oriented production; 3) establishment of pilot social enterprises with marketable production; and 4) improved and accessible processing and logistic facilities and equipment through public-private partnerships (PPPs). These outputs contribute to the improvement of local agricultural and sea-aqua product production in quality, diversity, and consolidation, in response to the needs of the market. By uplifting the socio-economic conditions of agri-fishery sector, in which majority of poor and remote Bangsamoro communities work, the project aimed to build their resilience to drivers of conflict and instability including poverty, inequality and lack of social cohesion, thereby contributing to a peaceful, cohesive, secure and inclusively developed Bangsamoro. The joint final evaluation will be conducted to examine the higher-level results of the project and facilitate learning, promoting accountability and enhancing decision-making for policymakers, programme managers, and other key stakeholders. IOM, FAO, and ITC will use the findings and recommendations from the FAIR-VALUE project evaluation to design, implement, and monitor projects of similar nature, as well as document lessons learned and best practices from the FAIR VALUE project. It will focus on four primary objectives: • Generate evidence on the impact and results of the project, including documentation of lessons learned, effective strategies, and best practices; • Determine the significant higher-level effects of the project interventions; • Assess the program’s efficiency and effectiveness in fostering collaboration among Participating United Nations Organizations (PUNOs); and • Identify recommendations, lessons learned, and good practices to inform programming and future resource mobilization in supporting similar projects within the same themes. The final external evaluation of the project is scheduled to occur one (1) month after the end of the project. The evaluation will cover the following: Full project period from 12 September 2023 to 11 September 2026; Full geographic scope of the project, including the Basilan, Sulu, and Tawi-Tawi provinces; All groups of project participants, including members of the project team, select participants and resource persons in the training, consultation, and community activities, stakeholders from the local and regional governments, and project partners including service providers and consultants, with logistical considerations for programme participants; and Cross-cutting themes that will be assessed, including gender mainstreaming, environmental sensitivity and sustainability, cultural sensitivity, and accountability to affected populations (AAP). [1] Philippine Statistics Authority, 2020, Agricultural Indicators System [2] Philippine Statistics Authority, 2022, Highlights of the Preliminary Results of the 2021 Annual Family Income and Expenditure Survey, https://psa.gov.ph/content/highlights-preliminary-results-2021-annual-family-income-and-expenditure-survey Department / Unit to which the Consultant is contributing: Programme Support Unit, CS.1221: Farmers-Fisherfolks’ Advancement and Integration to Resilient Value Chains in BARMM (FAIR-VALUE). Responsibilities: Tasks to be performed under this contract: The evaluator or the evaluation team will hold overall responsibility for the methodology, data collection and analysis, report writing, and presentation of evaluation findings. Additional team members may be included by the team lead upon discussion with and approval of the Evaluation Manager. The evaluator shall also be responsible for coordinating the schedule and modality of interviews and FGDs with interviewees. Below are the expected evaluation deliverables: • Inception Report o Includes a detailed description of the evaluation approach and methodology, work plan, evaluation matrix, interview and FGD guides, list of persons to be interviewed, and other data collection instruments to be used for the evaluation. o The Evaluation Management Group (EMG) and the Evaluation Reference Group (ERG) shall review and approve the inception report. • Evaluation Report (First Draft) o First draft report, supported by annexes including the evaluation TOR, evaluation matrix, list of documents reviewed, list of persons interviewed, and data collection instruments, submitted to the Evaluation Manager. o The EMG and ERG shall review and provide comments on the draft evaluation report. • Presentation of Evaluation Findings o The evaluator shall present the initial findings to the EMG and ERG. • Final Evaluation Report o The final evaluation report shall incorporate inputs and recommendations from the EMG and ERG. o The EMG and ERG shall review and approve the final evaluation report. • Final Presentation of the Evaluation Report o The evaluator shall present the key findings from the final evaluation report to the EMG and ERG. • Evaluation Brief o The evaluator shall submit an evaluation brief, along with the final evaluation report. The evaluation brief shall be cleared and accepted by the EMG and ERG • Management Response Matrix (partially filled-out) o The evaluator shall submit a partially filled-out Management Response Matrix to the Evaluation Manager. Performance indicators for the evaluation of results: • All evaluation deliverables shall be reviewed and cleared by the Evaluation Management Group (EMG) and Evaluation Reference Group). • Timely delivery of the evaluation deliverables Qualifications: Required Qualifications and Experience: Education: • Advanced degree in a relevant field such as social sciences or statistics is required. Experience: • Minimum of five years of experience leading and conducting evaluations is required; • Knowledge/experience of UN system is desirable; • Understanding of BARMM and BaSulTa context is an advantage; • Experience in community stabilization and development projects is preferred; • Skills in evaluation design, qualitative and quantitative data collection and analysis, drafting and editing in English, communication, time management, and cultural and conflict sensitivity are required. Languages: For this consultancy, fluency in English is required. Basic familiarity with Tagalog and the local language in Basilan, Sulu, and/or Tawi-Tawi is desirable. The evaluator shall hire translation services if the evaluator does not have adequate fluency in the local language in BaSulTa. Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments. Encourages diversity and inclusion. • Integrity and transparency: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct. • Professionalism: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges. • Courage: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance. • Empathy: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated. description: Research Specialist – Global WASH Cluster/Field Support Team Introduction ACF is currently looking for a consultant, or consultant team, to undertake a research and analysis assignment. This assignment sits within the Field Support Team mechanism, in support of the Global WASH Cluster. General Background The Field Support Team (FST) is a surge and remote support mechanism for National Coordination Platforms (NCPs) and other WASH coordination arrangements in humanitarian contexts. The FST operates under the aegis of the Global WASH Cluster (GWC) Strategic Advisory Group (SAG) and under the strategic leadership of the GWC Cluster Advocacy and Support Team (CAST). The FST provides reliable and predictable coordination support to enable effective, efficient, and accountable WASH response coordination at national and sub-national levels. The team is composed of surge cluster coordinators, information management officers and an assessment specialist. Support is delivered through in-country and virtual deployments, as well as through remote, task-based technical assistance and global services provided to multiple countries through online platforms, guidance, tools, and capacity strengthening activities. Objectives Building on the existing evidence generated by the Global WASH Cluster, the objectives of this consultancy are: 1. Identify, compare and analyze operational transition pathways across different humanitarian contexts to develop practical recommendations for strengthening National Coordination Platforms in the context of the Humanitarian Reset, with particular attention to Area-Based Coordination (ABC), localization, multisectoral coordination and sustainable national leadership. 2. Examine how coordination arrangements evolve across different crisis trajectories, identifying the factors that enable or hinder sustainable transition. 3. Identify the institutional, governance and financing arrangements that enable sustainable coordination, including the contribution of government institutions, development actors and appropriate financing mechanisms. 4. Identify effective models for engaging Women-Led Organizations (WLOs), Women's Rights Organizations (WROs) and other nationally rooted actors in coordination and assess which approaches can be adapted across different contexts. The consultancy is expected to build on the substantial body of evidence already generated by the Global WASH Cluster. Rather than repeating previous analyses, it should focus on translating existing knowledge into forward-looking operational recommendations and practical coordination models. Assignment Duration and Indicative Workplan The assignment is expected to run for approximately three months, from mid-September to mid-December 2026. Given the timeframe, the research should adopt a focused and iterative approach, building on the existing GWC evidence base rather than undertaking a new comprehensive literature review. A Research Committee (RC) will be established to steer the process, comprising one member of the GWC SAG, one to two members from CAST and two to three members from ACF (around five people in total). The work will be organized according to the following indicative schedule: Phase 1 – Inception and research design (mid to end September 2026) The researcher will: • Review the existing GWC Secondary Data Reviews on Transition and Area-Based Coordination, the related workshop findings and other priority reference materials; • Review existing UNICEF materials related to systems strengthening, emergency preparedness and contingency planning, and sectoral coordination; • Refine the analytical framework and research questions; • Propose a focused sample of countries and/or contexts representing different crisis trajectories and levels of transition progress; • Develop the stakeholder-engagement and data-collection plan; • Confirm the proposed methodology, interview tools and comparative analysis framework; • Assess the added value of field visits in November, subject to feasibility and approval. • Present the progress to the Research Committee (RC) for validation (1st touch point with the RC). Deliverables: Inception report, including the refined methodology, country or context-selection rationale, detailed workplan, tools (e.g. questionnaires, etc.) and, if relevant, initial proposal for any field visits. Phase 2 – Initial data collection and interim analysis (October 2026) The researcher will conduct focused data collection through: • Key informant interviews; • Targeted review of country-level documentation; • Consultations with NCPs, UNICEF country offices/program, government counterparts, local and national actors, development partners and other relevant stakeholders; • Comparative analysis of countries progressing towards transition, countries where transition has stalled or reversed and countries adapting to changing crisis trajectories. The analysis should begin identifying: • Barriers to / Factors of a successful transition; • How progress has been achieved in practice, and which coordination functions have been key; • Which enabling conditions are transferable; • How coordination models or pathways differ across improving, protracted, deteriorating, recurrent-shock and mixed humanitarian-development contexts; • Emerging options for rethinking/supporting emergency coordination functions across sectoral stakeholders and defining governance and escalation arrangements. Phase 3 – Sense-making and complementary data collection (End of October to November 2026) An online sense-making workshop will be held at the end of October to review the initial findings, challenge emerging assumptions and refine the areas requiring further investigation (2nd touch point with the RC). Following the workshop, the researcher will: • Adjust the analytical framework based on participant feedback; • Conduct additional interviews and targeted follow-up research; • Deepen the comparative analysis of selected country cases; • Refine the proposed context-specific coordination models/pathways and practical options; • Confirm the relevance of any proposed field visits. Any field visits should provide evidence that cannot reasonably be gathered remotely, particularly through direct engagement with government, development and locally rooted actors. Destinations will be proposed during the inception phase and validated by ACF and the GWC based on analytical value, country-office engagement, security, operational feasibility and budget availability. Deliverable: Interim findings and presentation for the sense-making workshop, followed by a short note outlining the conclusions of the workshop and any resulting adjustments to the research. Phase 4 – Final analysis, operational recommendations and restitution (Late November to mid-December 2026) The researcher will consolidate and translate the evidence into forward-looking and practical findings. The final analysis should: • Identify key factors of / barriers to a successful transition of humanitarian coordination functions; • Identify how the foci of coordination transition changes as crisis trajectories (or capacities) evolve; • Propose practical approaches for identifying, retaining, sharing or transferring core coordination functions; • Set out workable governance, accountability, financing and institutional arrangements that support sustainable coordination models; • Identify practical ways to preserve WASH analytical leadership within ABC and other multisectoral structures; • Define transition-readiness considerations and safeguards against stalled, reversed or funding-driven transition. A final in-person restitution workshop will be held in mid-December to present and discuss the research findings and proposed operational ways forward (3rd touch point with the RC, potentially in Rome or Geneva or Berlin or Paris, t.b.d.). Final deliverables, due by mid-December 2026: • Present the final research findings at an in-person international workshop in December, supported by a presentation (PowerPoint or equivalent). • Produce a comprehensive comparative research report, including key findings, lessons learned, good practices, strategic recommendations, comparative typology of context-specific coordination pathways and the enabling conditions that support them; • Produce a concise signposting note, framed through the Transition and Area-Based Coordination (ABC) lens, directing National Coordination Platforms (NCPs), Women-Led Organizations (WLOs), and Women's Rights Organizations (WROs) to existing guidance and resources (e.g. IASC Localization Guidance, GWC Localization Roadmap etc.). • Present the research findings during a global webinar for National Coordination Platforms and other relevant members of the Global WASH Cluster community (online, date to be confirmed). • Present the research outcomes at an internal ACF learning event (online, date to be confirmed). Throughout the consultancy, findings should be interpreted in relation to the operational context in which coordination takes place. Rather than seeking a single transition model, the research should examine how coordination models/pathways adapt to different humanitarian contexts and capacities—including conflict, protracted crises, recurrent climatic shocks, mixed humanitarian-development settings and recovery contexts—and identify which operational approaches appear transferable or adaptable across contexts. Ways of Working: The researcher is expected to: • Maintain an adaptive research approach, refining the scope and priorities in response to emerging evidence and ongoing discussions on transition, localization, and multisectoral coordination. • Work closely with the Global WASH Cluster, its relevant working groups (including WIA/Climate Change), and ACF's Emergency Response and Recovery Unit (ERRU) and WASH Department to ensure complementarity, maximize synergies, and avoid duplication of efforts. • Where agreed during the inception phase, undertake a limited number of field visits (indicatively two, subject to confirmation) to engage directly with government counterparts, development partners, and other key stakeholders. Proposed destinations should be identified based on the initial research findings, thematic priorities, and the enabling environment confirmed by the relevant country offices and will be validated by ACF and the Global WASH Cluster, taking into account operational feasibility, security considerations, and budget availability. Highly insecure or operationally complex contexts requiring extended lead times are not expected to be included. Evaluation Criteria Selection criteria are organised into six components to support a transparent and evidence-based evaluation process: 1. Assessment of the application form; 2. Review of previous work samples; 3. Financial proposal; 4. Availability; 5. Interview. Only applicants meeting the requirements of the first five evaluation components will be shortlisted for an interview. Evaluation Criterion 1 – Application Form Review Applications will be assessed against the following criteria: • Master's degree (or higher) in a relevant discipline, such as humanitarian or development studies, political science, international relations, public policy, social sciences or a related field. Experience in academia and/or having a PhD are considered assets. • Minimum five (5) years of professional experience in humanitarian and/or development research, policy analysis, operational research or similar assignments. • In-depth experience in humanitarian coordination mechanisms, including previous experience with the Global WASH Cluster (GWC), the Field Support Team (FST), UNICEF, cluster coordination or other relevant humanitarian coordination architecture. Having coordinated with the cluster as WASH partner is not considered as an in-depth experience. • Excellent written and spoken English. • Working knowledge of French. • Working knowledge of Spanish (desirable). Evaluation Criterion 2 – Draft methodology: Applicants are requested to submit a brief methodology note (maximum 2 pages) outlining how they would approach the assignment. The note is not expected to provide a detailed research proposal but should demonstrate the applicant's understanding of the assignment and their proposed approach to delivering it within the available timeframe. Evaluation Criterion 3 – Sample of previous work: • Sample 1: One research report, analytical paper or similar publication demonstrating the applicant's experience in conducting applied research relevant to this consultancy. Work samples may be submitted in English, French or Spanish. • Sample 2: One presentation (PowerPoint or equivalent) prepared for a high-level workshop, conference or similar event, demonstrating the applicant's ability to communicate complex findings effectively. Work samples may be submitted in English, French or Spanish. Evaluation Criterion 4 – Daily rate: Applicants should provide their proposed daily consultancy rate (USD), inclusive of all applicable taxes and professional fees. Travel costs and mission-related expenses should not be included at this stage, as these will be managed separately in accordance with ACF procedures. The financial proposal will be assessed based on overall value for money rather than lowest cost alone. Evaluation Criterion 5 – Availability: Applicants should clearly indicate: • availability to undertake the assignment between mid-September and mid-December 2026; • ability to commit sufficient time to complete the assignment within the proposed timeframe; • availability to participate in the in-person final restitution workshop (mid-December); • willingness and ability to undertake international travel, if required, during November. Evaluation Criterion 6 – Quality of the interview: Shortlisted candidates will be assessed on their ability to demonstrate: • Strong understanding of the humanitarian coordination architecture and the cluster system. • Proven ability to conduct secondary data reviews and synthesise complex material into clear, actionable findings. • Experience conducting key informant interviews and light qualitative data collection • Familiarity with the development donor and financing landscape (institutional donors, IFIs, Nexus funding instruments) • Demonstrated experience with the humanitarian-development nexus, transition, localization or area-based approaches • Demonstrated ability to use Artificial Intelligence responsibly to support research, evidence synthesis and comparative analysis. How to apply: To apply, please follow this link: Application for the position of Research Specialist - Consultant: https://forms.cloud.microsoft/e/ZKyx5iNzmj Applicants shall submit the following documents to madadamo@actioncontrelafaim.org in a single PDF file named Surname_Name_Researcher_ApplicationDocuments: • Completed Application Form - (Evaluation Criterion 1): 28 August 2026 • CV(s); • Draft methodology (maximum two pages) - (Evaluation Criterion 2); • One research sample - (Evaluation Criterion 3); • One presentation sample - (Evaluation Criterion 3).

description: TERMS OF REFERENCE Hiring of Technical Specialist to do desktop review on Youth in Agriculture: Mapping Policy Gaps and Opportunities Across Four Countries to Inform Fairtrade NAPP Youth Advocacy Agenda August 2026 Hiring Organisation: Fairtrade Network of Asia, Pacific and Producer (NAPP) Country covered of the study: India, Sri Lanka, Indonesia, Uzbekistan Assignment Type: Individual Technical Consultancy, Team consultancy, Firm consulting agency Location: Remote work Duration: 8 week Reporting To: Fairtrade NAPP Advocacy Manager Language of Work: English Financial Proposal: Please quote in EUR Application Deadline: August 28, 2026 Expected Start Date: September 14, 2026 Fairtrade Network of Asia and Pacific Producers (Fairtrade NAPP) was established in 2014 and is one of the Producer Networks under Fairtrade International. Producer Networks are regional associations that Fairtrade-certified producer organizations may join voluntarily. They represent small-scale producers, workers, and other key stakeholders within the Fairtrade system. Fairtrade NAPP supports and empowers Fairtrade-certified farmers and workers across the AsiaPacific region. Producers collectively hold 50% ownership of the Fairtrade system and have equal decision-making power on matters that affect them. As a Producer Network, Fairtrade NAPP ensures that the voices of producers are effectively represented at regional and global levels. Currently, Fairtrade NAPP comprises 270+ Producer Organizations across 21 countries in the AsiaPacific region, representing over 260,000 farmers and workers. The organization focuses on producer support and relations, social compliance, youth and gender, advocacy, partnershipbuilding, capacity development, and improving access to international markets for its members. It also supports producers in addressing cross-cutting challenges such as climate change, gender inequality, and compliance with evolving market and sustainability standards. For more information, please visit: https://www.fairtradenapp.org/ 1. Background of the Assignment Fairtrade NAPP, in partnership with Fairtrade International, is implementing the Future is Fair project (2024-2027), co-funded by the European Commission through the Funding Framework Partnership Agreement (ECFFPA). As part of this initiative, a study is being conducted to review and consolidate national policies and programs related to youth in agriculture, The study will cover 4 selected countries, including India, Indonesia, Sri Lanka, and Uzbekistan, with the aim of identifying policy gaps, good practices, and opportunities to strengthen youth inclusion. It will also map the policy and program landscape to inform Fairtrade NAPP’s advocacy messaging in support of young farmers affiliated with Fairtrade-certified producer organizations. 2. Objectives of the Assignment The primary objective of this consultancy is to map and analyse the policy and programme landscape governing young people engagement in agriculture across four countries, identify key gaps and opportunities, and generate evidence-based recommendations to inform Fairtrade NAPP’s youth advocacy agenda. The specific objectives of this consultancy are to: Map and document the landscape of existing national and subnational policies, schemes, and programs that directly or indirectly address young people engagement in agriculture. Critically analyze the scope, coverage, implementation mechanisms, and accessibility of identified policies and programs for young people and agricultural workers, including those connected to Fairtrade value chains and analyse level of awareness of young people on these agricultural public schemes. Identify gaps, overlaps, and opportunities for Fairtrade NAPP and its members to leverage, align with, or advocate for improvements in existing government interventions, policies, and frameworks for young people to utilise their knowledge and skills in the agricultural sector Produce a consolidated, accessible reference document that can serve as a practical tool for program design, capacity building, and stakeholder engagement. Provide actionable recommendations for Fairtrade NAPP's strategic engagement with government frameworks on young people in agriculture. 3. Scope of Work and Key Tasks The Technical Specialist will be expected to undertake the following tasks: 3.1 Desk Review and Mapping Conduct a systematic desk review of national government documents, policy frameworks, scheme guidelines, budget allocations, and program reports related to young people in agriculture. Map relevant programs, schemes,policies for young people across national and state/regional Government ministries and agencies. In India, with particular attention to areas of Fairtrade producer organization presence: Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Odissa, Uttarakhand, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Kerala, Jammu, Punjab, Assam and West Bengal. For Indonesia, national level, Sumatera region, other region with fairtrade certified groups. Review reports and data from development banks, agricultural research institutions, and international organizations (including FAO, ILO, IFAD, and relevant NGOs) on young people agricultural engagement. 3.2 Stakeholder Consultations Conduct key informant interviews with NAPP staff, producers, active young people within producer organization, and young people engaged with NAPP Youth program Engage with Fairtrade NAPP Gender and Youth staff to understand on-the-ground realities and alignment opportunities Document insights from consultations in a structured manner to complement the desk review findings 3.3 Analysis and Synthesis Analyze the extent to which existing policies and programs address the specific needs and barriers faced by young people in agriculture, including gender-disaggregated analysis where data is available. Assess the reach, relevance, and effectiveness of identified policies, schemes, and programmes in enabling young people to apply and develop their knowledge, skills, and capabilities within the agricultural sector. Identify entry points for Fairtrade NAPP to engage in policy advocacy, program codesign, or leveraging of government resources for young people. 3.4 Consolidation and Reporting Prepare a comprehensive consolidation report synthesizing findings, analysis, and recommendations Present findings to Fairtrade NAPP staff and key stakeholders for validation and feedback Finalize all deliverables incorporating feedback from the review process Submit database of comprehensive Government Schemes/Policies Guide that includes scheme names, target beneficiaries, eligibility criteria, financial and other support provisions, key features, and objectives of each scheme for circulation to Fairtrade NAPP members (pdf and excel format) How to Apply Interested and qualified individuals are invited to apply and submit the following: A cover letter (maximum 2 pages) explaining your suitability for this assignment and your approach to the work. Sample work relevant to the assignment. A current CV or resume (maximum 4 pages) highlighting relevant qualifications and experience. A brief technical note (maximum 3 pages) outlining your proposed methodology, key data sources, and workplan. A financial proposal stating consultancy rate (in EUR) and estimated total number of days Contact details for two (2) references familiar with your recent work Applications must be submitted by email to advocacy@fairtradenapp.org with the subject line: 'Application – Youth in Agriculture Policy Review– [Your Name]' no later than August 28, 2026. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. Fairtrade NAPP reserves the right to modify or cancel this assignment at any stage of the recruitment process. description: Since 2014, Agora Energiewende develops evidence-based strategies for ensuring the success of clean energy and industry transitions around the globe. As an independent and non-partisan think tank and policy laboratory, it analyses upcoming challenges, shares knowledge with decision-makers and stakeholders and enables a productive exchange of ideas. The decarbonisation and resilience of the energy system and European industry require a transformation across all sectors of the economy and significant investments into productive assets, infrastructure and R&D. Public finance plays a crucial role in addressing these investment needs: at EU level the currently negotiated next Multiannual Financial Framework will decide funding allocation for the next decade, alongside revenues from the EU Emissions Trading System, CBAM and the ETS2. The role is full- or part-time (at least 80% of 38 hours per week), based in Brussels, with an unlimited employment duration. Responsibilities include: conducting research and analysis on funding and investment needs to support Europe's transformation to climate neutrality across sectors, with focus on energy, industry, buildings and transport; researching instruments, including carbon pricing revenues, through which private and public funding can be deployed in a targeted, efficient and fair way; providing support and oversight for the execution of research projects internally and with external partners and subcontractors; monitoring and assessing technical, regulatory and political developments on the Multiannual Financial Framework and EU-level funding instruments, including the Industrial Decarbonisation Bank, the Innovation Fund, the Modernisation Fund, InvestEU and the Competitiveness Fund; facilitating exchange with stakeholders and expanding networks, representing Agora ThinkTanks with stakeholders and decision makers; and close collaboration with colleagues from the Europe team to link EU-level political discussion with key Member States and beyond. Requirements: at least three years of working experience in policy analysis or consulting, applied research, or representing civil society or business; a Master's degree or equivalent in a relevant field of research including an economic component; good understanding of the EU budget (MFF) and relevant EU funding instruments (IDB/CCfDs, IF, MF, ECF etc.) with deeper expertise on at least one; strong demonstrated quantitative skills related to analysis of investment needs, budgets and funding instruments; relevant networks in European policy and ideally key Member States; ability to communicate complex matters clearly and produce high-quality analytic output; a confident, constructive team player open to a diverse and intercultural team; and working fluency (C2) in English plus another EU language. Offered: a mission-driven professional team, a modern workspace in central Brussels with hybrid working options, professional growth and travel opportunities, 29 vacation days, flexible working hours, generous family leave, mental wellbeing support, contributions to meal vouchers and medical insurance, and a structured onboarding programme. description: ABOUT LAW: Legal Action Worldwide (LAW) is an independent non-profit organization of human rights lawyers and jurists, united in our belief that those who have experienced human rights violations and international crimes, should receive survivor-centered, gender-competent, and trauma-informed support to access the justice they deserve. The fellowship may be undertaken either part-time (minimum 40% FTE or 15 hours per week) for at least one law school semester, or full-time for a period of three to six months. The fellowship may be extended beyond the initial three months term, up to a maximum of six months subject to funding and satisfactory performance. The final compensation package will be tailored to the successful candidate's individual circumstances including their part-time or full-time status, student or recent graduate status, and any external funding available. Provide research and background inputs for preparation of public reports or policy briefs or other evidence-based advocacy and policy outputs. Assist with high-level advocacy strategies and support engagements at the HRC, UNGA, ASP, and related forums. Assist with logistics and content preparation for side events, briefings, and advocacy meetings. Draft and edit material for legal information dissemination amongst victims and survivors, particularly on the status of the legal proceedings affecting them. Support coordination and follow-up related to stakeholder engagements with Member States and other key actors in the accountability ecosystem. Monitor relevant updates on requested areas of international law and policy developments, including outcomes from HRC, UNGA, and related processes. Programme Support, Partner Coordination, and Capacity-Building Support: Assist adaptation of existing training materials credible documentation of crimes and human rights violations, focussed on sexual and gender-based crimes. Provide note-keeping and documentation support during capacity-building sessions. Assist with documentation, note-taking, and knowledge management related to partner coordination. Compile and synthesize information to strengthen joint advocacy and network engagement. Support the drafting, and formatting of funding proposals and concept notes. Support LAW in implementing the protection interventions for its clients, as directed. Background knowledge in International Law, specifically International Human Rights Law (IHRL) or International Criminal Law (ICL) is essential. Fluency in English is essential. Strong desk research and drafting skills. Attention to detail and analytical ability. Ability to work independently in a remote setting. Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite and strong technical literacy. Strong communication and interpersonal skills. Prior professional, volunteer experience in research, human rights initiatives, or non-profit work is preferred. Prior experience on Afghanistan context is desirable. Proposed Timing and Duration: Indicate your preferred start date, anticipated duration of the fellowship, and any flexibility you may have with these dates.
